entries: Having a character that has a curse associated with them can lead to many fun and exciting moments, both for mechanics and for elements of plot and storytelling. However, should a player decide upon having their character have a curse, it is best to work out some degree of understanding regarding not only the nature of the curse and the ways in which it manifests itself, but also having an understanding of how to end the curse or break it.

Players, should you choose this background for a character, work with your DM to discuss how one would go about breaking your curse. Perhaps your character is fully aware of how to break it, yet the means with which to do so are incredibly difficult to obtain. Or, your character may know very little about the curse, and may only have a small clue or hint towards how to break it, or maybe no clue at all.

entries.name: Curses
entries: A curse can manifest itself in a variety of different ways. Some are cursed with a disease that allows them to transform into different beings, such as lycanthropy or vampirism. Other curses can render one unable to properly use one or more of their senses, may cause one to live an unnaturally long life, or may never allow for someone to ever feel loved again. Talk with your DM about the nature of your character's curse, and how it will best fit within the confines of your DM's world and campaign.

To DMs: Some curses are severe, while others are not. If a curse is severe, consider possibly giving your player a small bonus to them to compensate. For example, if a curse blinds the character, perhaps allow them to have advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on hearing.

items.name: Languages
items.entry: One exotic language (Abyssal, Celestial, Deep Speech, Draconic, Infernal, Primordial, Sylvan, or Undercommon)

items.name: Equipment
items.entry: A memento from a time before you were cursed, a set of {@item traveler's clothes|phb}, a {@item pouch|phb|small bag} of sage, a {@item ink pen|phb|quill}, an {@item ink (1-ounce bottle)|phb|ink pot}, a {@item book|phb|blank journal}, a cloak, and a {@item pouch|phb|small coin sack} of 5 gp

entries.name: Feature: Cursed Existence
entries: The nature of your curse can change not only your appearance, but how others react to you as well. Your curse may cause others to take pity upon you, offering anything that they can to aid or help you. In doing so, they may give you advice or directions to people who might be able to help you more.
However, your curse may also cause others to fear you, and shut their doors and homes to you, fearing that you may bring your curse upon their family or home.

entries.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: Those who are cursed can be varied in terms of their appearances, backgrounds, and professions. How they choose to interact with others, as well as how they handle their curses, can shape their outlook on their lives.

rows: I try to focus on anything but my curse, hoping it will distract me from it.
I speak often about my optimism on finding a cure, but secretly I doubt I will ever be rid of this curse.
I try my best to hide the effects of my curse, so as to not alarm others.
I embrace my curse as just another part of my personality and being. I want to find the cure, but am not sure if I would use it on myself.
I have little memory of my life before I received this curse.
I long to find a way to remove this curse so that others will not suffer from it.
I have little care for the gods.
I often put a lot of hope behind every clue I can regarding a cure for this curse.
Freedom. I long to be free of this curse. (Any).
Redemption. It is my fault that I am cursed, thus it is my burden to remove myself of it's grasp. (Lawful)
Revenge. I swear to defeat the one who cursed me, no matter what. (Chaotic)
Acceptance. I wish only to be accepted as a normal person, and not to let this curse define me. (Good)
Distribution. I will have all who wronged me suffer from this same curse. (Evil)
Purity. I long to not only rid myself of my curse, but the curses of others as well. (Good).
Though I journey to rid my curse, I would gladly die for my friends.
The gods cruelly manipulate people. I will stand against this.
I will free my family from the curse that has haunted us.
I can feel the curse tempting me with power every day, but I always deny it.
I yearn for companionship, as my curse often drives others away.
Having been cursed, I sympathize with those who fall upon terrible times or fortunes of which they have no control over.
I assume everyone thinks little of me.
I jump at even bad gambles for any clue to a cure.
When I am in pain, I never confide in others so as to not burden them with my troubles.
My curse has a voice that only I can hear. I struggle to not listen to it.
I care little for companionships, knowing that I won't have them for long.
I do anything I can to take my mind off of my curse. Anything.

name: Custom Background

entries.name: Choose Abilties
entries: Choose three abilities that seem appropriate for the background:

items.name: Strength or Dexterity
items.entry: These abilities are ideal for a background involving physical exertion.

items.name: Constitution
items.entry: This ability is ideal for a background that involves endurance or long hours of activity.

items.name: Intelligence or Wisdom
items.entry: One or both abilities are ideal for a background that focuses on cerebral or spiritual matters.

items.name: Charisma
items.entry: This ability is ideal for a background that involves performance or social interaction.

entries.name: Choose a Feat
entries: Choose one feat from the {@filter Origin|feats|category=O} category. See the {@book Player's Handbook|XPHB} for examples of {@book Origin feats|XPHB|5|Origin Feats}.

entries.name: Choose Skill Proficiencies
entries: Choose two skills appropriate for the background. There needn't be a relationship between the skill proficiencies a background grants and the ability scores it increases.

entries.name: Choose a Tool Proficiency
entries: Choose one tool used in the practice of the background or often associated with it.

entries.name: Choose Equipment
entries: Assemble a package of equipment worth 50 GP (including unspent gold). Don't include Martial weapons or armor, as characters get them from their class choices.
{@note See the section on {@book Creating a Background|XDMG|2|Creating a Background} in the {@book Dungon Master's Guide|XDMG} for more information.}

items.name: Equipment:
items.entry: Choose A or B: (A) map case containing 1 {@item Map|xphb}, a {@item Hunting Trap|xphb}, {@item Tent|xphb}, {@item Traveler's Clothes|xphb}, and 8 GP; or (B) 50 GP

_.displayName: a bit of dirt from your grave in a sacred vial

_.special: two rare coins with which you were buried

items.name: Equipment
items.entry: {@item hempen rope (50 feet)|PHB|50-feet of rope}, a bit of dirt from your grave in a sacred vial, a set of {@item common clothes|PHB}, two rare coins with which you were buried, and a belt {@item pouch|PHB} with 5gp

entries.name: Feature: Spirit Talk
entries: You can connect with the souls of the dead thanks to the long time you spent dead. You may spend a day of downtime communicating with the souls to learn a piece of information by asking a question. The quality and specifics of the information you get are up to the DM.

entries.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: You have experienced something few living people have yet to go through. You might be the type who embraces the second chance and loves life, relishing every opportunity and letting nothing stand in your way. Or you might be quiet and brooding, thinking of the revenge you seek for your death or missing the planar heaven you left behind. People who have died often live in one of these extremes, experiencing life to the fullest or becoming fixated on a single goal that gives their new life meaning.

rows: When faced with a new experience the word "no" isn't in my vocabulary.
I always have the loudest laugh in the room.
When I want something, I'm direct and simple in my request.
The story of my demise, like all stories, is greatly exaggerated.
Those who ask me about my death quickly learn to never ask again.
I treat most people like they're idiots. They don't know what I know.
If I don't want to do something, I simply don't do it.
I don't excite easily.
{@b Freedom}. Life is short so live how you want. (Chaotic)
{@b Despair}. Nothing in life is worth celebrating and death is the destination we all deserve. (Evil)
{@b Vengeance}. I will find and punish what killed me. (Neutral)
{@b Clarity}. I want to prevent others from dying before their time. (Good)
{@b Mercy}. I was given a second chance and others should get the same opportunity. (Good)
{@b Labor}. Life is short, so I must keep working to make my mark. (Lawful)
I have a great fear of that which killed me.
The scars of my death wound are still on my body.
My vengeance is more important than any other task.
I never wish to return to my gravesite.
I wish to bring back another who died by my side.
Any mention of my hometown reminds me of my first life.
Death isn't a big deal to me. I've died and come back. People should stop whining.
I don't listen to protests before I do something reckless.
I'd rather be mad than solve a problem making me angry.
I would rather cheat, lie, and steal than be honest because none of this matters.
Everything was better when I was dead.
I'm believe that I am better than everyone who hasn't died and come back from the dead.

entries: You died and came back. This experience changed you and defines who you are today. The specifics of your death are up to you, but the following questions and suggestions will help you determine your odd personal history.

How did you die? It probably wasn't of old age. Spells like raise dead can bring back those who die before old age takes them, but after dying of old age there is almost no magic which can bring a person back to life. Was it combat? An accident? A disease?

How long were you dead? Spells like true resurrection allow a character to return from death after as many as 200 years. How has the world changed politically, technologically, and culturally since your death? What remains of your family, friends, and personal life?

What was your life after death like? Did you spend time in the glory of eternal battle is Ysgard? Did you enjoy the paradise of Elysium? Were you tortured in the Nine Hells or Abyss? Do you remember nothing from that time?

Maybe you didn't completely pass on, but lived life as an undead, such as a {@creature ghost} or {@creature vampire}. Why did you become such a being? What acts did you commit that you now regret? Who still thinks of you as a monster?

Finally someone brought you back. Who was it, and why? Maybe it was to face an old enemy. Maybe it was a loved one who searched for a long time and sacrificed much to revive you. Maybe you were brought back for a secret only you knew. How did this person bring you back? Was it straightforward magic? What about a spell like reincarnate, which could bring your spirit back in the body of a different humanoid race? Or maybe it was some other magic that has a more sinister secret.

_.special: omniral weapon (replacing one you start with)
trophy taken from a fallen enemy (a dagger, broken blade, or a piece of a fiend's horn)

items.name: Equipment
items.entry: One set of {@item traveler's clothes|phb}, an omniral weapon (replacing one you start with), a trophy taken from a fallen enemy (a dagger, broken blade, or a piece of a fiend's horn), a {@item pouch|phb} containing 5 gp.

entries.name: Feature: Omniral and Douzen Communication
entries: As a member of one of the Douzen Clans you have access to their communication network within Xhoria. The clans have an intricate network of trained birds that are used to deliver messages, missions, and return reports back to the clan headquarters. This, together with divination, is the spine of the Douzen Clan communication network.

You also have your own omniral weapon, created from the magical ore from Valuren and a bit of your own blood, which grows with you the more evil you vanquish from Xhoria. Douzen Clan members will most always use their personal omniral weapon above any other magical weapon. Your weapon evolve according to the clan you belong to.

entries.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: Use the tables for the soldier background in the Player's Handbook as the basis for your traits and motivations, modifying the entries when appropriate to suit your identity as a member of one of the Douzen Clans.

For instance, your bond might involve other clan members or the individuals that employ you. Your ideal could be associated with your determination always to defeat evil and become better at the art of the blade.

You have been accepted into one of the three Douzen Clans. You are either member of the Clan of the Fierce Monkey, Clan of the Thunderdrake, or Clan of the Tide. You have the rank of Novice within the clan.

name: Demon Tainted

_.special: a small memento from your previous life

entries: At some point, you were corrupted by the powers of the Abyss, and your very being was pierced to the core by dark energies. Now you wander as a pariah, haunted by the event that made you this way. Now you have turned to adventuring to either win the favor of the people through deed, or find enough coin to sway anyone that might judge you for what you have become. You might flinch at what they call you, or embrace it. Either way, it is difficult to hide that you are "demon tainted."

items.name: Equipment
items.entry: Traveler's clothes, a hooded cloak, a staff, a small memento from your previous life, and a pouch containing 10 gp

entries.name: Feature: Dark One's Reputation
entries: When you encounter a demon, they immediately recognize you for what you are and treat you as though you are a fiend yourself. Though they might not necessarily act friendly towards you, they treat you with more respect and esteem than other mortals and readily parley with you as long as you have not already met them with open hostility.

entries.name: Spell List
entries: {@i Prerequisite: Spellcasting or Pact Magic class feature}

If you are a spellcaster, the spells on the Demon Tainted Spells table are added to the spell list of your spellcasting class. (If you are a multiclass character with multiple spell lists, these spells are added to all of them.)

entries.caption: Demon Tainted Spells Table
rows: Cantrip
{@spell chill touch}, {@spell produce flame}, {@spell thaumaturgy}
1st
{@spell burning hands}, {@spell hellish rebuke}, {@spell inflict wounds}
2nd
{@spell crown of madness}, {@spell darkness}, {@spell flaming sphere}
3rd
{@spell fear}, {@spell fireball}, {@spell summon lesser demons|xge}
4th
{@spell summon greater demon|xge}, {@spell wall of fire}
5th
{@spell destructive wave}

entries: When you cast spells from your Demon-tainted spell list, the air around you might grow hot, your eyes might glow, or other signs of demonic power. Each of these spells as you cast them are far from subtle.

entries.name: Dark Origin
entries: The moment when your life force was corrupted by demonic powers is what made you who you are today. That moment changed you forever, maybe through your own doing, or someone else's. Choose a dark origin, or roll on the Dark Origin table to determine the event that changed you.

rows: You tried to bargain for power, and in turn the demon you bargained with took a few liberties with the idea of granting you power.
You were intended as a sacrifice to a Demon Prince, but instead became their champion.
In a moment of trauma, the demonic ancestry in your bloodline manifested.
You were born this way, and were raised far away from society's judgemental eyes.
You took an unexpected trip to the Abyss, and did not return the same person.
After stealing a dark tome belonging to your master, you attempted to cast a spell from it, and things went horribly awry.
Little did you know, your past lover had actually been a demon, and their presence slowly changed you.
After having scorned a powerful spellcaster, this cursed form manifested over time.
You made a bet with a demon and lost.
After a night of debauchery, you woke up to find yourself like this.

entries.name: Demonic Mark
entries: The tainted nature of your being has its own physical manifestation that gives away what you are. You can choose one of the following from the Demonic Marks table, or roll for one. Alternatively, you might choose to create your own.

rows: One or more of your limbs turned red and demon-like.
Your eyes resemble that of a goat's and glow red in the dark.
You have a second mouth somewhere on your body that incessantly mumbles and whispers words of disaster in Abyssal.
Long curled horns sprout from your forehead and a spaded tail extends from your lower back.
Parts of your body look charred and ashen and you always smell of smoke.
A ghastly unblinking eye sits in the middle of your forehead. Although you can't see through it, you get the sinking feeling someone or something else can.
Your body is covered in Abyssal runes that glow faintly in the presence of divine magic.
Your tongue is forked and vestigial wings sprout from your shoulder blades.

entries.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: Demon-tainted characters, underneath their unusual appearance and dark histories, are still people. Although you might draw your powers from darkness, nothing dictates that your character is truly evil. In fact, you might be drawn to try to find healing and closure through good deeds. Alternatively, your character could feel drawn to darker ambitions and deeds as they struggle with the pull of the supernatural corruption within them.

rows: I am slow to speak up. The less attention I draw to myself, the better.
People think I'm scary, and I'm not going to ruin the illusion.
I talk to myself constantly. I also reply to myself constantly.
My scowl is more noticeable than the manifestation of my curse.
Wherever I am, I act like I am in charge. It's not like anyone is going to argue with a demon.
Something about what I am burns through energy like crazy. As a result, I am always hungry.
For some reason, people always want to fight me. Who am I to say no?
I hate when people judge me for what I am, therefore I don't judge others based on what they are. It's who they are that matters.
Revenge. This world is made up of wrongs and injustices, someone has to right them. (Chaotic)
Redemption. If you give others a chance to shine, the world can become a beautiful place. (Good)
Power. I've been granted a gift, and I am sure as hell going to make use of it. (Evil)
Justice. The natural order has to be upheld, if it isn't, there will be more tormented souls like mine wandering the realm. (Lawful)
Chaos. There is nothing but chaos in the Abyss, and I am the embodiment of that chaos. (Chaotic)
Peace. I just want to be left alone, and I'll stop whatever conflicts I can to find some quiet. (Any)
I am still looking for a way to repay someone for their awe-inspiring kindness.
I'm seeking a way to remove my demonic curse so I can be with the love of my life.
I am hunting the demon that did this to me. When I find it, I will make them pay.
With the mortal realm shunning me, I am looking for a place in the Outer Planes to call home.
A religious order is hunting me at all costs, and I have to keep moving if I am going to survive.
Someone gave me a home, and I will do anything to protect them and that home.
I can't get enough when it comes to carnal pleasures: food, drink, company—I want it all.
Angry is an understatement, my temper is downright (and sometimes literally) explosive.
A voice whispers in my ear that I am better than everyone, and I am sorely tempted to believe it.
I'm always jealous of what others have. Why was I denied happiness?
I can't be bothered to do things for myself. It is so much easier to pawn off my work onto others.
I take what I want, and I want a bit of everything

name: Desert Guide

_: desert goggles and a dust mask

entries: {@b Weapon Proficiencies:} Shortbows, spears, simple rifles, martial rifles.

Some, such as the Idrians, various tribes of desert-dwelling bogrin, and trollkin, know the Bloodstone Marches intimately. Those with such skills travel far and wide and live for extended periods in the desert, making them desirable as guides for caravans and armies traversing the scorching plains.

entries.name: Feature: Badlands Explorer
entries: You were brought up in the harsh and hostile environment of the Bloodstone Marches. Desert living is second nature to you, and coping with the baking heat, lack of water, and scouring winds is inherent to your upbringing. You have advantage on Constitution checks made to resist heat or bright light and Wisdom (Survival) checks made to find a water source.

entries.caption: Personality Trait
rows: The sun cleanses everyone, regardless of their faith.
My anger is like the constant thunder of the Bloodstone Marches.
Eventually, everything becomes sand and dust under the scorching winds.
By understanding a new language, you know how a society thinks and feels.
When Calder is bright, I recite the songs of my people.
Hunting big game gives me a thrill.
Under the tribal elders, I have learned all the names of the beasts that roam the deserts.
I will be like the desert wind: quiet but deadly. Like the shadows cast by the midday sun, I am unseen but ready to appear again.

entries.caption: Ideal
rows: Nature. All we do is part of the cycle of nature. (Lawful)
Self-Sufficiency. If you fall, you are a danger to others. We must stand on our own feet. (Chaotic)
Precision. Even the biggest beast can be felled by a splinter. (Any)
Glory. Others will know my prowess as a hunter of unequaled skill. (Any)
Exploration. I am driven to seek out new horizons and search out the clues that may aid my people. (Neutral)
Community. We must help each other through hardship. (Good)

entries.caption: Bond
rows: This tooth from a crag lion was taken from my first kill.
My sibling lived among the people of the Protectorate of Menoth and I have not seen them since the Claiming.
I have discovered cave paintings made by my people thousands of years ago that tell of the first hunt.
I took my weapon from the grip of a soldier whom I was leading through the desert. That soldier was in pain, and I eased their passing.
I carry a token that has been passed down through the tribe and is important to our rites and prayers.
The song I sing when I am down was taught to me by my mother.

entries.caption: Flaw
rows: I don't take other people's feelings into consideration.
Justice must always be pursued.
I feel I am closer to the gods than others.
I only trust my own instincts over all else.
Maintaining my weapons uses up all my focus.
Some foods don't agree with me well.

items.name: Equipment:
items.entry: {@item Traveler's clothes|PHB}, {@item herbalism kit|PHB}, {@item waterskin|PHB}, {@item pouch|PHB} with 10 gp

entries.name: Feature: Nomad
entries: Living in the open desert has allowed your body to adapt to a range of environmental conditions. You can survive on 1 gallon of water in hot conditions (or 1⁄2 gallon in normal conditions) without being forced to make Constitution saving throws, and you are considered naturally adapted to hot climates. While in a desert, you can read the environment to predict natural weather patterns and temperatures for the next 24 hours, allowing you to cross dangerous terrain at the best times. The accuracy of your predictions is up to the GM, but they should be reliable unless affected by magic or unforeseeable events, such as distant earthquakes or volcanic eruptions.

entries.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: Those raised in the desert can be the friendliest of humanoids—knowing allies are better than enemies in that harsh environment—or territorial and warlike, believing that protecting food and water sources by force is the only way to survive.

rows: I'm much happier sleeping under the stars than in a bed in a stuffy caravanserai.
It's always best to help a traveler in need; one day it might be you.
I am slow to trust strangers, but I'm extremely loyal to my friends.
If there's a camel race, I'm the first to saddle up!
I always have a tale or poem to share at the campfire.
I don't like sleeping in the same place more than two nights in a row.
I've been troubled by dreams for the last month. I am determined to uncover their meaning.
I feel lonelier in a crowded city than I do out on the empty desert sands.
{@bold Greater Good.} The needs of the whole tribe outweigh those of the individuals who are part of it. (Good)
{@bold Nature.} I must do what I can to protect the beautiful wilderness from those who would do it harm. (Neutral)
{@bold Tradition.}  I am duty-bound to follow my tribe's age-old route through the desert. (Lawful)
{@bold Change.} Things seldom stay the same and we must always be prepared to go with the flow. (Chaotic)
{@bold Honor.} If I behave dishonorably, my actions will bring shame upon the entire tribe. (Lawful)
{@bold Greed.} Seize what you want if no one gives it to you freely. (Evil)
I am the last living member of my tribe, and I cannot let their deaths go unavenged.
I follow the spiritual path of my tribe; it will bring me to the best afterlife when the time comes.
My best friend has been sold into slavery to devils, and I need to rescue them before it is too late.
A nature spirit saved my life when I was dying of thirst in the desert.
My takoba sword is my most prized possession; for over two centuries, it's been handed down from generation to generation.
I have sworn revenge on the sheikh who unjustly banished me from the tribe.
I enjoy the company of camels more than people.
I can be loud and boorish after a few wineskins.
If I feel insulted, I'll refuse to speak to anyone for several hours.
I enjoy violence and mayhem a bit too much.
You can't rely on me in a crisis.
I betrayed my brother to cultists to save my own skin.

entries: You grew up in the desert. As a nomad, you moved from place to place, following the caravan trails. Your upbringing makes you more than just accustomed to desert living—you thrive there. Your family has lived in the desert for centuries, and you know more about desert survival than life in the towns and cities.

Few have the stomach for war. Even fewer have the courage to flee from it. You forsook your oaths of honor or the promise of payment and fled the field of battle—or never reached the killing grounds at all.
Whether your former superiors believe you died in battle or you face execution for your desertion if ever caught, you know one thing for certain: you will never belong to an army again.

items.name: Tool Proficiencies:
items.entry: One type of {@item gaming set|phb} of your choice

items.name: Languages:
items.entry: One {@table standard languages|phb} of your choice

items.name: Equipment:
items.entry: A {@item two-person tent|phb|tent}, 5 days of {@item rations|phb}, one simple {@item weapon|phb} of your choice, a {@item compass|phb}, a set of {@item common clothes|phb}, and a belt {@item pouch|phb} containing 10 gp

entries.name: Justification
entries: Just as your peers had reason to fight, you had a reason to run. The reasoning for your cowardice might haunt you, or strengthen your resolve. Choose a rationale or roll on the table below to determine why you fled the military.

rows: Abuse; I refuse to suffer under cruel officers any more.
Cowardice; I fear combat and death.
Deception; I have orders to pretend to desert.
Defeat; I never managed to rendezvous after a loss.
Family; my loved ones need more than this army.
Rout; my unit fled together to escape the slaughter.
Self-preservation; I refused suicidal orders.
Surrender; I was a prisoner of war, now released.

entries.name: Feature: Secret Intelligence
entries: Your firsthand experience as a former soldier gave you a wealth of information. While useless and obvious to you, a skilled strategist would kill to gain your valuable insights into morale, training, supplies and logistics, attitude, army composition, and more. You may even have details about a force's long-term goals or overarching strategies.
You can use the promise of this information to gain asylum with a military enemy or ally... but many despise traitors regardless of the gifts they bring.

entries.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: Deserters are often broken, fearful creatures who dread discovery. They hold secrets close to their chest and may struggle to make lasting relationships. Some fear reprisal from a faction long gone, while others drown themselves in hedonistic pleasures.

rows: I'm wary of getting close to people lest I slip up and reveal my shameful past.
I committed terrible crimes and will atone in every small way I can.
I revel in the slightest luxury.
Exhausting days are no obstacle; they are nothing compared to what I faced before.
Rare is the conversation in which I speak more than a few words.
Pleasurable company is all well and good, but I prefer to be left alone.
I fear nothing for I am already broken.
Exuberance is the best disguise; if I don't act like a deserter then I won't get caught.
{@b Obedience.} I regret disobeying orders and won't do it again. (Lawful)
{@b Rejection.} "Just following orders" is no excuse. (Good)
{@b Freedom.} No one tells me what to do. (Chaotic)
{@b Avoidance.} I always shift blame to others. (Evil)
{@b Renewal.} I will put my past behind me. (Neutral)
{@b Impermanence.} Keep moving. I'll be executed if found out. (Any)
I will find and support the families of the comrades I failed to save.
I must escape 'justice' and reach a safe haven.
I will return to my family and live out my days in peace.
Inner peace guides me to a new future.
I'll never leave someone behind again.
I lost something valuable at my last battlefield.
I drown my misery in drink and vice.
I believe everyone is out to get me.
I wallow in guilt and accept any abuse to punish myself.
I disparage courage and honor.
I blindly hate both my former allies and old enemies.
I curse the gods and belittle anyone religious.

_.special: a memento of your destiny (a keepsake from your betrothed, the seal of your destined office, your family {@item signet ring|PHB}, or similar)

items.name: Equipment:
items.entry: A {@item dagger|PHB}, {@item quarterstaff|PHB}, or {@item spear|PHB}, a set of {@item traveler's clothes|PHB}, a memento of your destiny (a keepsake from your betrothed, the seal of your destined office, your family {@item signet ring|PHB}, or similar), a belt pouch containing 15 gp

entries.name: Destiny
entries: You're a person who's running from something or hurtling headfirst towards something, but just what is it? The responsibility or event might be happily anticipated or simply dreaded; either way, you're committed to the path. Choose a destiny or roll a {@dice d8} and consult the table below.

rows: You are running away from a marriage.
You are seeking your runaway betrothed.
You don't want to take over your famous family business.
You need to arrive at a religious site at a specific time to complete an event or prophecy.
Your noble relative died, and you're required to take their vacant position.
You are the reincarnation of a famous figure, and you're expected to live in an isolated temple.
You were supposed to serve an honorary but dangerous position in your people's military.
Members of your family have occupied a civil office (court scribe, sheriff, census official, or similar) for generations.

entries.name: Feature: Reputation of Opportunity
entries: Your story precedes you, as does your quest to claim—or run away from—your destiny. Those in positions of power, such as nobles, bureaucrats, rich merchants, and even mercenaries and brigands, all look to either help or hinder you, based on what they think they may get out of it. They're always willing to meet with you briefly to see just how worthwhile such aid or interference might be. This might mean a traveler pays for your passage on a ferry, a generous benefactor covers your group's meals at a tavern, or a local governor invites your adventuring entourage to enjoy a night's stay in their guest quarters. However, the aid often includes an implied threat or request. Some might consider delaying you as long as politely possible, some might consider taking you prisoner for ransom or to do "what's best" for you, and others might decide to help you on your quest in exchange for some future assistance. You're never exactly sure of the associated "cost" of the person's aid until the moment arrives. In the meantime, the open road awaits.

entries.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: Destined characters might be running toward or away from destiny, but whatever the case, their destiny has shaped them. Think about the impact of your destiny on you and the kind of relationship you have with your destiny. Do you embrace it? Accept it as inevitable? Or do you fight it every step of the way?

rows: I'm eager to find this destiny and move on with the next stage in my life.
I keep the fire of my hope burning bright. I'm sure this will work out for the best.
Fate has a way of finding you no matter what you do. I'm resigned to whatever they have planned for me, but I'll enjoy my time on the way.
I owe it to myself or to those who helped establish this destiny. I'm determined to follow this through to the end.
I don't know what this path means for me or my future. I'm more afraid of going back to that destiny than of seeing what's out in the world.
I didn't ask for this, and I don't want it. I'm bitter that I must change my life for it.
Few have been chosen to complete this lifepath, and I'm proud to be one of them.
Who can say how this will work out? The world is an uncertain place, and I'll find my destiny when it finds me.
{@bold Inevitability.} What's coming can't be stopped, and I'm dedicated to making it happen. (Evil)
{@bold Tradition.} I'm part of a cycle that has repeated for generations. I can't deny that. (Any)
{@bold Defiance.}  No one can make me be something I don't want to be. (Any)
{@bold Greater Good.} Completing my duty ensures the betterment of my family, community, or region. (Good)
{@bold Power.} If I can take this role and be successful, I'll have opportunities to do whatever I want. (Chaotic)
{@bold Responsibility.} It doesn't matter if I want it or not; it's what I'm supposed to do. (Lawful)
The true gift of my destiny is the friendships I make along the way to it.
The benefits of completing this destiny will strengthen my family for years to come.
Trying to alter my decision regarding my destiny is an unthinkable affront to me.
How I reach my destiny is just as important as how I accomplish my destiny.
People expect me to complete this task. I don't know how I feel about succeeding or failing, but I'm committed to it.
Without this role fulfilled, the people of my home region will suffer, and that's not acceptable.
If you don't have a destiny, are you really special?
But I {@i am} the "Chosen One."
I fear commitment; that's what this boils down to in the end.
What if I follow through with this and I fail?
It doesn't matter what someone else sacrificed for this. I only care about my feelings.
Occasionally — ok, maybe "often" — I make poor decisions in life, like running from this destiny.

entries: Destined characters might be running toward or away from destiny, but whatever the case, their destiny has shaped them. Think about the impact of your destiny on you and the kind of relationship you have with your destiny. Do you embrace it? Accept it as inevitable? Or do you fight it every step of the way?

items.name: Tool Proficiencies
items.entry: {@item disguise kit|phb}, one {@filter gaming set|items|source=null|type=gaming set} of your choice

items.name: Equipment
items.entry: A set of {@item common clothes|phb}, a {@item disguise kit|phb}, a notebook of investigation notes, a letter from an old friend, and a belt pouch containing 15 gp.

entries.name: Feature: Hunch
entries: When confronted with a mystery, you may get a hunch that will lead you to more clues. Your intuition is keen even when details of a case are missing or unclear and shortens the logical leaps required to unravel the mysteries of a case.

entries.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: In general, detectives are evidence-minded and exceptionally observant individuals. Their forays into seedy locales often foster unsavory habits with them, but these never conflict with their underlying sense of idealism. If it did, they would sooner give up when they face resistance or the investigation at hand turns cold.

rows: When I get a hunch, I follow it without hesitation.
I am quiet but observant, drinking in the hidden motivations of any scene.
I love reading old legends and lore.
In spite of my persistent cough, I'm never to be found without my pipe.
My language is as foul as an otyugh nest.
Every day, I have terrible nightmares of my investigations.
I'm far more comfortable in a noisy tavern than I am at home.
My notebook is filled with conflicting observations and accounts of the Elder Evil cults. I zealously take notes whenever I learn something new.
{@b Greater Good.} The Elder Evils pose a threat against the whole of the multiverse. (Good)
{@b Logic.} Impulsive emotions should not cloud our thinking. (Lawful)
{@b Truth.} Any secret can be revealed and any problem can be learned. (Neutral)
{@b Independence.} Every person should be able to stand alone, if need be. (Chaotic)
{@b Supremacy.} Knowledge is power, and my expertise happens to be in acquiring it. (Evil)
{@b Justice.} Every investigation should serve to sort out the guilty from the innocent. (Lawful)
I know someone badly affected by an Elder Evil cult. I owe it to them to find out the truth.
Perhaps I can steal away some of the great power of the Elder Evils for myself.
I am determined to discover the origin of a small yet ancient statue of an Elder Evil.
I seek the final component of a power ritual, rumored to be locked away within someone's skull.
I bear a mortal grudge against a warlock of the Great Old Ones.
A scar appeared on my body overnight in the shape of an ancient rune. I seek to unravel this mystery.
I am suspicious of strangers and expect the worst of them.
I'll take any investigation for any client, so long as it pays well.
Things never seem to go my way. I fear I may actually be cursed.
I am easily distracted by the promise of information.
I speak without really thinking through my words, invariably insulting others.
Drinking for me is a weakness I can't quite overcome.

entries: The investigators that discover the Elder Evils and their numerous cults follow the clues from places and people, wherever the occult hides. Through these adventures, you hope to gain the clues and resources needed to confront and ultimately thwart the eldritch threat.

You might be investigating the Elder Evils alone, or you may find assistance or direction from a church or similar organization. Regardless, only a few people would believe you if you told them what you're after, so it's often wise to conceal your goals.

name: Detective

_.special: a set of {@item common clothes|PHB} including a greatcoat and hat

entries: The grand cities of the North are rife with sleaze, scandal, and skulduggery, giving rise to a gamut of crimes that the traditional City Watch are illequipped to deal with. In such cases, the private detective steps from the lamplight to investigate, employing a diverse range of mental and social talents to unravel each mystery.

items.name: Equipment
items.entry: A magnifying glass, a bottle of ink, a quill, a folded parchment notepad, a set of common clothes including a greatcoat and hat, and a pouch containing 8 gp.

entries.name: Feature: Master Sleuth
entries: If you spend ten minutes talking to a stranger, you uncover hidden information about them by studying their mannerisms, tiny scuffs on their clothing, and so forth. At the DM's discretion, you deduce one of the following pieces of information about them: a recent location they've visited, an object they've handled, or a person they've spoken with.

entries.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: Adventurers are well adjusted to life on the road. They are often comfortable doing dangerous things, such as dungeoneering and fighting. They can stay level-headed in the face of danger, but may not be well adjusted to other parts of life.

rows: Before I leave a room, I often turn to ask one last question.
I don't play by the rules.
I find ignorance amusing.
I like to reveal my findings to a captive audience.
I'm witheringly sarcastic.
I rarely reveal my true feelings.
I solve crimes because life bores me.
I'm oddly superstitious.
{@bold Adventure.} I'm sworn to bring criminals to justice (Lawful)
{@bold Intellect.} The mind is a muscle that must be exercised to achieve brilliance (Any)
{@bold Greed.} I need coin to dig me out of this pit (Neutral)
{@bold Redemption.} I'm trying to undo all the bad things I've done in my life (Any)
{@bold Recklessness.} If they break the rules, so can I (Chaotic)
{@bold Curiosity.} We don't learn anything unless we experiment (Any)
The same nemesis is secretly behind many of my greatest investigations.
I wear a signature article of clothing, moustache style, or accessory.
My assistant travels everywhere with me.
I've a trauma in my past that still haunts me.
I'm immaculately dressed/
I'm attracted to people who live fast and dangerously.
I have a self-destructive vice that I indulge in secret.
I lack empathy for my prey.
I underestimate or look down upon the common folk.
All my relationships end in ruin.
I'm cripplingly obsessive.
I don't know how to handle failure.

_.special: small chip of delerium encased in glass

_.displayName: amulet with a symbol of your chosen god

items.name: Skill Proficiencies:
items.entry: Two of the following: {@skill History}, {@skill Religion}, {@skill Arcana}, {@skill Nature}

items.name: Equipment:
items.entry: A set of pale {@item robes|PHB}, a small chip of delerium encased in glass, a walking stick, an {@item amulet|PHB} with a symbol of your chosen god, a small {@item book|PHB} of religious text

rows: I was on a quest of self-enlightenment.
I ritualistically surround myself with lit candles and ancient texts when I rest.
I had taken a vow of silence until the time that my voice was needed to fulfil my destiny.
I was the caretaker of ancient relics of our faith and am quested with finding others.
I am but a pilgrim hoping to find divine light in dark places in the world.
I was guided to my faith by angels who rescued me from my dark past.
I broke my vows to my faith and was exiled. I seek redemption.
I must prove myself worthy to my faith and its purpose, no matter the amount of blood spilled or lives lost.

entries.name: Feature: Guided by Faith
entries: A number of times per day equal to your proficiency bonus, you may ask the Game Master to reveal the DC of any ability check you make before rolling the dice. You may then decide whether or not you wish to attempt the roll.

entries.caption: Suggested Characteristics
rows: I empathize with those who do not follow the path of light. Creatures of all types can be brought back to the path of righteousness and are often suffering and in great pain.
I believe in the words of my religion and quote its texts and scriptures as often as I can.
I am tolerant (or intolerant) of other faiths and respect (or condemn) the worship of other gods.
I have spent my life in a temple or church. Rough living wears on me quickly.
I believe very strongly that everything will turn out okay, and nothing can shake my positive attitude.
My faith kept me distant from others. I have very little experience with the world outside the church/temple/shrine.
I have extremely strict etiquette and manners for interactions and tasks, and I refuse to stray from them.
I am working on my thesis of religious ongoings in the world and excitedly discuss the nuances of these ideas with anyone and everyone.
Logic. Emotions must not cloud our judgement on what is right or true. (Lawful)
Self. My religious journey is that of discovering myself. If I can obtain that, there is nothing left to know. (Any)
Charity. I will always help those in need, no matter the cost. (Good)
Faith. The path laid out before me is determined by the divine entity I worship. I will follow its signs and patterns to fulfil my purpose. (Lawful)

Power. The gods have granted me divine powers and I must use them to make those who do not worship as strongly as I see the divine light and understand that I am the one true speaker of my faith. (Chaotic)
Peace. I do not like to be part of conflicts, rather a neutral voice of reason to all sides. (Neutral)
Nothing is more important than my church and what it represents.
I joined my religion to hide from a past I would rather forget.
The path to enlightenment is unending. I must stay the course.
I will die if it means doing right by my religious beliefs.
Everything I do is for the good of the common people.
I seek to preserve the ancient texts and artefact of my religion.
I judge others harshly and believe my path to be the one true path.
I believe in the words of my religion so strongly that I follow them without question.
The goal I have set for myself is my destiny, and I can not act against it or abandon it for any reason.
My religion was meant to keep the dark thoughts at bay, but I find myself losing that battle and a blood thirst grows within me.
This is my first taste of life outside my religion, and I enjoy its pleasures a little too much.

The gods and my faith have determined that I am always correct as I speak on their behalf. There is no question in my mind that I speak the ultimate truths and any who do not agree are misguided fools.

_.special: a letter of passage from a local minor authority or traveling papers that signify you as a traveling diplomat

items.name: Equipment:
items.entry: A set of {@item fine clothes|PHB}, a letter of passage from a local minor authority or traveling papers that signify you as a traveling diplomat, and a belt {@item pouch|PHB} containing 20 gp

entries.name: Feature: A Friend in Every Port
entries: Your reputation as a peacemaker precedes you, or people recognize your easy demeanor, typically allowing you to attain food and lodging at a discount. In addition, people are predisposed to warn you about dangers in a location, alert you when a threat approaches you, or seek out your help for resolving conflicts between locals.

entries.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: Diplomats always have kind words and encourage their companions to think positively when encountering upsetting situations or people. Diplomats have their limits, however, and are quick to discover when someone is negotiating in bad faith.

rows: I like to travel, meet new people, and learn about different customs.
I intercede in minor squabbles to find common ground on all sides.
I never disparage others, even when they might deserve such treatment.
I always try to make a new friend wherever I travel, and when I return to those areas, I seek out my friends.
I have learned how to damn with faint praise, but I only use it when someone has irked me.
I am not opposed to throwing a bit of coin around to ensure a good first impression.
Even when words fail at the outset, I still try to calm tempers.
I treat everyone as an equal, and I encourage others to do likewise.
{@bold Harmony.}  I want everyone to get along. (Good)
{@bold Contractual.} When I resolve a conflict, I ensure all parties formally acknowledge the resolution. (Lawful)
{@bold Selfishness.} I use my way with words to benefit myself the most. (Evil)
{@bold Freedom.} Tyranny is a roadblock to compromise. (Chaotic)
{@bold Avoidance.} A kind word is preferable to the drawing of a sword. (Any)
{@bold Unity.} It is possible to achieve a world without borders and without conflict. (Any)
I want to engineer a treaty with far-reaching effects in the world
I am carrying out someone else's agenda and making favorable arrangements for my benefactor.
A deal I brokered went sour, and I am trying to make amends for my mistake.
My nation treats everyone equitably, and I'd like to bring that enlightenment to other nations.
A traveling orator taught me the power of words, and I want to emulate that person.
I fear a worldwide conflict is imminent, and I want to do all I can to stop it.
I always start by appealing to a better nature from those I face, regardless of their apparent hostility.
I assume the best in everyone, even if I have been betrayed by that trust in the past.
I will stand in the way of an ally to ensure conflicts don't start.
I believe I can always talk my way out of a problem.
I chastise those who are rude or use vulgar language.
When I feel I am on the verge of a successful negotiation, I often push my luck to obtain further concessions.

entries: You have always found harmonious solutions to conflict. You might have started mediating family conflicts as a child. When you were old enough to recognize aggression, you sought to defuse it. You often resolved disputes among neighbors, arriving at a fair middle ground satisfactory to all parties.

_.displayName: holy symbol of the Radiant One

items.name: Languages:
items.entry: One of your choices between {@language Elvish|PHB|Elven} and {@language Orc|PHB|Orcish}, representative of the main forces within the Church.

items.name: Equipment:
items.entry: A {@item holy symbol|phb} of the Radiant One, a prayer {@item book|phb}, 5 sticks of incense, vestments, a set of {@item common clothes|phb}, and a {@item pouch|phb} containing 15 gp

entries.name: Features
entries: Your skill set varies depending on the role you serve within the Church, pick from the following features the one that is most appropriate for your character, with your GM's approval.

entries.name: Divine Guidance
entries: You have spent countless hours praying, studying scriptures, and performing rituals. Your devotion is so great that it draws the attention of the Radiant One, or so you believe. You can call upon this divine favor to guide your path. Once per day, you may ask your deity for guidance. How this guidance manifests can vary—a sudden insight, a prophetic dream, or perhaps a subtle sign in the environment around you.

entries.name: Forceful Miracle
entries: Through your dedicated service, you have harnessed the powers of the Radiant One. In the most dire of situations, you may extract this power for a miracle. However, these miracles are not to be taken lightly and should not be used frivolously. The miracle cannot be stronger in power than a spell of level equal to half your character level (rounded down, minimum 1st level). After a miracle has been granted, your hit points maximum are lowered by an amount equal to your character level for {@dice 1d12} days, and you must perform a significant service for the Radiant One to regain this miracle.

entries.name: Scribe of Radiance
entries: You've spent years studying the ancient scripts and texts of the Radiant Church, and with time, you've become a skilled scribe. Not only can you flawlessly replicate any scripture, but you can also identify and understand most religious texts related to your faith. This ability can prove invaluable when deciphering forgotten scriptures or understanding cryptic prophecies.

entries.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: You have dedicated your life to the Radiant One, and its teachings have molded you. Your faith may be the source of your strength, or it might be a yoke that weighs you down. Regardless, you are certain of the power of the Church and its role in your life.

entries.caption: Personality Traits
rows: I am deeply philosophical and enjoy pondering the mysteries of the universe.
I'm optimistic and always looking for a silver lining.
I strive to be a beacon of hope and strength for others.
I am assertive and never back down from what I believe in.
I often recount stories and parables from the Radiant Church.
I always try to offer guidance to those who seem lost.
I have a peaceful demeanor and a comforting presence.
I am strict and expect others to abide by the teachings of the Church.

entries.caption: Ideals
rows: {@b Strength}. I must be strong so that I can guide others through adversity. (Lawful)
{@b Hope}. I am a beacon of light in the darkness, showing the way to a brighter future. (Good)
{@b Faith}. My faith in the Radiant One gives me strength and purpose. (Any)
{@b Knowledge}. The true path to enlightenment is the pursuit of knowledge. (Neutral)
{@b Charity}. It's my duty to help those in need, and to provide for the less fortunate. (Good)
{@b Independence}. I must question and challenge my faith to truly understand it. (Chaotic)

entries.caption: Bonds
rows: I owe my life to the Church, and I will serve it until my last breath.
I believe that the Radiant One has a grand destiny in store for me.
I will bring the teachings of the Radiant Church to those who live in darkness.
I aim to preserve the unity of the Church amidst its division into factions.
I feel responsible for those who stray from the path of the Radiant One.
I will redeem the Church from its insidious corruption and restore its noble ideals.

entries.caption: Flaws
rows: I am dogmatic and find it hard to accept beliefs that contradict the teachings of the Church.
I am naive and often overoptimistic, which sometimes leads me to underestimate dangers.
I am plagued by an overwhelming fear of divine judgment, constantly doubting whether my actions are in accordance with the teachings of my faith.
I struggle with doubt and question my faith, particularly when facing the unfairness of life.
I have high expectations for myself and others, which often leads to disappointment.
I find it hard to forgive myself for past mistakes and often dwell on them.

items.name: Equipment:
items.entry: Choose A or B: (A) {@item Book|XPHB} (prayer), {@item Calligrapher's Supplies|XPHB}, {@item Fine Clothes|XPHB}, {@item Holy Symbol|XPHB}, 5 GP; or (B) 50 GP

a.special: a letter from a family member who still cares for you

b.special: a family memento that was broken when you were banished

items.name: Skill Proficiencies:
entries: {@skill Deception}, {@skill History}

items.name: Language Proficiencies:
entries: One of your choice

items.name: Tool Proficiencies:
entries: One {@item artisan's tools|PHB} of your choice, or {@item thieves' tools|PHB}

items.name: Equipment:
entries: A letter from a family member who still cares for you or a family memento that was broken when you were banished, {@item crowbar|PHB}, {@item book|PHB} of history, fine clothes, and a {@item pouch|PHB} containing 15gp.

entries.name: Feature: Cunning of a Liege
entries: You grew up around the courts of kings and their knights. When someone attempts to make a Charisma ({@skill Intimidation}) check against you, you have advantage on your opposition roll.

entries.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: Banished from their home, disgraced nobles tend to be one of two things; secretive or boastful. They either hide their true nature or flaunt it. They may have bonds that reflect their noble background or possibly that of a traveller, having lived on the road after their exile. Their flaw may be the reason they were exiled or possibly the reason they won't go back.

rows: I am proud of my past and flaunt it everywhere I go.
I've been mistreated before and would rather kill than let it happen again.
I tend to keep people at a distance, so I cannot get hurt again.
Everyone I meet is my family, and I will protect them to the end.
I keep my promises, but only to those who keep theirs.
I aim to control every situation.
I let others take the lead, afraid of failing myself.
I tend to show mercy to even the worst people, I don't know who's waiting for them at home.
{@b Blind Faith}. No one is completely evil; everyone deserves a chance at redemptions. (Good)
{@b Redemption}. Those who have failed must work to rectify the harm they caused. (Lawful)
{@b Mighty Rule}. Those who do not recognize strength, fail to do so because of their weakness. (Chaotic)
{@b Blasphemy}. Some people are despicable by nature, all they are good for is target practice. (Evil)
{@b Balanced}. Strength is meaningless, without the knowledge and respect to use it. (Neutral)
{@b Disheartened}. Running from one's failings will only lead to more. (Any)
My family was right to cut ties with me, what I did was despicable.
I will reunite with my family and regain their respect.
My family is wretched and I will have my revenge once I am powerful enough.
Faith is only something the faithless speak of, that is why it is my go-to topic.
I will do everything in my power to find a new family and protect them with my life.
I can bring forth a new era, one that resides far from my family.
I cannot notice the mistakes I've made, blaming others for my failings.
My search for vengeance causes me to do things I would otherwise find horrendous.
All wrongdoers deserve death, no matter the crime.
I cannot help but carry burden, taking responsibility for everything. Especially that which is not mine.
I must hold my head up high so no one knows my pain.
I use my own pain as a justification to hurt others.

items.name: Equipment:
items.entry: Choose A or B: (A) {@item Spear|XPHB}, {@item Navigator's Tools|XPHB}, {@item Traveler's Clothes|XPHB}, Dilapidated Rowboat, 8 GP; or (B) 50 GP

entries: You were a raider associated with one of the greatly feared Vaikan clans. The terror you and your allies struck within sailing distance of your homeland was massive and palpable. The risks were great, but the respect was undeniable.

You lost that respect, however, when something went wrong. Perhaps you lost your nerve and fled the battlefield. Perhaps you lost your mind and killed when you were only supposed to capture. Perhaps you saw the terror you inspired in others as a moral failing rather than a point of honor. Regardless, you were cast out of your clan and could never return. You now travel Etharis having to live with what you've done and the shame (or honor) of your clan's shunning.

name: Disgraced Traitor

_.special: a painful memento that reminds you of your past

items.name: Equipment
items.entry: A set of {@item commoner's clothes|phb}, a {@item disguise kit|phb}, a {@item bedroll|phb}, a belt containing 25gp, a painful memento that reminds you of your past, and 5 days worth of rations.

entries: Some folks would rather their past be forgotten. Whether it be selling out your village for a payday, running out on family, or even leaving someone to certain doom, a shadow of regret hangs over your head. You often find yourself looking at mementos, wishing you could undo all the wrong you put into this world.
Ask yourself what heinous deed you did? How do you seek to undo it? And when you do, will you set your eyes on some new goal?

entries.name: Feature: Nightmares of Yesteryear
entries: You have dreams about your past failings. When you take a long rest your dreams will dwell on those lost. While they may offer premonitions of the future, they will prevent you from ever truly finding solace in slumber.

name: Displaced

_.special: wallet with a dozen banknotes of a currency not accepted in this world

entries: You don't belong in this world. You come from an alien realm where magic doesn't exist, technology is far more advanced, and the adventures you now face are confined only to fiction.

Consider how long you have been in this world, and how you managed to procure the powers associated with your class. Have you been stuck here for years, learning the ways of this world as a means to survive? Did you appear not only in an unfamiliar place, but an unfamiliar body? Think about your previous life, what skills you have, and how you apply these to your new life.

items.name: Skill Proficiencies
items.entry: Any two skills that are not Arcana, History, or Religion

items.name: Tool Proficiencies
items.entry: Two of your choice from any artisan's tools (except alchemist's supplies), any musical instrument, or any gaming set

items.name: Equipment
items.entry: A communications device with no power, a wallet with a dozen banknotes of a currency not accepted in this world, a ring of keys, a set of strange clothes, and a pouch with 10 gp

entries.name: Feature: Modern Knowledge
entries: Though you came to this world without a copper piece to your name, the advanced knowledge you brought with you has given you something of value to offer. You are well versed in a field that is farther advanced in your world than the one you are in now. You could be well educated, but even a basic education in some places of your world is extraordinary in this one.

To make a life for yourself, you have contributed your knowledge to some organization in this world. You may have taught a cult the secrets of calculus, or instructed a blacksmith's guild in how to make stronger steel. The organization considers itself indebted to you for your contribution, and is willing to support you at a modest lifestyle. They consider you a member of their organization, although you may have to pay monthly dues to gain the full benefits of membership. The technology you introduce may cause disruption in the world and its balance of power. Work with your DM to determine what impact your knowledge has on the world, if any.

entries.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: Displaced characters are strangers in a strange land. They might see this as a call to action to become a hero like in the stories they grew up with, or they may only care about making it out alive. In any case, they are defined by a culture that those around them can't come close to relating to.

rows: I'm taking this predicament as a chance to reinvent myself and be a better, stronger person.
I have trouble pronouncing all these weird fantasy names.
Back home I was a nobody, so I'm amazed whenever I pull off something crazy and heroic.
When someone asks me where I'm from, I tell the truth. They never believe me.
I frequently make pop culture references that no one else understands.
I channel my favorite fictional hero in battle to give myself courage.
Since I'm clearly  the protagonist in an isekai anime, I frequently flirt with the natives to get my harem started.
I hate camping.
{@bold Heroism.} Now that I have the power to be a hero, I want to use it for good. (Good)
{@bold Fun.} While I'm here, I might as well explore and go on crazy adventures (Chaotic)
{@bold Domination.} With my modern mind and technology, I will bring this barbaric world to its knees. (Evil)
{@bold Discovery.} The mysteries of this new world never cease to amaze me. (Any)
{@bold Progression.} This place has some backwards attitudes and political systems, and I plan to bring everyone up to my modern standards. (Lawful)
{@bold Safety.} I don't want to die! (Neutral)
I will do whatever it takes to get back home.
I try my best to be a representative from my world that my people could be proud of.
Magic fascinates me and I want to understand how it works, perhaps scientifically.
I want to build a life for myself that is comfortable as what I enjoyed in my own world.
The friends I've made in this world mean more to me than the ones I had back home.
I owe my life to the kind people who took me in after I arrived in this world.
I cower in the face of real danger.
I'm convinced that I'm delusional, and that nothing I do in this world really matters.
I don't know how to research anything without the help of the internet.
I make up stories about who I am and where I'm from to avoid questioning, and I've lost track of all my lies.
My survival instincts leave much to be desired.
I haven't adjusted to the lower standard of living in this world well, and I'm easily won over by the promise of luxuries.

entries: You are a Doctor: a medical professional. You may be physician, nurse or surgeon. You have extensive knowledge about the humanoid body and how it functions. You have studied the cause and cure of many injuries, diseases and other types of ailments.

items.name: Tool Proficiencies
items.entry: {@item Doctor's kit|ba} and (a) a {@item surgery kit|ba} or (b) {@item dissection tools|ba}.

items.name: Equipment
items.entry: A doctor's kit, a thick medical tome, a notbook, three quills, ink, a set of {@item common clothes|phb} and a belt {@item pouch|phb} containing 15 gp

entries.name: Medical Training
entries: All medical professionals are educated in some way in the healing arts by a mentor or institution. How you were taught your trade may influence how you practice it. You can create one yourself or pick randomly from the table below.

rows: Military
Books (self-taught)
Coroner or mortician
Divine (skills granted by a deity)
{@creature green hag|mm|Hag} or {@creature Barovian witch|cos|witch}
Homeschooled/parent
Medical school or institution (e.g. guild)
Village or tribe elder

entries.name: Feature: Diagnostic Professional
entries: When you study a diseased creature for at least 10 minutes you have advantage on Medicine checks to determine the origin for their illness as well as potential dangers and effects if the disease is left untreated.

entries.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: Doctors are generally very analytical. Depending on how they were trained they might be adventurous or academic in nature. Because of their inclination to heal and cure people, most doctors have a Good alignment. However, malpractitioners are not uncommon and can have a huge impact on society.

rows: I think a lot about the lives I have saved, but more about those I could not save.
I feel strongly that healing with magic is not always the right solution.
I'm unphased by suffering and pain.
I sacrifice my own well-being for the well-being of others.
I study every inch of any body I encounter to better my understanding of it.
I keep my tools and weapons extremely clean and in order.
I write down all my findings and plan on publishing them in the future.
I try not to befriend patients lest I become too attached to them.
{@b Duty:} I swore an oath to help others, and I must live by it. (Lawful)
{@b Health:} I will do anything to protect and save lives in any way I can. (Good)
{@b Efficiency:} Placebos work as well as any medicine, without the hassle. (Chaotic)
{@b Pain:} I want to know how to cause the most intense physical suffering. (Evil)
{@b Relief:} Life and death should both be without any pain. (Neutral)
{@b Reputation:} I want to be respected for my medical skill and achievements. (Any)
I am an admirer of a famous medical author and their writings.
I used to have an assistant, but they have run off with some of my research.
I accidentally performed a wrong procedure on a patient of mine.
I only became a doctor to make my parent(s) proud of me.
I had an apprentice to whom I imparted my knowledge, but they have surpassed me on every level.
One of my patients adores me because I saved their life. They stalk me constantly.
I have horrible handwriting.
I feel entitled to charge a lot of gold for my services.
I'm extremely disorganized, causing my patients to doubt my abilities.
I often speak in obscure medical terms.
I forget about my own health because I worry about others so much.
I get extremely depressed when I fail to save or cure a patient.

name: Doctor

_.special: token of appreciation given to you by a patient

entries: You are a well-trained and studied healer, sworn to cure the ailing and mend the wounded. Your talents may bring you fame and renown, or you might be regarded with suspicion by common people.

When you choose this background, work with your DM to determine the role and prominence of doctors in the world. Is medical knowledge of your kind rare? Are there institutions that teach such healing, and if so where? Were you self-taught, apprenticed to a village healer, or educated in a medical academy?

items.name: Skill Proficiencies
items.entry: {@skill Medicine}, and one from {@skill Arcana}, {@skill Nature}, or {@skill Religion}

items.name: Equipment
items.entry: A piece of doctor's equipment (such as a scalpel, pouch of aromatic herbs, or a small mirror), a healer's kit, a token of appreciation given to you by a patient, at set of traveler's clothes, and a belt pouch containing 15 gp.

entries.name: Specialty
entries: As a doctor, you likely specialize in a particular field and manner of medicine. Choose one specialty, or roll on the table below.

rows: Apothecary
Battlefield Medic
Dentist
Spiritual Healer
Medical Arcanist
Herbalist
Nurse
Surgeon
Veterinarian
Psychologist

entries.name: Feature: House Calls
entries: Your talents make you highly sought after, particularly in regions or communities with little access to medicine. Those who recognize you as a doctor may request your services, and may offer you a reward in return should you choose to provide them. You might be able to receive free or discounted food and lodging, or gain access to normally off-limits locations by leveraging your position as a doctor if your services are needed.

entries.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: Doctors are defined by their ability to give succor to the pained and strength to the wounded. All doctors are united by their desire to cure the ailing, although some view this ability as a means to an end instead of a gift in and of itself.

rows: I am sympathetic to anyone in pain.
I have a tendency to become focused on my work to the exclusion of everything else.
I like to explain my theories of medicine to anyone who will listen.
I have seen too much horror to be affected by scenes of suffering.
I am skeptical of magic, and instead I trust in the sciences.
When someone is injured, I will drop all other responsibilities to tend to them.
I am constantly taking note of potential signs and symptoms in the people I meet.
I take every opportunity I can get to wash my hands.
{@bold Empathy.} All I care about is the relief my skills bring to others. (Good)
{@bold Change.} Those who seek to cure must be as adaptable as those who seek to harm. (Chaotic)
{@bold Respect.} The sick and dying deserve to be treated with dignity. (Good)
{@bold Greed.} Those in need of my services will pay through the nose to get them. (Evil)
{@bold Efficiency.} I must not let my emotions cloud my ability to do my job. (Lawful)
{@bold Preservation.} Life must be preserved by any means. (Any)
I'll always remember the place where I learned my medical skills.
Nothing is more important than my patients.
I am working on a cure for the plague that decimated my home.
Someone I loved died of an illness. I want to spare others from the same fate.
I am compiling my medical discoveries in a series of tomes, which I hope will educate future generations.
I have a terminal disease and I am trying to find a cure before it's too late.
I am haunted by the memories of every patient I could not save.
I use hard drink to numb myself to stress.
I am disgusted by the body's potential for filth and disease.
I make more mistakes than I should, a fact that I hide from even myself.
I have a propensity to see my patients as opportunities instead of people.
I am hesitant to injure others, even in self-defense.

items.name: Skill Proficiencies
items.entry: {@skill Medicine}, plus one from among {@skill Investigation}, {@skill Nature}

items.name: Tool Proficiencies
items.entry: One from among {@item herbalism kit|phb}, or {@item alchemist's supplies|phb}

items.name: Equipment
items.entry: A set of {@item common clothes|phb}, a {@item healer's kit|phb}, a piece of medical equipment (latex gloves, a syring, a medical mask), and a {@item credit stick|TTT} with 1000 credits.

entries.name: Feature: Doctor Specialty
entries: No doctor is familiar with all fields of medicine. There's simply too much for an individual to learn, and it gets harder every year as medical science continues to progress. Instead, a doctor specializes in a certain field of medicine. You can select your specialty from the table below or roll to select it randomly.

rows: Pediatrics
Family Medicine
Neurology
Surgeon
Plastic Surgery
Veterinarian
Medical Genetics
Radiologist
Pathology
Battlefield Medicine
Nursing
Paramedic

entries.name: Feature: Primary Care
entries: You can always find a back alley clinic or hospital willing to treat you and your companions' wounds without asking too many awkward questions. You also have an easier time acquiring pharmaceutical chemicals and drugs, as well as other medical supplies. Additionally, you know where you can gain access to a medical lab for research and experimental purposes.

entries.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: The medical profession is full of dedicated individuals willing to work long hours in service to others. They are capable, studious, and not prone to squeamishness. Doctors are no stranger to pain, death, and loss.

rows: I have a dry, detached, and clinical personality.
I'll spare no effort to help others.
I tend to get too personally involved and care too much.
I'm a nervous wreck, but I try to keep it together around others.
I have a very warm bedside manner for my patients and those I care about.
I'm not good enough. I never have been.
I think that laughter is the best medicine.
Every day I live is a joy.
{@bold Healer.} Save everyone you can, ease the suffering of those you can't. (Good)
{@bold Oath.} First, do no harm. (Lawful)
{@bold Alternative.} I've tried traditional medicine, now it's time for something new. (Chaotic)
{@bold Knowledge.} Medical and professional advancement are more important than petty things like ethics. (Evil)
{@bold Professional.} I have a job to do, lofty ideals are unrealistic. (Neutral)
{@bold Guardian.} I'll safeguard those I care about. (Any)
I lost a patient with mysterious symptoms. I must learn the root cause.
The hospital I worked at was doing illegal research.
I never got a real medical degree, but I've never let that stop me.
My research requires subjects who are consistently in harm's way.
I'm no doctor, just a washed-up husk after the biggest mistake of my life.
The best preventative medicine is stopping those who hurt others.
I don't need a second opinion, I know what's best.
I'm hard on myself because I can't afford to make a single mistake.
I secretly can't stand the sight of blood.
I jump to conclusions, and it's hard to dissuade me.
I tend to fall apart when I lose a patient.
I am easily distracted at the worst times.

entries: Between fast cars, big guns, powerful drugs, and the steep decline in the value of life, society has no shortage of casualties. Doctors will always be in heavy demand, their skills and tools allowing them to make the difference between life and death for their patients. They are often respected for saving the lives of family members, or blamed and despised for their perceived failures.

Modern medicine has advanced to the point of completely restructuring a person's face and body, replacing limbs and organs with vat grown tissue, enhancing individuals past their natural limits with cybernetics, and more. Of course, a person's access to healthcare may depend heavily on their financial situation. The same limits apply to medical professionals, who hold positions that range from underfunded community clinic nurses to the personal physicians of corporate senior executives. A doctor can rise as high as their ambitions, skill, and ruthlessness allow.
