Aggression. I worked hard for the power I have— damn right I want to use it. I throw myself into challenges and dangerous situations. If you think you can beat me, bring it on.
There is no law I won't break to protect those I care about.
Although I do care for others, my duty is to myself. I come first in my book.
The teacher who taught me the secrets of element bending remains a trusted friend and confidant. I make great efforts to keep in touch; they are family to me.
I stole a treatise on bending and studied in secret. Now the people I took it from are looking for me.
I struggle to feel like I belong. I pursue power in the hope it will keep me useful to those around me.
I once lost control of my power and grievously wounded an innocent. I am still searching for a way to make it up to them.
I push myself too hard. Sometimes I leave myself weak and vulnerable in the pursuit of strength.
I am not subtle. I am loud, flashy, and eager to fight.
I am afraid of my own power. I second-guess myself and doubt my ability to wield it responsibly.
Despite wielding elemental powers of earth, I don't like sand. It's coarse and rough and irritating, and it gets everywhere.
I am noble to a fault, always play fair, and am seen as predictable and naive..
I am forever changing my mind and struggle to focus on a single thing.

items.name: Skill Proficiencies
entries: {@skill Persuasion}, {@skill Riddle|TLotRR}

items.name: Tool Proficiency
entries: {@item Calligrapher's supplies|PHB}

items.name: Distinctive Features
entries: Cunning, Lordly

name: Emere Dancer
entries: Your ancestors were great Emere dancers. You gain advantage once per day on a Charisma ({@skill Performance}) roll to dance.

name: Engineer
entries: Clockwork, machinery, and technology have all played parts of high importance in your life. You have apprenticed and trained to become a skilled engineer, learning how to work with a variety of tools and even vehicles throughout your life. You might have been an inventor whose creations helped out the place you came from, or you may have been someone who worked on constructs or weapons of war.

When you choose this background, work with your DM to determine where and on what you worked on regarding your engineering skills, how far your skills have progressed, and what kind of experiences you have had due to your trade. Were you and engineer who worked on machines of war? Or were you someone who helped to build newer tools and technology for a city?

items.name: Equipment
items.entry: A {@item pouch|phb} containing 15 gp, a set of {@item tinker's tools|phb}, a small bundle of copper wire, a dozen small gears, a set of protective eyewear, a small hammer, and a set of {@item common clothes|phb}

entries.name: Speciality
entries: During your time as an engineer, you developed the knowledge and skills to focus on a certain type of creation. Roll a d6 or choose from the options in the table below to determine your focus.

rows: Gunsmith
Construct Creator
Electrical Engineer
War Machinery
Gadgetry
Vehicles

entries.name: Feature: Skilled Engineering
entries: You have considerable knowledge regarding engineering. You know much about famous engineers and tinkerers, and what they are famous for. You also always have free room and board in any place where engineers reside, and the individuals in such a settlement might grant you use of their shops or tools.
In addition, you can generally find the materials needed to repair various tools, equipment, or even constructs, and can inspect them to understand exactly what went wrong and how to repair them.

entries.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: The life of an engineer means working with a variety of equipment and creations. This has led you to have a different outlook on life based on your work with machines and technology.

rows: I always read any type of manual or instructions regarding a new piece of equipment.
I never go anywhere without my trusty tools.
I am always fiddling and tinkering with something, looking for new ways to improve it.
I like making sure my work station is clean and tidy, and my equipment is clean, in great condition, and tidy.
I am constantly fascinated with new developments in technology.
I find great companionship in automations and constructs.
I tend to think logically, preferring to adhere to schedules and structure.
I don't mind getting myself dirty, so long as I am productive.
Knowledge. Through technology and my engineering skills, I can acquire fantastic knowledge. (Any).
Logic. I tend to favor logic as opposed to my emotions. (Neutral)
Innovation. I aim to create new machinery that can benefit the lives of others. (Good)
Profit. I see my creations as a viable way to make money, regardless of what my creations can do. (Evil)
Power. I aim to show the world how strong my creations can be. (Chaotic)
Foresight. I know that civilization would benefit from well conducted research into engineering. (Lawful)
I find relationships with constructs more valuable to me than with people.
Knowledge should be shared, and I'm always willing to teach others how things work.
My tools were given to me by my instructor. I will use them to make them proud.
I find that working on a specific lifelong project distracts me from any pain or sadness I may feel.
I will prove myself by way of my creations.
It is my duty to serve civilization by making helpful creations.
If something doesn't make logical sense to me, I get easily flustered.
I focus on fixing anything but myself.
If something I make fails or breaks down, I feel incredibly sad or angry about it.
I often find myself chatting on and on and on about machinery and what I make.
I sometimes forget how loud my work can get.
I often scoff at primitive technology.

items.name: Specialty
entries: A good entertainer is versatile, spicing up every performance with a variety of different routines. Choose one to three routines or roll on the table below to define your expertise as an entertainer.

rows: Actor
Dancer
Fire-eater
Jester
Juggler
Instrumentalist
Poet
Singer
Storyteller
Tumbler

items.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: You spent much of your youth following roving fairs and carnivals, performing odd jobs for musicians and acrobats in exchange for lessons. You may have learned how to walk a tightrope, how to play a lute in a distinct style, or how to recite poetry with impeccable diction. To this day, you thrive on applause and long for the stage.

Successful entertainers have to be able to capture and hold an audience's attention, so they tend to have flamboyant or forceful personalities. They're inclined toward the romantic and often cling to high-minded ideals about the practice of art and the appreciation of beauty.

rows: Members of my family made ends meet by performing, so it was fitting for me to follow their example.
I always had a keen insight into other people, enough so that I could make them laugh or cry with my stories or songs.
I ran away from home to follow a minstrel troupe.
I saw a bard perform once, and I knew from that moment on what I was born to do.
I earned coin by performing on street corners and eventually made a name for myself.
A traveling entertainer took me in and taught me the trade.
I know a story relevant to almost every situation.
Whenever I come to a new place, I collect local rumors and spread gossip.
I'm a hopeless romantic, always searching for that "special someone".
Nobody stays angry at me or around me for long, since I can defuse any amount of tension.
I love a good insult, even one directed at me.
I get bitter if I'm not the center of attention.
I'll settle for nothing less than perfection.
I change my mood or my mind as quickly as I change key in a song.
Beauty. When I perform, I make the world better than it was. (Good)
Tradition. The stories, legends, and songs of the past must never be forgotten, for they teach us who we are. (Lawful)
Creativity. The world is in need of new ideas and bold action. (Chaotic)
Greed. I'm only in it for the money and fame. (Evil)
People. I like seeing the smiles on people's faces when I perform. That's all that matters. (Neutral)
Honesty. Art should reflect the soul; it should come from within and reveal who we really are. (Any)
My instrument is my most treasured possession, and it reminds me of someone I love.
Someone stole my precious instrument, and someday I'll get it back.
I want to be famous, whatever it takes.
I idolize a hero of the old tales and measure my deeds against that person's.
I will do anything to prove myself superior to my hated rival.
I would do anything for the other members of my old troupe.
I'll do anything to win fame and renown.
I'm a sucker for a pretty face.
A scandal prevents me from ever going home again. That kind of trouble seems to follow me around.
I once satirized a noble who still wants my head. It was a mistake that I will likely repeat.
I have trouble keeping my true feelings hidden. My sharp tongue lands me in trouble.
Despite my best efforts, I am unreliable to my friends.

items.name: Equipment:
items.entry: Choose A or B: (A) {@item Dagger|XPHB}, {@item Calligrapher's Supplies|XPHB}, Diplomatic Papers, {@item Fine Clothes|XPHB}, {@item Signet Ring|PHB}, 10 GP; or (B) 50 GP

entries: You are the official representative of a government or other powerful group, traveling to further the objectives of the group you represent. You must be ready at a moment's notice to travel to the next town, or to other parts of the world. Such travel requires not just social skills but also a strong drive and a hardy disposition.

Your responsibilities change based on the organization you represent and their goals: forge alliances or maintain existing ones, establish business ties, oversee far-ranging projects, etc. However, many of your tasks are reactive: responding to a noble's threats, securing defensive pacts in times of conflict, or bolstering border defenses. Everywhere you go, something is at stake.

items.name: Languages:
items.entry: Two of your choice between Elvish, Dwarvish, Gith, or Orc

items.name: Equipment:
items.entry: A {@item holy symbol|phb}, a prayer {@item book|phb}, 5 sticks of incense, vestments, a set of {@item common clothes|phb}, and a {@item pouch|phb} containing 10 gp

entries.name: Feature: Together as One
entries: People of the Eratus have learned that together they can face anything. Under Arzen's banner the empire is able to face even the worst enemies. Whenever you make a saving throw to resist an effect that would make you {@condition frightened} and you can see at least one more creature with the same background, you have a +2 bonus to those saving throws.

items.name: Equipment
items.entry: Tattered robes, a symbol of your dark lord, a blasphemous holy text, a curved ritual {@item dagger|phb}, a {@item poisoner's kit|phb}, and a small {@item pouch|phb} containing 5 gp.

entries.name: Feature: Secret Signs
entries: You know the secret symbology of your cult, which can pop up in some surprising places. Some nobles, influential persons, or even common townsfolk may also be members of your cult, and with a subtle gesture or knowing handshake you can discern who still follows the ways of your dark lord.

Cloisters of your cult may also be hidden across the land, identified by the secret signs and symbols designed to lead the faithful to places of dark worship. Such cloisters often con- tain enough lodging and food for at least ten people, for a week, and sometimes harbor eldritch treasures belonging to the cult. Cloisters with treasure still intact likely contain practicing cultists or guardian monsters, however; your cult was not foolish enough to let its secrets remain unguarded.

entries.caption: Personality Traits
rows: Everything is a sign of coming doom. Every. Single. Thing.
The world outside is so exciting! Now I can do everything the dark lord used to forbid, like drinking wine, or wearing shoes!
The dark lord used to order us to do everything. It's a little hard for me to live without that.
if my friends will let me, I'll openly reminisce about my old days in the cult all day long.
I still can't help but check the holy scriptures for advice about any given situation.
It's no big deal, it's not the end of the world. That's not for another five years, three months, ten days, twelve hours...
It's still important to leave the old offerings, to perform the old rites.
I'll happily inform those I meet of the many ways in which they are being heretical.

entries.caption: Ideals
rows: {@b Loyalty}. My new companions are my new family, I will protect them. (Lawful)
{@b Reparation}. I must fix the evils my cult has done. (Good)
{@b InLoyalty}. My new companions are my new family, I will protect them. (Lawful)
{@b Reparation}. I must fix the evils my cult has done. (Good)
{@b Independence}. I'll never be bound in servitude again! (Chaotic)
{@b Power}. The dark lord was weak in the end. I will be stronger than they ever were. (Evil)
{@b Secrets}. The lore of my cult is historic- ally important, and I should preserve it. (Neutral)
{@b Revision}. The cult failed because the holy book was wrong. I must learn about the outside world, and fix the book's errors. (Neutral)

entries.caption: Bonds
rows: I must discover the truth behind my dark lord, even if it kills me.
I need to reconnect with the people from my life before the cult, if I can ever find them.
I must free other minions from un- witting service to dark masters.
A monstrous, immortal guardian of the cult is hunting me. I pray it never finds me.
I sold my soul in service to the dark lord, and now I seek to reclaim it.
The day of reckoning is coming, and my knowledge is the key to stopping it.

entries.caption: Flaws
rows: If I ever had the chance, I'd definitely rejoin my cult.
I'm a little too into blood sacrifice.
Knowledge is more important than sanity.
I'm often more interested in than frightened of abominable eldritch monsters.
I'm almost too willing to follow orders without thinking.
Murder was significantly less frowned upon by the cult than in the outside world.

entries: Once, perhaps not too terribly long ago, you served alongside your fellow neophytes. You worshipped at altars to a dark creature or eldritch god. performed the sacraments and blood sacrifices and adorned yourself with the proper tattoos or ceremonial scars. For a while. you basked in this dark glory with your fellows, feeling the camaraderie and clarity of purpose that comes with service to a higher, malign power.

But, something changed. Now, you wander the world outside of your isolated circle of brethren, either unwillingly or of your own volition. Surviving in the outside is difficult and often confusing after living as you did for so long, but perhaps a new circle of comrades could be of some assistance...

entries.name: Change of Heart
entries: Why did you walk away from the world you knew, and why did you seek something different? Was this a choice you made, or did fate separate you from your fellow devotees? Do you wish to undo the evil that your cult perpetuated, or would you rejoin your cult if given the chance?
Work with your DM to decide what you and your cult worshipped, how much of your cult still exists. You may also need to work out why you left the cult, which you can roll on the following table.

entries.caption: Change of Heart
rows: I witnessed a particularly gruesome rite and ran for my life.
A botched ritual slaughtered the other members of my circle. Only I survived.
I asked the wrong kind of questions. The others planned to sacrifice me to our dark lord, but I escaped.
Adventurers hunted us down, and only I was able to escape.
The other cultists disappeared through a portal to a land of unspeakable horrors. Terrified, I stayed behind.
The others took their own lives to ascend. I could not.
I no longer believed in what we were doing. It seemed wrong, somehow.
A friend or family member rescued me, taking me away by force.

items.name: Equipment:
items.entry: Choose A or B: (A) {@item Dagger|XPHB}, {@item Smith's Tools|XPHB}, Someone Else's Journal, {@item Traveler's Clothes|XPHB}, 10 GP; or (B) 50 GP

entries: You were employed as an executioner by some group or organization in a position of power. Your legally sanctioned murders have given you a strong arm and a knowledge of death and fatal blows.

You may have worked for the Crimson Court, dispatching those who work against the nobility (if their blood is not worth draining). You may have worked for the Arcanist Inquisition, putting unrepentant mages to death. You may have carried out sanctioned sacrifices for the Prismatic Circle.

For some reason, you left your career: maybe you were wracked by guilt, maybe the group you worked for fell out of power, maybe you displeased your bosses, or maybe you decided to move on to a different occupation. But your actions have stayed with you, and your time as a dealer of death have made a lasting impact.

items.name: Skill Proficiencies
items.entry: {@skill Insight}, plus one from among {@skill Persuasion} or {@skill Deception}

items.name: Equipment
items.entry: A set of fine clothes, a smartphone, an award from your company, and a credit stick with 2500 credits.

entries.name: Feature: Corporate Etiquette
entries: You know how to speak with corporate employees, speaking to managers and wage slaves each in a manner befitting their station. You know how to communicate with corporate bureaucrats in an effective manner to get what you desire with minimal delay. When negotiating a transaction with a corporation, you can always at least get a fair market price.

entries.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: Executives are cut from different cloth than the average person. Something drives them to perform above and beyond, to excel in the cutthroat world of business. Executives are often untrusting, assuming everyone has their own agenda and hidden motivation. Even if they were never the most dedicated employee, an executive's outlook on life is doubtlessly affected, or even stained, by their time in a seat of power.

rows: I am condescending to those I see as beneath me.
I am cold and calculating, with an analytical mind.
I'm the hands off kind of manager, and I see my employees as my friends or family.
I tend to make and hold grudges with grim determination.
I'll talk about anything anywhere. I love the sound of my own voice.
I was promoted far above my level of competence, so I fake it.
I prefer to supervise instead of getting physically involved.
I promote a balanced work environment with proper flow of energy.
{@bold Equality.} People are people, regardless of their position in the hierarchy. (Good)
{@bold Model Citizen.} I will use the power granted to me responsibly and in accordance with rules and regulations. (Lawful)
{@bold Unpredictable.} Bureaucracy just gets in the way, I'll cut out the middleman. (Chaotic)
{@bold King.} There's nothing I wouldn't do to reach the top. (Evil)
{@bold Wealth.} Money measures one's worth in life. (Neutral)
{@bold Dedication.} Any business is like a family, and I will ensure my family prospers. (Any)
I was terminated after a hostile takeover, and the parting was not clean.
The world is spiraling out of control, and I need to take the reins.
I know the dirty secrets of a major corporation.
My company was dissolved after a series of unfortunate events, and I will rebuild it.
I want to escape my old corporate life, but that's easier said than done.
The terrible things I've done can never be forgiven.
Money and power have given me some eccentric tastes that others find bizarre.
I am tightfisted with my money, even when I have plenty.
I'm too proud for my own good, I have a hard time accepting help from others.
I splash my money around to impress people, spending more than I can afford.
I'm impulsive, acting before I think things through.
I will talk about my family for hours, whether people care or not.

entries: When the international megacorporations expanded until they became more powerful than governments and nations, corporate executives rose above politicians and royalty as the true ruling class. On the world stage, these executives wield the power to shape the future to their own designs. The highest executives and company shareholders hold such great wealth that it is measured more in orders of magnitude than simple numbers.

Like any form of organization, corporate hierarchies take many forms. For some corporations, the corporation is a family business. The sons and daughters of executives are bred and trained for succession, the money passed down the bloodline. For other corporations, promotions are merit- based. Of course, in many cases, 'merit' is defined by the most cunning, ruthless, and vicious individuals willing to ascend a staircase of bodies and broken dreams.

items.name: Equipment
items.entry: A {@item dagger|PHB}, a small strongbox, a memento from your homeland, a set of {@item common clothes|PHB}, and a pouch containing 5 gp

entries.name: Feature: Exile Network
entries: You keep in touch with a network of exiles and expatriates, who possess an eclectic mix of skills and the durable spirit of pioneers. If you need to find someone with an unusual or specialized skill (such as art forgery, translation of ancient languages, or poison-brewing), you likely know where to find them.

entries.name: Variant Feature: Radical Sympathizers
entries: As a prominent figurehead for a group of religious, political, or ethnic radicals, you are often able to find people who sympathize with your situation. When you employ hirelings, they may offer you better rates, fanatical loyalty, or enhanced services.

entries.name: Reason for Exile
entries: You were exiled for a reason. Choose a 'crime' or roll on the table below to determine why you were forced to leave your home.

entries.caption: Ship Names
rows: Opposition to political rulers
Tax exile
Religious dissent/radicalism
Sentenced to exile for serious crime
Death sentence commuted to exile after committing capital crime
Forbidden love
Refugee displaced by war or disaster
Escaping shameful failures committed at home
Fleeing false accusations
Self-imposed exile/journey of self-discovery

entries.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: Being exiled is a deeply painful experience, and life as a stateless persona non grata is extremely challenging. Such a trial is sure to leave some marks on the exile's personality.

rows: I jump whenever anyone knocks on my door.
I stand by my principles, rather than compromising them.
Hand-written letters are my preferred means of communication.
I am fascinated by different cultures.
I sometimes become pensive and withdrawn.
I have a lot of interesting and unusual friends.
I often reminisce about my years before exile.
I write a lot of poetry in my spare time.
Homecoming. I hope to return to my homeland one day. (Any)
Liberty. I will live the way I want to! (Chaotic)
Peace. I will make the most of my time in exile, living a peaceable life. (Lawful)
Leadership. It is on me to lead my people through the wilderness. (Good)
Revenge. I must take revenge on those who cast me out! (Evil)
Refuge. In these dangerous times, I must focus solely on survival. (Neutral)
I have made many good friends in the émigré community.
I still write to my family back home.
People count on me as a symbol of resistance.
I have started a new family in my adoptive homeland.
I cannot return home until I have found what I am looking for.
I am still wanted by the courts.
I have trouble keeping my big mouth shut, and often end up ranting against my opponents.
I get in trouble with the law wherever I go.
I can't seem to put down roots or form lasting connections anywhere.
My hatred for the people who exiled me sometimes crowds out reason in my head.
I prefer to work alone, and rarely seek compromise with others.
I've been away so long, I have lost touch with my family/culture/language.

entries: Sometimes seen as a fate worse than death, exile has long been a popular sanction for radicals, dissidents, and troublemakers. Exiling these people allows the authorities to remove a thorn from their sides without creating a martyr or having to keep the unwanted person in costly perpetual captivity. Many a coup or revolution has resulted in the leaders and courtiers of the old regime being consigned to exile, sometimes on a moon or neighboring planet, sometimes on the other side of the 'verse.

On occasion, a person may choose exile voluntarily, either as an alternative to something worse or because they desire time on the Frontier to grow and develop. An exile has a unique opportunity to absorb foreign cultures and contact émigré communities while rallying support remotely. Living in exile might provide benefits that aren't available back home, such as the freedom to pursue otherwise forbidden love interests or take advantage of more lenient tax policies, either of which could deliver the impetus to accept a self-imposed exile.

Exiles take to adventuring for a number of reasons. For some, their exile was only temporary, and now they seek to embark on a dangerous journey home, while others might seek to foment rebellion in absentia so as to be welcomed as liberating heroes on their return. Some exiles are gripped by wanderlust, traveling the world with a small group of companions. The unluckiest of all, however, might find themselves unwelcome everywhere, with no choice other than to continue wandering forever.

items.name: Tool Proficiency:
items.entry: Choose {@item Disguise Kit|XPHB} or {@item Forgery Kit|XPHB}

items.name: Equipment:
items.entry: Choose A or B: (A) {@item Disguise Kit|XPHB} or {@item Forgery Kit|XPHB} (same as above), {@item Igniter|DarkMatter24}, {@item Traveler's Clothes|XPHB}, 18 CR; or (B) 50 CR

entries: You were exiled from your homeworld or system and forced to live in a strange land under strange stars. Perhaps you were a political dissident, a troublemaker, or simply ran afoul of the local powers that be. As you've traveled the 'Verse, you've discovered allies and enemies in all corners, wonders and horrors you could never have imagined, but never a place like home.

name: Exile
entries: Through a series of events, you became an exile to your homeland. Banished and forbidden to ever return, you have set off on a journey to find a new home. It could have been that you committed some terrible act, or were wrongly accused of doing so. Or perhaps it was a mass banishment decreed by a new leadership in your homeland.

When you choose this background, work with your DM to determine what exactly caused you to become an exile, how those events took place, and what the terms of your banishment are. Was it the case that you rightfully deserved to be exiled from your home? Or were you innocent, and wrongfully accused of acts you were told you committed?

items.name: Skill Proficiencies
items.entry: {@skill Survival}, and one other skill of your choice

items.name: Equipment
items.entry: A walking stick, a set of {@item traveler's clothes|phb}, one week's supply of {@item rations (1 day)|phb|rations}, a {@item backpack|phb}, a small knife, a {@item tankard|phb}, and a small {@item pouch|phb} containing 5 gp

entries.name: Feature: Exiled Life
entries: Whatever your prior standing was in your homeland, you are now an exile. You are able to find refuge with others who are exiled, as well as those who sympathize with your situation. Generally, this means that you can find a place to bed down, recover, and hide from any potential followers or trackers attempting to hunt you down. People from where you hail from are less willing to assist you if it means putting themselves in harms way.

entries.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: The life of an exile is a tough one, and is often filled with strife and change. They are unmoored from the only life they have ever known, which could radically change them from the person they used to be.

rows: Though I am exiled, I remember my homeland fondly.
I am glad to be gone from the hellish conditions that were plaguing my home.
I yearn to one day return to my homeland to prove my innocence.
I openly admit to others what caused me to be banished. I am proud of what I did.
While I do miss my homeland, I don't mind learning of and experiencing other lands and cultures.
I often cook dishes or read books that were prominent in my homeland.
I try to hide why I was exiled, as it brings me great shame.
I long to bring both myself and others back to my homeland to live as we once did.
Revenge. I know I was wrongly accused, and those who accused me will pay. (Chaotic)
Return. I want to do all that I can to right make things right again so that I can return home. (Good)
Renewal. I will find a new home for myself and others in a place where we can be free. (Lawful)
Redemption. I know I was wrong with my actions, yet I will prove that I am worthy of a second chance. (Good)
Retribution. I will bring all of the might and power that I can against those who exiled me. (Evil)
Retrospection. At the time, I did not know why I was exiled. However, I will try to learn from my actions. (Any)
I take those who were exiled alongside me.
I have someone I care deeply about back home.
My new friends are who I care about now in my journeys.
I found comfort in knowing that there are others in similar predicaments as me.
I had a dear friend who was exiled with me. I will learn to at least give them a way to return home.
The new rules of my homeland will stop at nothing to hunt down exiles. I will find a way to stop them.
I am slow to trust anyone after my trials.
I often speak too harshly about those who exiled me.
I become sad very easily when I think or speak about my home.
Even though I know I deserved to be exiled, I still want to take it out on those who banished me.
I often belittle other cultures and countries for minor cultural habits.
I lash out with anger at anyone who belittles my homeland.

_.displayName: a ruined spellbook that once belonged to one of your peers
a scroll tube that contains four preserved humanoid eyeballs

_.special: a necklace with a trio of tiny crystals that have been woven together with silver filigree

items.name: Equipment:
items.entry: A {@item Thayan trinket|TLotRW}, a ruined {@item spellbook|PHB} that once belonged to one of your peers, a {@item Map or Scroll Case|PHB|scroll tube} that contains four preserved humanoid eyeballs, a necklace with a trio of tiny crystals that have been woven together with silver filigree, a set of {@item traveler's clothes|PHB}, and 20 gp

entries.name: The School of Sacrifice
entries: What did you give up in order to enter tutelage? What concessions did you make to stay there?

entries.caption: Sacrifices and Concessions
rows: You had to give up your family; they were disappeared by the zulkir's enforcers, but you entered into your education for free.
As you became close with your peers, they were removed from class. You never heard from them again, and the administrators didn't recognize their names or descriptions when you inquired.
You had to give up part of your eternal soul.
You had to accept part of the zulkir's soul into yourself. You have no control over or communication with this fragment, but its presence mars your existence.
You had to swear an oath to Thay upon pain of eternal torment, and you're convinced that actions taken against Thay would result in excruciating retaliation.
You willingly accepted a curse that causes you to lose your memories if you act against Thay. You have no idea how much you've already forgotten.

entries.name: Feature: Student of Evil
entries: You are familiar with the Zulkir that you trained under, and know the information presented in their description elsewhere in this supplement. You may not have spent significant time with them directly as your training was primarily handled by their advisors, but your awareness may open (or inadvertently close!) doors when speaking with other people, especially adventurers, merchants, and nobles. Similarly, the Zulkir may have a bounty on your head for your safe (or otherwise) return.

items.name: Equipment:
items.entry: Choose A or B: (A) {@item Alchemist's Supplies|PHB}, {@item Manacles|PHB}, {@item Perfume (vial)|PHB|Perfume (to cover chemical smell)}, {@item Traveler's Clothes|PHB|Travler's Clothes (with hooded cloak)}, 5GP; or (B) 50 GP

items.name: Ability Scores:
items.entry: Increase one of your starting ability scores by 2 and another by 1, or increase three scores by 1 each.

items.name: Equipment:
items.entry: Choose A or B: (A) {@item Alchemist's Supplies|XPHB}, {@item Manacles|XPHB}, {@item Perfume|XPHB|Perfume (to cover chemical smell)}, {@item Traveler's Clothes|XPHB|Travler's Clothes (with hooded cloak)}, 5GP; or (B) 50 GP

items.name: Equipment:
items.entry: Choose A or B: (A) {@item Dagger|XPHB}, {@item Navigator's Tools|XPHB}, Maps, {@item Traveler's Clothes|XPHB}, 8 GP; or (B) 50 GP

entries: You pursue a life traversing the wilds, driven by wanderlust or the orders of a distant patron. For you, there is no greater pursuit than to discover the lost, forgotten, and unseen reaches of the world.
You may travel unaccompanied or lead companions, establishing encampments in remote areas or living completely off the land. You might lead pioneers looking to settle uncharted lands.

You may help establish settlements in the areas you explore, but before long, your attention wanders, and the call of the unknown beckons too strongly to ignore. And when that happens, you blaze a new trail into the darkness, rushing headlong into whatever thrills await.

name: Explorer

_: a scroll case containing maps in progress

entries: You've charted paths through the inhospitable jungles of Alchiere and the trackless wastes of the frozen north to fill in the blank areas on the map. You are more at home in a freshly unsealed Orgoth tomb than in the bustling streets of a major city.

entries.name: Feature: Patron
entries: You receive a stipend from a university, a wealthy individual, or another organization each month as long as you continue to explore new regions, report back regularly, and bring your patron the occasional gift from an exotic place. The amount of this stipend is {@dice 1d10} gp per character level. At the GM's discretion, your benefactor can give you heftier sums for noteworthy accomplishments.

entries.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: Explorers feel called to the unknown and forgotten. They are accustomed to packing light enough to travel but well enough to be prepared for whatever challenges await. Their motivations generally involve increasing either their general knowledge or their personal gain, while their flaws are often the consequence of too much curiosity.

entries.caption: Personality Trait
rows: I crave the excitement of being the first to enter a long-forgotten place.
I can quote any of Professor Pendrake's essays; in fact, I do so whenever I get the chance.
Studying at a prestigious university has prepared me for life on the road.
I believe knowledge is for everyone, and I work to make sure all my discoveries end up in museums, where others can benefit from them.
I love learning new languages and can sit with a book of lore for hours.
I've spent so much time in the wilderness that I forget myself in polite company.
Despite wise counsel, if it involves a tomb, the Orgoth, or a curse on all who enter, I'm going in.
Campfires are the perfect stage, and I love telling stories.

entries.caption: Ideal
rows: Discovery. I want to discover all there is to know about the world, expand my understanding of it, and share that understanding with others. (Good)
Ambition. My name will go down in history as one of the greatest explorers of the age. (Any)
History. Understanding our nations' past is the only way to plot our path forward. (Good)
Profit. I want to sell my discoveries in order to acquire immense personal wealth. (Neutral)
Adventure. I cannot be content living an everyday life and seek adventure however I can find it. (Chaotic)
Power. I want to discover ancient relics and use them to amass power. (Evil)

entries.caption: Bond
rows: I owe a significant debt to a prestigious institution as a result of a previous expedition.
I "accidentally" defiled a sacred site and am no longer allowed in particular villages.
A rival I once beat to a find will stop at nothing to discredit me.
I will one day have my writings published in my university's library.
I will be the first to chart the unknown mysteries of Zu.
One day, I will be as famous as Viktor Pendrake.

entries.caption: Flaw
rows: Being first to a discovery is more important than being safe, and I have the scars to prove it.
If presented with a riddle or puzzle, I can think of nothing else until it's solved.
I cannot abide a closed door. I must at least take a peek at what's behind it.
My obsession with being prepared often leaves me overly encumbered and broke.
I am irrationally terrified of an ordinary animal.
My overconfidence in my abilities is matched only by the inadequateness of my preparation.

items.name: Equipment:
items.entry: Choose A or B: (A) {@item Dagger|XPHB}, {@item Poisoner's Kit|XPHB}, {@item Hunting Trap|XPHB}, {@item Traveler's Clothes|XPHB}, 8 GP; or (B) 50 GP

entries: Etharis is overrun with vermin, but for you those pests of the four-legged variety. In the cities these are generally rats and other rodents. In the country, the pests might come in the form of raccoons or other critters that steal food and destroy structures piece by piece.

You've trained in the arts of getting pests away from people and coin away from clients. You may run an honest business, helping farmers and shop owners eliminate potentially life-threatening pests. Or you may introduce those pests in the first place, then solve the problem you created, skipping town before your ploy is discovered.

name: Fallen
entries: You were once a being of greater power, and possessed magic beyond what mortals imagine. You were prayed to for guidance and miracles, or had worshippers among many peoples. Then you fell - you angered a powerful deity, touched a corrupted artifact, or underestimated a group of mortals. You are now reduced to a mere mortal, vulnerable and stripped of your once mighty powers to live alongside the creatures you love or despise.

items.name: Equipment
items.entry: A holy symbol (related to yourself), a set of common or traveler's clothes, robes, and a belt pouch containing 10 gp.

entries.name: Divine Domain
entries: When you were powerful, you held superior power over a domain of action and thought. Consider what your powers entailed, and how that shaped you to be the mortal you are today. Choose your domain of power, or choose from the table below.

rows: Reroll
Knowledge
Life
Light
Nature
Tempest
Trickery
War

entries.name: Feature: Protection of the Faithful
entries: You have little problem convincing those that worshipped you that you are the deity they serve. You can achieve this by showing extensive and personal knowledge of the stories, artifacts, and symbols associated with yourself. You also know the names of your clerics, and a brief summary of their lives before you anointed them.

After convincing someone of your true identity, you gain their protection from hostile members of other faiths that seek to harm you, as long as you are within the city or town where the place of worship is located. They will resort to violence as a means of protecting you. If you ask them to, they will cover your tracks or delay your pursuers. They will not attack powerful foes or otherwise get into a situation more than they feel they can handle.

entries.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: The fallen once possessed great power, but it was extinguished from them. This sudden turn leave a significant mark on how they view themselves, deities, mortals, and the multiverse.

rows: I don't mind telling people who I really am. They won't believe me, anyway.
I try to make people convert their faith to the worship of me.
I sound like I know everything, because I do.
I always perk up or get curious when I hear my domain of power come up in conversation.
I dress to blend in (or stand out).
It irks me that mortals take a long time to do anything. It doesn't help that now I'm the same.I accept (or condemn) people of other faiths. I try to get along (or argue) with them.
I accept (or condemn) people of other faiths. I try to get along (or argue) with them.
I have little or no experience interacting with mortals. I have trouble socializing with them.
{@bold Responsibility.} Being stripped of my power does not make me any less bound to my duty. It's still my responsibility to guide and watch over mortals. (Good)
{@bold Compliance.} I must get along with mortals and live by their rules if I wish to mingle with them. (Lawful)
{@bold Liberty.} Now that I have lost my power, I can pursue a new passion and do as I wish. (Chaotic)
{@bold Tyranny.} Being stripped of my power will not stop me from lording over mortals. (Evil)
{@bold Secrecy.} I must keep my identity a secret if I wish to avoid real trouble. (Neutral)
{@bold Restoration.} Someday I will get my power back. (Any)
I will not rest until I've finally confronted those who took my power.
When my divine family abandoned me, the mortals took me in. I choose them over the gods any day.
My worshippers are valuable to me. They are the only ones I have left.
Despite my circumstances, I will do anything to protect other deities from suffering the same fate I have suffered.
I have come to appreciate the peaceful, quiet life of a mortal. Anyone who disturbs it will pay.
I will do anything for the mortal I fell in love with.
Admitting failures and mistakes is a thing mortals do.
I don't understand the value of a single mortal life - mortals can always make more mortals.
My temper makes me forget that I am no longer a powerful being.
I hardly feel sorry after doing something 'wrong' to anyone.
I feel miserable when my friends do better than me.
I will do anything to get my power restored to me. Anything.

entries.name: Variant Fallen: Forgotten
entries: You are an ancient, lost to history. Fewer and fewer came to be faithful to you, and others gained dominance. You have become forgotten, both in memory and power. You now live your life as a mortal.
If your predicament is caused by a lack or absence or worshippers, choose the Old Ruins feature instead of the Protection of the Faithful feature.

entries.name: Variant Feature: Old Ruins
entries: If your character has a fallen background, you may select this background feature instead of Protection of the Faithful.

You know the locations of abandoned places of worship dedicated to you. Aside from being completely abandoned, there is no food to be found, and there's very few or no objects aside from furniture. Although these places are in varying stages of decay, they remain intact enough to be used as shelter.

_.special: common clothes made from an unusual material or in an odd style relevant to a plane where you spent time
piece of terrain or other trinket from a plane you visited

items.name: Skill Proficiencies
items.entry: Choose two from among {@skill Arcana}, {@skill Insight}, {@skill Perception}, {@skill Stealth}

items.name: Equipment
items.entry: A set of common clothes made from an unusual material or in an odd style relevant to a plane where you spent time, a piece of terrain or another trinket from a plane you visited, and a belt {@item pouch|phb} containing 15 gp

entries.name: Plane-Touched
entries: Intelligent, nonhostile creatures who are native to a different planes and exotic cultures sense a kindred spirit in you. They are more willing to converse with you or offer you hospitality, and readily share lore of their native plane with the belief that you welcome such knowledge.

entries.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: Far plane wanderers have spent time in strange and alien places, and it's opened their eyes to new languages and cultures that don't exist on the Material Plane. They are often hungry for knowledge and eager to learn by conversing with others. Conversely, their time in another plane might make them wary and hyper-aware of the deadly threats of the multiverse.

rows: An exotic language was my native tongue for a long time. I sometimes relapse into speaking it when I'm excited or distracted.
I have an eye for items that originate from another plane and love collecting them.
I picked up odd habits or cultural mannerisms from people of another plane that leaves others around me baffled.
I'm never satisfied staying in one place for long. The more unusual and exotic the next destination, the better!
I sometimes forget and attempt to move myself through force of will, as though I were still on a plane like the Astral Sea or Limbo.
I wear clothes, jewelry, or other trinkets considered fashionable on another plane but bizarre among the peoples of the Material Plane.
I keep a journal with me and record the cultural oddities of the places I visit like a planar anthropologist.
I'm obsessed with planar magic and teleportation.
Dominance. The only law of the multiverse is strength. (Evil)
Wonder. The multiverse is a beautiful place full of amazing cultures. (Good)
Malleability. Even the laws of physics can change on a whim. I should be just as adaptable. (Chaotic)
Order. A strong will can impose structure and serenity to even the most chaotic planes. (Lawful)
Balance. All elements, even light and dark, are balanced between opposites in the multiverse. (Neutral)
Aspiration. I've seen more incredible places and peoples than others could dare to dream. I must use those experiences to have an impact on the world. (Any)
I escaped slavery under an extraplanar master. I fear bonds and wonder if they're still hunting their lost 'property.'
I had a meaningful relationship with someone on another plane, and they were lost to me. I hope to find my way back to them one day.
Someone was following me throughout my planar travels. I never found out why or how they continued to stalk me across the multiverse.
I called a particular city or settlement in a particular plane home for some time.
An organization or individual is keenly interested in stories of my travels, though I'm not entirely sure why.
I travelled the planes with a companion. Our shared experiences brought us closer than the bonds of blood.
I look down on people who have never left their hometown or their own country.
I show off my multilingual talent and cultural knowledge to show my superiority to others.
I often vocally judge the quality of items or practices by comparing them to similar things I've seen on my travels.
My fond reminiscing about planar travels can distract me from the here and now.
Bad experiences in the multiverse have made me distrustful and wary.
I sometimes misjudge people because I'm used to completely alien cultures and values.

items.name: Skill Proficiencies
entries: {@skill Deception}, {@skill Travel|TLotRR}

items.name: Tool Proficiency
entries: Land vehicles

items.name: Distinctive Features
entries: Cunning, Proud

A.special: poorly wrought maps from your homeland that depict where you are
small piece of jewelry in the style of your homeland's craftsmanship

items.name: Tool Proficiency:
items.entry: Choose one kind of {@item Musical Instrument|XPHB}

items.name: Equipment:
items.entry: Choose A or B: (A) {@item Musical Instrument|XPHB} (same as above), {@item Dagger|XPHB}, {@item Rope|XPHB}, {@item Bedroll|XPHB}, {@item Traveler's Clothes|XPHB}, {@item Pouch|xphb}, {@item Tent|xphb}, poorly wrought maps from your homeland that depict where you are, a small piece of jewelry in the style of your homeland's craftsmanship, 20 GP; or (B) 50 GP

entries.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: You are from a distant place, one so remote that few common folk realize that it exists, and chances are good that even if some people you meet have heard of your homeland, they know merely the name and perhaps a few outrageous stories. You have come to this part of Selerim for your own reasons, which you might or might not choose to share.

colLabels: I became a far traveler because...
rows: I am an emissary from a far-flung nation, seeking alliances and knowledge to bring back to my homeland.
I was exiled for my beliefs, my actions, or a crime—real or fabricated—and now I wander in search of a new purpose.
A desperate flight from justice—or injustice—left me with no choice but to keep moving, lest I be caught.
Faith and prophecy sent me on a sacred journey, one that takes me ever farther from home.
I am a sightseer of sorts, desperate to soak up all the magnificent views this world has to offer.
The road calls to me, and I have never felt content staying in one place for long.
I have different assumptions from those around me concerning personal space, blithely invading others' space in innocence, or reacting to ignorant invasion of my own.
I have my own ideas about what is and is not food, and I find the eating habits of those around me fascinating, confusing, or revolting.
I have a strong code of honor or sense of propriety that others don't comprehend.
I express affection or contempt in ways that are unfamiliar to others.
I honor my deities through practices that are foreign to this land.
I begin or end my day with small traditional rituals that are unfamiliar to those around me.
Open. I have much to learn from the kindly folk I meet along my way. (Good)
Reserved. As someone new to these strange lands, I am cautious and respectful in my dealings. (Lawful)
Adventure. I'm far from home, and everything is strange and wonderful! (Chaotic)
Cunning. Though I may not know their ways, neither do they know mine, which can be to my advantage. (Evil)
Inquisitive. Everything is new, but I have a thirst to learn. (Neutral)
Suspicious. I must be careful, for I have no way of telling friend from foe here. (Any)
So long as I have this token from my homeland, I can face any adversity in this strange land.
The gods of my people are a comfort to me so far away from home.
I hold no greater cause than my service to my people.
My freedom is my most precious possession. I'll never let anyone take it from me again.
I'm fascinated by the beauty and wonder of this new land.
Though I had no choice, I lament having to leave my loved one(s) behind. I hope to see them again one day.
I am secretly (or not so secretly) convinced of the superiority of my own culture over that of this foreign land.
I pretend not to understand the local language in order to avoid interactions I would rather not have.
I have a weakness for the new intoxicants and other pleasures of this land.
I don't take kindly to some of the actions and motivations of the people of this land, because these folks are different from me.
I consider the adherents of other gods to be deluded innocents at best, or ignorant fools at worst.
I have a weakness for the exotic beauty of the people of these lands.

items.name: Skill Proficiencies
entries: {@skill Athletics}, {@skill Travel|TLotRR}

items.name: Tool Proficiency
entries: Land vehicles

items.name: Distinctive Features
entries: Bold, True-hearted

items.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: You grew up close to the land. Years tending animals and cultivating the earth rewarded you with patience and good health. You have a keen appreciation for nature's bounty alongside a healthy respect for nature's wrath.

rows: I was born into a family of farmers and continued the tradition.
My village was destroyed, and I became a farmer to help rebuild and sustain the survivors.
My family made a pact with a nature spirit to care for the land in exchange for its protection.
An old farmer took me in when I had nowhere else to go.
The land I farm was a gift or reward for my service to a noble.
I was stranded in a small farming town after a horse knocked my memories out of my head.
I rise before the sun every day and believe that a strong work ethic builds character.
I have an unshakable connection to the land and often speak of it as if it were alive.
I refuse to harm animals and I will not consume any animal products.
I tend to treat everyone with the same care and patience that I give my crops.
I have a stubborn streak as wide as a plow—once I've made up my mind, it's hard to change.
I measure success by the health of the earth and the quality of what it produces.
I'm deeply superstitious, performing rituals to ensure good harvests and ward off bad luck.
I have a natural talent for storytelling and love sharing tales of life on the farm, often with embellishments.
Harmony. The land provides for us when we respect its balance and natural rhythms. (Good)
Self-Reliance. Hard work and determination are the keys to a fruitful life. (Lawful)
Freedom. Every person should have the right to cultivate their own land and reap their own rewards. (Chaotic)
Exploitation. The land and those who work it exist to serve my ambitions, no matter the cost. (Evil)
Ambition. I aim to create a legacy so great that generations will remember my name. (Any)
Resilience. Like a hardy crop, I believe that enduring hardship makes us stronger. (Neutral)
The farm I grew up on is my sanctuary, and I'll do anything to protect it.
I am devoted to an ancient tree or landmark on my land, which I believe holds mystical power.
I owe my livelihood to a neighbor who helped me when my crops failed.
I'm determined to reclaim the fertile land my family lost to a greedy noble.
My bond with my animals is stronger than any bond I have with people.
I work tirelessly to ensure my children (or future generations) inherit a prosperous farm.
I am fiercely protective of my land and often see threats where none exist.
I hoard my harvests, trusting no one to share in what I've grown.
I can't resist a gamble, whether it's with crops, coin, or my future.
I hold grudges against those who wronged me, even for minor slights.
I am obsessed with perfecting my crops, often neglecting relationships and my own well-being.
I distrust anyone who doesn't understand or value hard work in the fields.

items.name: Equipment
items.entry: A {@variantrule farm implements|BelzorMM|farm implement} (such as a {@item pitchfork|BelzorMM} or {@item shovel|phb}), a set of {@item work clothes|BelzorMM} or {@item common clothes|phb}, a wide-brimmed hat, a sack containing 5 gp worth of {@filter trade goods|items|type=trade good}, and a belt pouch containing 5 gp or {@dice 1d4+2} gp.

entries.name: Feature: Of the Land
entries: You lack the formal education of the higher classes, but for how little you may know there is a great deal that you understand. You have a practical, working knowledge of astrology and meteorology, and can easily track the time and date as well as predict the weather within a few hours, or days if you're lucky. You understand the "secrets of life"; the needs of life (water, light, air, salt, etc.), the patterns of physical inheritance, and the connections between different plants and animals.

entries.name: Farm
entries: Not every farm is alike; there are a vast range of goods produced by farmers of different sorts, and nearly all farms focus on just one product or a limited group of products.

rows: {@b Rancher.} You raised animals for slaughter most likely for food, but also for leather, furs, and other useful materials.
{@b Grazier.} You harvested goods produced by animals such as milk, eggs, feathers, or wool.
{@b Stockman.} You bred animals to sell for work or as pets such as guard dogs, racing horses, and griffons.
{@b Peasant.} You harvested edible or useful plants such as wheat, corn crops, or apples at an orchard.
{@b Forester.} You grew trees for ornament or construction such as trees grown for bow staves, boat masts, or buildings.
{@b Silk.} You raised silk worms or another exotic animal, and harvested their silk.
I'm always early to bed and early to rise.
I keep my gear and supplies in careful check.
I speak with a distinctive drawl or accent common to my class.
I always save up as much as I can, spending and consuming only what I must.
When work needs doing, I do the work.
I keep constant track of the sun, moon, stars, seasons, and weather.
I like to sleep in the sun when I can.
I'm always chewing on a sprig of grass, a toothpick, tobacco, seeds, or preserved meat.
{@b Fill the Need.} There are a lot of hungry mouths in the world, with enough hands the world can feed them all. (Good)
{@b It's a Living.} I do what I'm good at because what I'm good at is good for me. (Neutral)
{@b Brutal Practicality.} Bury a fish or bury a man, just get the job done. (Evil)
{@b Hard Work.} A labor of love is a purpose and meaning. (Lawful)
{@b A Simple Way of Life.} If it ain't broke, don't fix it! (Neutral)
{@b Amusement.} Playing a hand in the growth and development of things delights me. (Chaotic)
I want to find that special someone and raise a home full of children.
I'll never forget the family farm I grew up on.
Some day, I'll be the lord of my own land.
I want to become the biggest or best example of my profession to prove that I am the best!
My son was sent to war and never returned. I must find him!
I am out to start a homestead of my own in an unexplored fringe territory.
I can be lazy and sleepy, sneaking off to take naps when work can wait.
I am absurdly isolated, innocent, or pious.
I believe in and obey my nation's nobility blindly.
I abandoned my home to avoid taxation, conscription, or court and cannot return.
I am not used to being wealthy and tend to overindulge.
I show off to attractive people too much.

images.title: Jean Francois Millet, {@i Peasant Spreading Manure}

entries: You were what most common folk are–a farmer. You worked on a lord's estate, their land, or you worked for a company and you produced resources from the land in return for food, shelter, clothing, protection, and other benefits. Farmers focus on raising living things and harvesting various useful goods–mostly food–from the land. Farmers make up the vast majority of the peasantry, alongside other raw resource producers, such as miners and fishermen. Farmers are a hearty, enduring folk, they work long hours under the sun often doing dirty and exhausting or even disgusting work. How did you become a farmer, and for how long were you one? What did you do on your farm? Were you the landlord of the farm, or were you just a farmhand? And what caused you to leave that life behind? Was your home destroyed by war? Were you cast out for some crime? Did you flee taxes you could not pay? Were you called to join the Lord's army? Was your home stolen by an unscrupulous rival? How did you learn your current profession?

name: Farmer

_: token given to you by your family when you left home

entries: You are the most vital citizen in any land, the producer and grower of food. From a young age you learned to care for the land and do chores until dusk. From these humble origins you venture out into the world.

items.name: Tool Proficiencies
items.entry: One musical instrument of your choice and vehicles (land)

items.name: Equipment
items.entry: A set of common clothes, a token given to you by your family when you left home, and a small pouch containing 5 gp

entries.name: Simple Folk
entries: Farmers of all types work across the land. Work with your DM to determine the type of land and work you specialized in, or roll on the table below.

rows: Grain Field
Rice Field
Vineyard
Cattle Ranch
Poultry Farm
Fruit Orchard
Vegetable Field
Horse Ranch
Shephard's Field
Fisher's Coast

entries.name: Feature: Farmer's Almanac
entries: Thanks to a lifetime growing food, you are able to discern simple information. You can accurately predict the weather in your area for the next week. You know what food is worth, and you can haggle for a better price for produce.

Additionally, when looking for shelter in farmlands, common folk are always willing to host you so long as you offer aid around the property. Your hosts will not shelter you from the law if it would bring harm to themselves.

entries.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: Farmers are humble and hardy folk with simple values. They hold to work ethic and emphasize communal ties.

rows: The wisdom of my ancestors gives me a unique outlook on life.
As a child, I played hero. Now that I'm of age, I'm determined to become one.
Nothing is more important than a job well done.
I've never backed down from a barnyard brawl.
I may not be the best thinker, but there's a simple solution to everything.
I celebrate the little things in life because I don't know when the hard times will hit.
I couldn't wait to get out of my small life in the farmlands and into the broader world.
I'm hard to bore. There's always something I can do to improve myself.
{@bold Diligence.} Don't put off to tomorrow work that can be done today. Laziness is a vice. (Lawful)
{@bold Preparation.}  Like the seasons, life changes frequently. Prepare for change and you'll come out on top. (Any)
{@bold Generous Pride.} Watching another enjoy the fruits of your labor is one of life's luxuries. (Good)
{@bold Freedom.} The landlord can't see everything that goes down in the stables. Enjoy life's little opportunities to let loose and have fun. (Chaotic)
{@bold Packing Order.}  Every animal has a social hierarchy. I'm the strongest, so what I say goes. (Evil)
{@bold Fairness.} Everyone helps around the farm from a young age, favorite child or not. All people must do their part. (Lawful)
I set out to earn riches for my family so they don't have to live harvest to harvest.
I've worked the land, I love the land, and I will protect the land at any cost.
Bandits raped and pillaged my hometown. I will destroy those bandits one day.
My landlord is kind to his people. I will pay back that kindness and make him proud to be my liege.
I was born in bondage but earned my freedom. I will become rich enough to free my family.
I am in love with a friend. I will do anything to protect their perfect smile.
I distrust and dislike new people. Most people just weren't raised right.
I only know country manners, and I don't know proper behavior in civilized settings. I ain't no cosmopolitan.
I'm a gullible and naive country person. It's easy for people to con me.
I was born and raised a servant to my betters. I find it hard to stand up to authority figures.
I'm a bit too fond of alcohol, and I don't hold my liquor well.
I got a girl pregnant, and ran from the wedding - a decision I regret. I'm prone to simply running from difficult situations instead of dealing with them.

items.name: Equipment
items.entry: A {@variantrule farm implements|dndwiki-bestbackgrounds|farm implement} (such as a {@item pitchfork|dndwiki-bestbackgrounds} or {@item shovel|phb}), a set of {@item work clothes|dndwiki-bestbackgrounds} or {@item common clothes|phb}, a wide-brimmed hat, a sack containing 5 gp worth of {@filter trade goods|items|type=trade good}, and a belt pouch containing 5 gp or {@dice 1d4+2} gp.

entries.name: Feature: Of the Land
entries: You lack the formal education of the higher classes, but for how little you may know there is a great deal that you understand. You have a practical, working knowledge of astrology and meteorology, and can easily track the time and date as well as predict the weather within a few hours, or days if you're lucky. You understand the "secrets of life"; the needs of life (water, light, air, salt, etc.), the patterns of physical inheritance, and the connections between different plants and animals.
