entries: Not every farm is alike; there are a vast range of goods produced by farmers of different sorts, and nearly all farms focus on just one product or a limited group of products.

rows: {@b Rancher.} You raised animals for slaughter most likely for food, but also for leather, furs, and other useful materials.
{@b Grazier.} You harvested goods produced by animals such as milk, eggs, feathers, or wool.
{@b Stockman.} You bred animals to sell for work or as pets such as guard dogs, racing horses, and griffons.
{@b Peasant.} You harvested edible or useful plants such as wheat, corn crops, or apples at an orchard.
{@b Forester.} You grew trees for ornament or construction such as trees grown for bow staves, boat masts, or buildings.
{@b Silk.} You raised silk worms or another exotic animal, and harvested their silk.
I'm always early to bed and early to rise.
I keep my gear and supplies in careful check.
I speak with a distinctive drawl or accent common to my class.
I always save up as much as I can, spending and consuming only what I must.
When work needs doing, I do the work.
I keep constant track of the sun, moon, stars, seasons, and weather.
I like to sleep in the sun when I can.
I'm always chewing on a sprig of grass, a toothpick, tobacco, seeds, or preserved meat.
{@b Fill the Need.} There are a lot of hungry mouths in the world, with enough hands the world can feed them all. (Good)
{@b It's a Living.} I do what I'm good at because what I'm good at is good for me. (Neutral)
{@b Brutal Practicality.} Bury a fish or bury a man, just get the job done. (Evil)
{@b Hard Work.} A labor of love is a purpose and meaning. (Lawful)
{@b A Simple Way of Life.} If it ain't broke, don't fix it! (Neutral)
{@b Amusement.} Playing a hand in the growth and development of things delights me. (Chaotic)
I want to find that special someone and raise a home full of children.
I'll never forget the family farm I grew up on.
Some day, I'll be the lord of my own land.
I want to become the biggest or best example of my profession to prove that I am the best!
My son was sent to war and never returned. I must find him!
I am out to start a homestead of my own in an unexplored fringe territory.
I can be lazy and sleepy, sneaking off to take naps when work can wait.
I am absurdly isolated, innocent, or pious.
I believe in and obey my nation's nobility blindly.
I abandoned my home to avoid taxation, conscription, or court and cannot return.
I am not used to being wealthy and tend to overindulge.
I show off to attractive people too much.

images.title: Jean Francois Millet, {@i Peasant Spreading Manure}

entries: You were what most common folk are–a farmer. You worked on a lord's estate, their land, or you worked for a company and you produced resources from the land in return for food, shelter, clothing, protection, and other benefits. Farmers focus on raising living things and harvesting various useful goods–mostly food–from the land. Farmers make up the vast majority of the peasantry, alongside other raw resource producers, such as miners and fishermen. Farmers are a hearty, enduring folk, they work long hours under the sun often doing dirty and exhausting or even disgusting work. How did you become a farmer, and for how long were you one? What did you do on your farm? Were you the landlord of the farm, or were you just a farmhand? And what caused you to leave that life behind? Was your home destroyed by war? Were you cast out for some crime? Did you flee taxes you could not pay? Were you called to join the Lord's army? Was your home stolen by an unscrupulous rival? How did you learn your current profession?

items.name: Equipment
items.entry: A handaxe or sickle, a set of common clothes, and a pouch containing 5 gp

entries.name: Feature: Plowshares to Swords
entries: You're a simple, hard-working individual, trying to make ends meet in this crazy world. Some (possibly abstract) authority figure took everything from you, and you've had enough. Common folk are sympathetic to your plight, and you can find a place to hide, rest, or recuperate among them, unless you have shown yourself to be a danger to them. They will shield you from the law or anyone else searching for you, though they will not risk their lives for you.

entries.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: A farmer is one of the common people, for better or for worse. Most farmers look on their humble origins as a virtue, not a shortcoming, and their home communities remain very important to them.

rows: I judge people by their actions, not their words.
If someone is in trouble, I'm always ready to lend help.
When I set my mind to something, I follow through no matter what gets in my way.
I have a strong sense of fair play and always try to find the most equitable solution to arguments.
I'm confident in my own abilities and do what I can to instill confidence in others.
Thinking is for other people. I prefer action.
I misuse long words in an attempt to sound smarter.
I get bored easily. When am I going to get on with my destiny?
Respect. People deserve to be treated with dignity and respect. (Good)
Fairness. No one should get preferential treatment before the law, and no one is above the law. (Lawful)
Freedom. Tyrants must not be allowed to oppress the people. (Chaotic)
Might. If I become strong, I can take what I want—what I deserve. (Evil)
Sincerity. There's no good in pretending to be something I'm not. (Neutral)
Destiny. Nothing and no one can steer me away from my higher calling. (Any)
I have a family, but I have no idea where they are. One day, I hope to see them again.
I worked the land, I love the land, and I will protect the land.
A proud noble once gave me a horrible beating, and I will take my revenge on any bully I encounter.
My tools are symbols of my past life, and I carry them so that I will never forget my roots.
I protect those who cannot protect themselves.
I wish my childhood sweetheart had come with me to pursue my destiny.
The tyrant who rules my land will stop at nothing to see me killed.
I'm convinced of the significance of my destiny, and blind to my shortcomings and the risk of failure.
The people who knew me when I was young know my shameful secret, so I can never go home again.
I have a weakness for the vices of the city, especially hard drink.
Secretly, I believe that things would be better if I were a tyrant lording over the land.
I have trouble trusting in my allies.

_.special: set of tools you are proficient with
farm implement (such as a pitchfork or shovel)
sack worth of trade goods (see PHB Equipment chapter)

items.name: Tool Proficiencies
items.entry: Vehicles (land), your choice of {@item cook's utensils|phb} or {@item brewer's|phb} supplies

items.name: Equipment
items.entry: One set of tools you are proficient with, a farm implement (such as a pitchfork or shovel), common clothes, a wide-brimmed hat, a sack containing 5 gp worth of trade goods (see PHB Equipment chapter), and a belt pouch containing 10 gp.

entries.name: Overview
entries: You have spent much of your life working with the Greenhands to produce food for the city, either tending crops or livestock or both. Are you from one of the wealthy families that owns terraced farmland sloping down from the city's walls, or greenhouses on the upper levels where plants can get sunlight? Or did you labor as a simple farmhand? In either case, you are accustomed to long days of hard work. If you were of one of the wealthy farming families, however, you also enjoyed the privileges of your station, including frequent meals made with real food rather than bland but filling conjured foodstuffs.

entries.name: Feature: Farmer's Almanac
entries: Thanks to a lifetime growing food in every imaginable condition, you are able to provide simple information and goods for your companions. You can accurately predict the weather in a maelstrom free area for the next week. You know what food is really worth, and you can often haggle a better price for produce.

name: Fate-Touched
entries: Players are not intended to select this background, but this is instead provided for the dungeon master to consider for one or more of their players, or perhaps a prominent NPC, as their campaign unfolds. It provides very minor mechanical benefit, but instead adds an element of lore, importance, and fate-bearing responsibility to a character within your story. Being fate-touched overlaps and co-exists with the character's current background, only adding to their mystique. Consider it for a player character who would benefit from being put more central to the coming conflicts of your adventure, or for an NPC who may require protection as they come into their destiny. Perhaps consider a powerful villain discovering their fate-twisting nature and using it to wreak havoc. All of these possibilities and more can be explored should you choose to include a fate-touched within your campaign.

entries.name: Feature: Wicked Awareness
entries: Your fate-touched essence occasionally leads surrounding events to shift in your favor. You gain 1 Luck point, as per the {@feat Lucky} feat outlined within the Player's Handbook pg 167. This luck point is used in the same fashion as the feat, and you regain this expended luck point when you finish a long rest. If you already have the Lucky feat, you add this luck point to your total for the feat.

Many lives and many souls find their ways through the patterns of fate and destiny, their threads following the path meant for them, oblivious and eager to be a part of the woven essence of history meant for them. Some souls, however, glide forth with mysterious influence, their threads bending the weave around them, toward them, unknowingly guiding history itself wherever they walk. Events both magnificent and catastrophic tend to follow such individuals. These souls often become great rulers and terrible tyrants, powerful mages, religious leaders, and legendary heroes of lore. These are the fate-touched.

Few fate-touched ever become aware of their prominent nature. Outside of powerful divination magics, it's extremely difficult to confirm one as fate-touched. There are many communities that regard the status as a terrible omen, treating a confirmed fate-touched with mistrust and fear. Others seek them as a blessing, rallying around them for guidance. Some of renown and power grow jealous, wishing to bend a fate-touched beneath their will, and some stories speak of mages of old attempting to extract or transfer the essence itself.

name: Fennblade
entries: {@b Weapon Proficiencies:} Greatswords.

Marching forward, swinging massive cleaving blades in wide arcs, Fennblades are a force of nature that hacks through soldiers and warjacks alike. The fighting art has been adopted by kriels across western Immoren.

entries.name: Feature: Drive Them Back
entries: You have been trained to fight shoulder to shoulder with your kin. When an enemy attack damages one or more friendly creatures within 10 feet of you, you can use your reaction to move up to 15 feet toward the attacker and make a single melee attack. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

entries.caption: Personality Trait
rows: I stand firm in the face of danger, even if it means more harm comes to me.
Some compare me to a raging dire troll on the field of battle.
Blades do not lie, and neither do I.
Showing others compassion means a stronger family.
I march on my stomach, and hunger turns me sour.
I honor the ancestors and my fallen comrades who shall never be forgotten.
I will laugh and sing the old songs, even as the world comes to an end.
People tend to view me as rough and without manners.

entries.caption: Ideal
rows: Might. On the battlefield, others will witness my strength. (Any)
Comradeship. Only by standing together can we win. (Good)
Guardian. Fighting means more than victory—it means survival of my kin. (Good)
Brute Force. Only through crushing my enemies do I feel alive. (Evil)
Vendetta. Any who taint the ancestral homelands must be cleaved in two. (Evil)
Faith. Dhunia has a destiny for us all in the cycle of nature. (Neutral)

entries.caption: Bond
rows: Corvis, while a human city, is not without its delights.
My family harbors a secret that would tear the kriel apart.
I am hunted by a family of Khadoran hunters because I killed one of their own for threatening a trollkin child.
During the Claiming, I lost a family heirloom, and I will travel to find it when possible.
I helped to found the kriel and have lived here for many years.
A fellow trollkin in the Cygnaran army is a friendly rival, and we have faced each other a few times on the field of battle.

entries.caption: Flaw
rows: I hope to take a seat on the council of my kriel.
Never have I run from a fight, and that often gets me into trouble.
Calling out liars to their face is important to me.
Money never lasts me long, as I buy too much food and drink.
It takes my friends' tremendous effort and calming words to break me out of a mindless rage.
North, south, east, west—these are no help to me, as I lose my bearings all the time.

name: Feral Blood
entries: You descend from a specific Spirit Animal. You gain advantage on Wisdom ({@skill Animal Handling}) checks for that specific type of animal (e.g. cheetah or vulture).

Like an outlander, you grew up in the wilds far removed from the trappings of civilization. But most outlanders live in organized tribes, remote nomadic nations, and other societies. You did not. Instead, you were raised among inhuman creatures, who left you with a unique sense of normalcy.

Even if you have lived among more typical humanoids, giants, or other 'civilized' species for many years, your odd behaviors and inadequate education on social mores can cause mutual discomfort—or even lead to violence.

items.name: Languages:
items.entry: One of {@language Bullywug|mm}, {@language Gnoll|mm}, {@language Grell|mm}, {@language Grung|mm}, {@language Hook Horror|mm}, {@language Otyugh|mm}, {@language Sahuagin|mm}, {@language Troglodyte|mm}, {@language Umber Hulk|mm}, {@language Worg|mm}, {@language Yeti|mm}, or another language spoken by a giant animal such as a {@language Giant Owl|mm}.

items.name: Equipment:
items.entry: A {@item dagger|phb}, 50 feet of {@item hempen rope (50 feet)|phb}, a {@item net|phb}, {@item fishing tackle|phb}, a set of {@item common clothes|phb}, and a {@item pouch|phb} containing 5 gp

entries.name: Brutish Behaviors
entries: Your near-alien origins make you conduct yourself in ways that seem entirely reasonable to you and bizarre or even horrific to others with more delicate attitudes. Choose a behavior or roll on the table below.

rows: Cannibalism
Public defecation/urination
Violent responses to surprises or insult
Aggressive mating displays/attempts
Refusal to wear appropriate clothing
Abnormal volume
Territoriality
Sloppy, offensive table manners

entries.name: Feature: Breath of the Wild
entries: Wild beasts often recognize you as kin, and respond accordingly. Through gestures, tone, guttural sounds, and body language, you can share simple concepts and ideas with most beasts and monstrosities.
You also gain sustenance from almost any vegetable or protein source, including normally indigestible substances like compost, bone, fur, and feces.

entries.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: Feral children are no strangers to being strangers in strange lands. They often feel out of place and alienated by those around them, even if they are more like their new acquaintances than they are the animals that raised them.

rows: The civilized world is full of wonders to experience.
I find the strongest creature in any given area so I can challenge it for dominance.
I love testing myself in dangerous situations and grow bored when comfortable.
I wish I could kill the people who annoy me, the way I can animals.
I want to learn more about my biological heritage.
My way of living is superior; civilization makes you soft.
I am terrified of magic and technology I don't understand.
A united pack under a strong leader makes me happiest.
{@b Education.} I want to experience more of the trappings of civilization and immerse myself in it. (Lawful)
{@b Preservation.} The wilds and civilization both have merits, but nature needs more protection. (Good)
{@b Expression.} Society ties us down and restricts our ability to be our true selves. (Chaotic)
{@b Regression.} Humanity must be returned to a more primal state by force, for its own good. (Evil)
{@b Survival.} Life is dangerous and I must do whatever I can to meet my needs. (Neutral)
{@b Exploration.} The world holds many wonders, and I'm determined to see them all. (Any)
Encroaching humanoids destroyed my home and I want to stop it from ever happening again.
I recognized my true species and left (or was banished) to discover my true identity and origins.
A great predator stalks me; our past and future battles guide my behavior now.
I have an insatiable drive for knowledge about my heritage and to act like those who look like me.
I would do anything to return to the wilds, but can't.
Danger makes me feel truly alive.
Rank, station, and social standing mean nothing to me.
I hate wearing clothes any more than I have to.
Violence gets both people and animals to back off. I refuse to accept the long-term consequences.
Gifts confuse, trouble, or even offend me.
I enjoy others' reactions to my antics and 'misbehave' on purpose.
I don't respect the sanctity of property unless forced to.

_.special: A flower with petals that will never wilt

items.name: Tool Proficiencies
items.entry: One type of {@filter gaming set|items|source=phb|miscellaneous=mundane|type=gaming set}, one type of {@filter musical instrument|items|source=phb|miscellaneous=mundane|type=instrument}

items.name: Equipment
items.entry: A flower with petals that will never wilt, a {@filter musical instrument|items|source=phb|miscellaneous=mundane|type=instrument} (one of your choice), a set of {@item fine clothes|PHB}, and a pouch containing 10 gp

entries.name: Life-changing Event
entries: The fey have a multitude of reasons for abducting—or rescuing—folk like you, and it's also possible that you or others did something to bring about your situation. Choose or randomly determine the reason behind your sojourn in the realm of the fey.

rows: My Childhood was tithed to the fey by my Family in return for prosperity for as long I remained in their care.
I made a bargain with a fox to play with its cubs in their den. The fox turned out to be an emissary of the Summer Court, and I was not released until the cubs came of age.

Centuries ago my ancestors were rulers and made a political alliance with the fey in exchange for tribute to be paid every third generation. We are no longer rulers, but the fey still demand their tithe.
I have no memories of my past before I was taken by the fey.
I wandered into an ancient, primeval wood shortly after learning to walk and was found by the fey, who took me in.
A fey child befriended me and invited me to their home.
I am the only Survivor of a fey raid. They killed my parents, but spared me for their own unknowable reasons.
My parents could not care for me, and their choices were to abandon me in a Forest or a city. They chose the Forest.

entries.name: Feature: First Impressions
entries: You were raised in a situation in which failing to adhere to the nuances, niceties, and intrigues of the fey court could have catastrophic repercussions. The first impressions one makes set the tone for future endeavors. You have learned that lesson well, and continue to apply it. In your initial social interaction with an individual fey, you gain a +2 bonus to the first Charisma-based check you make.

entries.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: A fey hostage will never forget the events that led to their capture, the treatment they experienced, or the circumstances of their release. Their experiences with the unpredictable fey might range from whimsical to pathological.

rows: I remain a child in thought, action, and deed.
I defer decisions to elves and fey that I encounter, always looking to them for Guidance.
I long for the accommodations and sustenance I became accustomed to as a hostage of the Fair Folk.
I distrust any who display Traits of fey heritage.
I tell others what I think they want to hear, whether I believe it not, to keep them happy.
I see danger in every Shadow, enemies behind each door, and threats in the eyes of strangers.
I never speak unless spoken to, and never look people in the eyes.
I am fascinated, Frightened, and uncomfortable in an urban Environment.
I left a friend behind when I escaped, and I am gathering resources to return and free them.
I did not Escape from my fey captors. They allowed me my freedom in exchange for my continued clandestine service.
I earned my freedom by tricking another to take my place with the fey. My betrayal of that person's trust haunts me.
I am free because of the actions of an unknown Benefactor. I wait for them to reveal why I was released.
I feel a constant, ever-tugging connection to the lands of the fey.
I was given my freedom after years of diligent, demeaning, and debauched servitude.
I cannot lie outright, only by omission, because of my years with the fey.
I will never willingly make another promise to anyone or anything.
The fey creature that abducted me haunts me in my dreams.
I will never accept free food, drink, or gifts from strangers.
I speak in sing-song voice and in rhymes. I never answer questions directly.
I am certain that my freedom from the fey is only temporary and that any fey I meet want to recapture me.
{@b Art.} Works of art are meant to question, challenge, and disturb. (Any)
{@b Pleasure.} There are no long-term Rewards, only the enjoyments of the moment. (Chaotic)
{@b Independence.} Independence is the privilege of the few who are strong to assert it. (Any)
{@b Fellowship.} Lasting fellowship is born in shared suffering and Teamwork when overcoming adversity. (Any)
{@b Self-}confidence. There are no views, perspectives, or standards of any worth aside from my own. (Evil)
{@b Malice.} I feel nothing but spite, rancor, and envy for those that took me, and for those that let me be taken. (Evil)

entries: Years, possibly centuries, ago you were captured by the fey. Each host, as the fey called themselves, treated their "guest" differently. The Relationship you forged with your captors defines you just as strongly as the circumstances of your abduction and of your Escape or release. You have been indelibly marked—emotionally, psychically, and physically—by the fey and their Special brand of hospitality.

items.name: Skill Proficiency
entries: {@skill Animal Handling}, {@skill Nature}

entries: One {@filter musical instrument|items|source=phb|miscellaneous=mundane|type=instrument}

entries: Sylvan and one other common language

entries: One {@filter musical instrument|items|source=phb|miscellaneous=mundane|type=instrument}, 20 gp

entries.name: Feature: Fortune of the Forest
entries: When you find yourself in the areas of the world outside of civilization, your blessed nature in the eyes of the fey come in handy. When you are lost, or in need of food or water, or trying to build a fire or a makeshift shelter, there's a 50% chance that you gain assistance from a creature of the wild. This might take for the form of a squirrel leading you to a sheltered cave or a fresh, clean spring.

entries.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: The blessing of the fey may have been granted because of who you are, or you may be who you are because of that blessing. While the blessing is often a boon, those who have the attention of the fey often find that it sometimes comes with some unpredictable and not always positive consequences.

rows: My grace and joy at the wonders of life are infectious and raise the spirits of those around me.
My mood changes to match the weather in my area.
I spend every second of my free time playing tunes that I hear in my dreams.
I have the personality that matches one of the wild beasts that live in the area.
I find my solace in the small times of peace and solitude in an otherwise chaotic world.
There is always hope, even when the dread and evil are at their worst.
The arcane {@i is} dangerous and evil, but it must be conquered with compassion rather than violence.
The unexamined life is a blessing that should not be overlooked... or overanalyzed.
Life is too short to not live it to its fullest.
Progress is an arch daemon's playground.
Nothing means anything. Life is futile and uncaring.
Children are the only ones who can make the world right.
The person who made me see the error in my inquisitioning ways keeps me grounded.
My old amulet of office never leaves my neck, a reminder of what I was and what I can never become again.
I adopted the pet of one of my former victims. I care for it as penance for all the lives I destroyed.
My former assistant left the Inquisition with me, and I feel beholden to lead them on a better path.
The spirit of someone who died at my hands has become my friend and confessor.
Although I have left the Inquisition, my former mentor still holds an important place in my heart.
I still exhibit some of the fear and hatred that drove me as an inquisitor.
When things don't go my way, I sulk and pout.
The terrors of my past occupation make others likely to fear and hate me.
I have a difficult time remaining calm when I know someone is lying to me.
I can be quite a coward when I don't have the upper hand in a conflict.
I keep close watch on my finances and never forgive a debt.

entries: You spent years traveling the countryside as a member of the Arcanist Inquisition, seeking out heretics and blasphemers, daemon and arcanist. Your work uncovered hidden evil that likely saved the lives of countless innocents. However, on more than one occasion the zeal of yourself or others brought low individuals who were themselves innocent.

After a crisis of conscience, you left the ranks of the inquisitors. Leaving those ranks is itself a dangerous prospect, but you could no longer abide. Maybe someone you love and care for starting showing arcane affinities that would have led to their destruction. Maybe you did. Maybe the last investigation you performed opened your eyes to new realities.

Now you are living with a target on your back. Your former peers don't take kindly to people leaving their ranks. Those whom you persecuted have not forgotten your deeds. But life must still be lived, and there's more than one way to find and destroy the evil in the world.

items.entry: Choose A or B: (A) {@item Dagger|XPHB}, {@item Musical Instrument|XPHB} (same as above), {@item Traveler's Clothes|XPHB}, 8 GP; or (B) 50 GP

entries: The powerful and fickle faerie-folk of your area have taken note of you, and your existence pleases them. Whether you were born under a lucky star, had a favorable run-in with a nature spirit, or simply were in the right place at the right time, the fey favor you with small gifts and boons. You find small trinkets in your shoes when you wake up in the morning. Beasts of the forest and field are more receptive to your presence and your training. Will this blessing somehow turn into a curse later in your life?

People you encounter instantly recognize your connection with the Realm of Faerie. Sometimes this works to your favor, as folks seem entranced by your glowing personality. Other times your power is a curse just waiting to seep into their lives. And they may not be wrong!

name: Flexible Ancestry
entries: You descend from a Spirit that can sneak such as an Octopus Spirit. Once per day you can sneak into spaces suitable for creatures up to two sizes smaller than you–this lasts for one round and ending it in such a space can result in injury or death.

entries.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: You come from a humble social rank, but you are destined for so much more. Already the people of your home village regard you as their champion, and your destiny calls you to stand against the tyrants and monsters that threaten the common folk everywhere.

colLabels: I became a folk hero because...
rows: I learned what was right and wrong from my family.
I was always enamored by tales of heroes and wished I could be something more than ordinary.
I hated my mundane life, so when it was time for someone to step up and do the right thing, I took my chance.
A parent or one of my relatives was an adventurer, and I was inspired by that person's courage.
A mad old hermit spoke a prophecy when I was born, saying that I would accomplish great things.
I have always stood up for those who are weaker than I am.
I judge people by their actions, not their words.
If someone is in trouble, I'm always ready to lend help.
When I set my mind to something, I follow through no matter what gets in my way.
I have a strong sense of fair play and always try to find the most equitable solution to arguments.
I'm confident in my own abilities and do what I can to instill confidence in others.
Thinking is for other people. I prefer action.
I misuse long words in an attempt to sound smarter.
I get bored easily. When am I going to get on with my destiny?
Respect. People deserve to be treated with dignity and respect. (Good)
Fairness. No one should get preferential treatment before the law, and no one is above the law. (Lawful)
Freedom. Tyrants must not be allowed to oppress the people. (Chaotic)
Might. If I become strong, I can take what I want—what I deserve. (Evil)
Sincerity. There's no good in pretending to be something I'm not. (Neutral)
Destiny. Nothing and no one can steer me away from my higher calling. (Any)
I have a family, but I have no idea where they are. One day, I hope to see them again.
I worked the land, I love the land, and I will protect the land.
A proud noble once gave me a horrible beating, and I will take my revenge on any bully I encounter.
My tools are symbols of my past life, and I carry them so that I will never forget my roots.
I protect those who cannot protect themselves.
I wish my childhood sweetheart had come with me to pursue my destiny.
The tyrant who rules my land will stop at nothing to see me killed.
I'm convinced of the significance of my destiny, and blind to my shortcomings and the risk of failure.
The people who knew me when I was young know my shameful secret, so I can never go home again.
I have a weakness for the vices of the city, especially hard drink.
Secretly, I believe that things would be better if I were a tyrant lording over the land.
I have trouble trusting in my allies.

items.name: Equipment:
items.entry: A set of {@item common clothes|PHB}, a {@item hunting trap|PHB}, a {@item wooden staff|PHB}, a {@item whetstone|PHB}, an {@item explorer's pack|PHB}, and a {@item pouch|PHB} containing 5 gp

entries.name: Feature: Forester
entries: Your experience living, hunting, and foraging in the woods gives you a wealth of experience to draw upon when you are traveling within a forest. If you spend 1 hour observing, examining, and exploring your surroundings while in a forest, you are able to identify a safe location to rest. The area is protected from all but the most extreme elements and from the nonmagical native beasts of the forest. In addition, you are able to find sufficient kindling for a small fire throughout the night.

entries.name: Life-Changing Event
entries: You have lived a simple life deep in the sheltering boughs of the forest, be it as a trapper, farmer, or villager eking out a simple existence in the forest. But something happened that set you on a different path and marked you for greater things. Choose or randomly determine a defining event that caused you to leave your home for the wider world.

rows: You were living within the forest when cesspools of magical refuse from a nearby city expanded and drove away the game that sustained you. You had to move to avoid the prospect of a long, slow demise via starvation.
Your village was razed by a contingent of undead. For reasons of its own, the forest and its denizens protected and hid you from their raid.
A roving band of skeletons and zombies attacked your family while you were hunting.
You are an ardent believer in the preservation of the forest and the natural world. When the people of your village abandoned those beliefs, you were cast out and expelled into the forest.

You wandered into the forest as a child and became lost. For inexplicable reasons, the forest took an interest in you. You have faint memories of a village and have had no contact with civilization in many years.

You were your village's premier hunter. They relied on you for game and without your contributions their survival in the winter was questionable. Upon returning from your last hunt, you found your village in ruins, as if decades had passed overnight.
Your quiet, peaceful, and solitary existence has been interrupted with dreams of the forest's destruction, and the urge to leave your home compels you to seek answers.
Once in a hidden glen, you danced with golden fey and forgotten gods. Nothing in your life since approaches that transcendent moment, cursing you with a wanderlust to seek something that could.

entries.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: Forest dwellers tend toward solitude, introspection, and self-sufficiency. You keep your own council, and you are more likely to watch from a distance than get involved in the affairs of others. You are wary, slow to trust, and cautious of depending on outsiders.

rows: I will never forget being hungry in the winter. I field dress beasts that fall to blade or arrow so that I am never hungry again.
I may be alone in the forest, but I am only ever lonely in cities.
Walking barefoot allows me to interact more intuitively with the natural world.
The road is just another kind of wall. I make my own paths and go where I will.
Others seek the gods in temples and shrines, but I know their will is only revealed in the natural world, not an edifice constructed by so-called worshippers. I pray in the woods, never indoors.
What you call personal hygiene, I call an artificially imposed distraction from natural living.
No forged weapon can replace the sheer joy of a kill accomplished only with hands and teeth.
Time lived alone has made me accustomed to talking loudly to myself, something I still do even when others are present.
{@bold Change.}  As the seasons shift, so too does the world around us. To resist is futile and anathema to the natural order. (Chaotic)
{@bold Conservation.} All life should be preserved and, if needed, protected. (Good)
{@bold Acceptance.} I am a part of my forest, no different from any other flora and fauna. To think otherwise is arrogance and folly. When I die, it will be as a leaf falling in the woods. (Neutral)
{@bold Cull.} The weak must be removed for the strong to thrive. (Evil)
{@bold Candor.} I am open, plain, and simple in life, word, and actions. (Any)
{@bold Balance.} The forest does not lie. The beasts do not create war. Equity in all things is the way of nature. (Neutral)
When I lose a trusted friend or companion, I plant a tree upon their grave.
The voice of the forest guides me, comforts me, and protects me.
The hermit who raised me and taught me the ways of the forest is the most important person in my life.
I have a wooden doll, a tiny wickerman, that I made as a child and carry with me at all times.
I know the ways of civilizations rise and fall. The forest and the Old Ways are eternal.
I am driven to protect the natural order from those that would disrupt it.
I am accustomed to doing what I like when I like. I'm bad at compromising, and I must exert real effort to make even basic conversation with other people.
I won't harm a beast without just cause or provocation.
Years of isolated living has left me blind to the nuances of social interaction. It is a struggle not to view every new encounter through the lens of fight or flight.
The decay after death is merely the loam from which new growth springs—and I enjoy nurturing new growth.
An accident that I caused incurred great damage upon my forest, and, as penance, I have placed myself in self-imposed exile.
I distrust the undead and the unliving, and I refuse to work with them.

entries: You are a creature of the forest, born and reared under a canopy of green. You expected to live all your days in the forest, at one with the green things of the world, until an unforeseen occurrence, traumatic or transformative, drove you from your familiar home and into the larger world. Civilization is strange to you, the open sky unfamiliar, and the bizarre ways of the so-called civilized world run counter to the truths of the natural world.

items.name: Skill Proficiencies
entries: {@skill Nature}, {@skill Stealth}

items.name: Tool Proficiency
entries: {@item Herbalism kit|PHB}

items.name: Distinctive Features
entries: Cunning, Rustic

_.special: an old souvenir from your previous adventuring days

items.name: Equipment:
items.entry: A {@item dagger|PHB}, {@item quarterstaff|PHB}, or {@item shortsword|PHB} (if proficient), an old souvenir from your previous adventuring days, a set of {@item traveler's clothes|PHB}, {@item hempen rope (50 feet)|PHB|50 feet of hempen rope}, and a belt {@item pouch|PHB} containing 15 gp

entries.name: Reason for Retirement
entries: Giving up your first adventuring career was a turning point in your life. Triumph or tragedy, the reason why you gave it up might still haunt you and may shape your actions as you reenter the adventuring life. Choose the event that led you to stop adventuring or roll a {@dice d12} and consult the table below.

rows: Your love perished on one of your adventures, and you quit in despair.
You were the only survivor after an ambush by a hideous beast.
Legal entanglements forced you to quit, and they may cause you trouble again.
A death in the family required you to return home.
Your old group disowned you for some reason.
A fabulous treasure allowed you to have a life of luxury, until the money ran out.
An injury forced you to give up adventuring.
You suffered a curse which doomed your former group, but the curse has finally faded away.
You rescued a young child or creature and promised to care for them. They have since grown up and left.
You couldn't master your fear and fled from a dangerous encounter, never to return.
As a reward for helping an area, you were offered a position with the local authorities, and you accepted.
You killed or defeated your nemesis. Now they are back, and you must finish the job.

entries.name: Feature: Old Friends and Enemies
entries: Your previous career as an adventurer might have been brief or long. Either way, you certainly journeyed far and met people along the way. Some of these acquaintances might remember you fondly for aiding them in their time of need. On the other hand, others may be suspicious, or even hostile, because of your past actions. When you least expect it, or maybe just when you need it, you might encounter someone who knows you from your previous adventuring career. These people work in places high and low, their fortunes varying widely. The individual responds appropriately based on your mutual history, helping or hindering you at the GM's discretion.

entries.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: Former adventurers bring a level of practical experience that fledgling heroes can't match. However, the decisions, outcomes, successes, and failures of your previous career often weigh heavily on your mind. The past seldom remains in the past. How you rise to these new (or old) challenges determines the outcome of your new career.

rows: I have a thousand stories about every aspect of the adventuring life.
My past is my own, and to the pit with anyone who pushes me about it.
I can endure any hardship without complaint.
I have a list of rules for surviving adventures, and I refer to them often.
It's a dangerous job, and I take my pleasures when I can.
I can't help mentioning all the famous friends I've met before.
Anyone who doesn't recognize me is clearly not someone worth knowing.
I've seen it all. If you don't listen to me, you're going to get us all killed.
{@bold Strength.} Experience tells me there are no rules to war. Only victory matters. (Evil)
{@bold Growth.} I strive to improve myself and prove my worth to my companions—and to myself. (Any)
{@bold Thrill.} I am only happy when I am facing danger with my life on the line. (Any)
{@bold Generous.} If I can help someone in danger, I will. (Good)
{@bold Ambition.} I may have lost my renown, but nothing will stop me from reclaiming it. (Chaotic)
{@bold Responsibility.} Any cost to myself is far less than the price of doing nothing. (Lawful)
I will end the monsters who killed my family and pulled me back into the adventuring life.
A disaster made me retire once. Now I will stop it from happening to anyone else.
My old weapon has been my trusted companion for years. It's my lucky charm.
My family doesn't understand why I became an adventurer again, which is why I send them souvenirs, letters, or sketches of exciting encounters in my travels.
I was a famous adventurer once. This time, I will be even more famous, or die trying.
Someone is impersonating me. I will hunt them down and restore my reputation.
It's all about me! Haven't you learned that by now?
I can identify every weapon and item with a look.
You think this is bad? Let me tell you about something really frightening.
Sure, I have old foes around every corner, but who doesn't?
I'm getting too old for this.
Seeing the bad side in everything just protects you from inevitable disappointment.

entries: As you belted on your weapons and hoisted the pack onto your back, you never thought you'd become an adventurer again. But the heroic call couldn't be ignored. You've tried this once before—perhaps it showered you in wealth and glory or perhaps it ended with sorrow and regret. No one ever said adventuring came with a guarantee of success. Now, the time has come to set off toward danger once again. The reasons for picking up adventuring again vary. Could it be a calamitous threat to the town? The region? The world? Was the settled life not what you expected? Or did your past finally catch up to you? In the end, all that matters is diving back into danger. And it's time to show these new folks how it's done.

items.name: Equipment:
items.entry: Choose A or B: (A) {@item Bedroll|xphb}, 5 days of {@item Rations|xphb}, {@item Tinker's Tools|xphb}, {@item Traveler's Clothes|xphb}, {@item Waterskin|xphb}, and 6 GP; or (B) 50 GP

items.name: Equipment:
items.entry: Choose A or B: (A) {@item Dagger|XPHB}, {@item Spear|XPHB}, {@item Gaming Set|XPHB} (same as above), {@item Robe|XPHB}, 10 GP; or (B) 50 GP

entries: Mud, blood, and coin have been your entire life since joining the Company of Free Swords. You may have been recruited from a fighting pit in Unterland, joined as a fugitive to escape justice, or been found as a babe in the mud and raised as a Free Sword. Your history before joining the Company doesn't matter now. Your comrades are your family. Violence is your trade.

The infantry ranks of the Free Swords live by the unspoken rule of Etharis—it's a place where only the strong survive. Your ambitions may stretch only as far as your payment for enduring the next battle. Few expect anything more from you. Yet a hidden ideal may truly drive your actions, or you may hope to lead your own company one day.

_.special: a pirate flag from your ship

items.name: Equipment:
items.entry: A pirate flag from your ship, several tattoos, {@item hempen rope (50 feet)|PHB|50 feet of rope}, a set of {@item traveler's clothes|PHB}, and a belt {@item pouch|PHB} containing 10 gp

entries.name: Feature: A Friendly Face in Every Port
entries: Your reputation precedes you. Whenever you visit a port city, you can always find someone who knows of (or has sailed on) your former ship and is familiar with its captain and crew. They are willing to provide you and your traveling companions with a roof over your head, a bed for the night, and a decent meal. If you have a reputation for cruelty and savagery, your host is probably afraid of you and will be keen for you to leave as soon as possible. Otherwise, you receive a warm welcome, and your host keeps your presence a secret, if needed. They may also provide you with useful information about recent goings-on in the city, including which ships have been in and out of port.

entries.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: Freebooters are a boisterous lot, but their personalities include freedom-loving mavericks and mindless thugs. Nonetheless, sailing a ship requires discipline, and freebooters tend to be reliable and aware of their role on board, even if they do their own thing once fighting breaks out. Most still yearn for the sea, and some feel shame or regret for past deeds.

rows: I'm happiest when I'm on a gently rocking vessel, staring at the distant horizon.
Every time we hoisted the mainsail and raised the pirate flag, I felt butterflies in my stomach.
I have lovers in a dozen different ports. Most of them don't know about the others.
Being a pirate has taught me more swear words and bawdy jokes than I ever knew existed. I like to try them out when I meet new people.
One day I hope to have enough gold to fill a tub so I can bathe in it.
There's nothing I enjoy more than a good scrap — the bloodier, the better.
When a storm is blowing and the rain is lashing the deck, I'll be out there getting drenched. It makes me feel so alive!
Nothing makes me more annoyed than a badly tied knot.
{@bold Freedom.} No one tells me what to do or where to go. Apart from the captain. (Chaotic)
{@bold Greed.} I'm only in it for the booty. I'll gladly stab anyone stupid enough to stand in my way. (Evil)
{@bold Comradery.} My former shipmates are my family. I'll do anything for them. (Neutral)
{@bold Greater Good.} No man has the right to enslave another, or to profit from slavery. (Good)
{@bold Code.} I may be on dry land now, but I still stick to the Freebooter's Code. (Lawful)
{@bold Aspiration.} One day I'll return to the sea as the captain of my own ship. (Any)
Anti-slavery pirates rescued me from a slave ship. I owe them my life.
I still feel a deep attachment to my ship. Some nights I dream her figurehead is talking to me.
I was the ship's captain until the crew mutinied and threw me overboard to feed the sharks. I swam to a small island and survived. Vengeance will be mine!

Years ago, when my city was attacked, I fled the city on a small fleet bound for a neighboring city. I arrived back in the ruined city a few weeks ago on the same ship and can remember nothing of the voyage.
I fell asleep when I was supposed to be on watch, allowing our ship to be taken by surprise. I still have nightmares about my shipmates who died in the fighting.
One of my shipmates was captured and sold into slavery. I need to rescue them.
I'm terrified by the desert. Not enough water, far too much sand.
I drink too much and end up starting barroom brawls.
I killed one of my shipmates and took his share of the loot.
I take unnecessary risks and often put my friends in danger.
I sold captives taken at sea to traders.
Most of the time, I find it impossible to tell the truth.

entries: You sailed the seas as a freebooter, part of a pirate crew. You should come up with a name for your former ship and its captain, as well as its hunting ground and the type of ships you preyed on. Did you sail under the flag of a bloodthirsty captain, raiding coastal communities and putting everyone to the sword? Or were you part of a group of former slaves turned pirates, who battle to end the vile slave trade? Whatever ship you sailed on, you feel at home on board a seafaring vessel, and you have difficulty adjusting to long periods on dry land.

items.name: Skill Proficiencies
items.entry: Choose two from among {@skill Deception}, {@skill Intimidation}, {@skill Investigation}, {@skill Perception}, {@skill Persuasion}, {@skill Stealth}

items.name: Tool Proficiencies
items.entry: One vehicle proficiency or {@item hacking tools|TTT}

items.name: Equipment
items.entry: A set of common clothes, a smartphone, a trophy from a previous job, and a credit stick with 2000 credits.

entries.name: Feature: Freelancer Specialty
entries: For one reason or another, people tend to avoid doing the kind of work that you specialize in. Perhaps they think that it's too dangerous, or too difficult, or maybe they think they're above getting their hands dirty, but that doesn't stop them from hiring an expert to do it instead. Choose your specialization as a freelancer, or roll on the table below.

rows: Assassin
Bodyguard
Burglar
Fixer
Mercenary
Saboteur
Smuggler
Spy

entries.name: Feature: Criminal Element
entries: You're familiar with various black markets, able to find potential fixers who can hook you up with jobs. However, it isn't guaranteed that the jobs are good and the clients are trustworthy. You are also familiar with other freelancers, able to identify the names and specialties of any given freelancer with at least a little bit of history in the scene.

entries.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: The kind of work a freelancer performs shapes their personality and attitudes. The constant threat of danger, and the illegal and potentially bloody nature of the work, shapes a freelancers mind, or breaks it.

rows: I can fall into a group and make friends quickly. After all, they can disappear at any time.
I don't feel good about something unless I plan it out first.
People think I'm cold, but it's really just that things cease to surprise or excite me anymore.
I'm an expert at my work, and I take pride in it.
Danger makes me feel alive, it's addictive.
I spend entirely too much energy making sure my family never learns what I do for a living.
I work hard and play harder.
We're all just disposable tools to be used, broken, and then thrown away.
I won't take on a job I morally disagree with, no matter the pay. (Good)
A deal's a deal, and I won't go back on my word. (Lawful)
Boring jobs are the worst, I won't bother unless there's a risk of it blowing up in my face. (Chaotic)
I like it neat and tidy, no matter how many loose ends I need to cut. (Evil)
I'm not paid to care about the consequences of my actions. (Neutral)
I'll find a good team and work my way to the top, until everyone knows our names. (Any)
I thought I'd lost my whole team, and nearly died myself, but I heard a rumor that they just finished a big job.
When a job went downhill, I was rescued by an unexpected benefactor, who I owe a favor.
It was just your average job... at least until I fell in love with the target.
I've gained a reputation as a cold-blooded, murderous psychopath after my last job. Just one problem: it wasn't me.
I want to retire, but it's not just about the money. There's too many strings on me.
If I can pull off this major job, I'll be a legend.
I tend to get antsy and nervous under pressure.
When things look bad, I'm the first to bail out.
I spend all my money on weapons, gear, and cybernetics, even if it means going hungry and homeless.
I hate that my work is slowly grinding away the last of traces of my compassion and goodwill.
After being betrayed a few times, I tend to assume the worst of people.
I'd like to take charge in some situations, but I know I'm just going to screw it up.

entries: Do you have a scumbag that needs killing? A vault that needs cracking? Illegal product that needs moving? Bodies that need guarding? There are numerous specialists looking for work on a contractual or contingent basis, often without the more official aspects of work, like documentation or benefits. They go by many names: freelancers, mercenaries, consultants, and other, less reputable titles.

Freelancers can find work by many means. A smart freelancer will have fixers looking to setup jobs for a small cut, while others may have to advertise their services on digital or physical black markets. It can be dirty, dehumanizing, and often dangerous work, but someone has to do it. Well, maybe some of the crimes you've committed didn't have to be done, but you gotta make a living somehow.

items.name: Equipment:
items.entry: Choose A or B: (A) {@item Binoculars|DarkMatter24}, {@item Flashlight|DarkMatter24}, {@item Traveler's Clothes|XPHB} (duster), {@item Utility Axe|DarkMatter24}, 18 CR; or (B) 50 CR

entries: You hail from the Galactic Frontier, the utter edge of the 'Verse where the planets are lawless, the people are tough, and help is usually a thousand lightyears away. On your homeworld, you might have lived off the land, operated a trading post, or practiced an essential trade for the people of your colony. You have almost experienced hardship, either at the hands of others or from the indiscriminate malice of alien beings. Yet you've survived all the same, with stories and tenacity to spare.

items.name: Tool Proficiencies:
items.entry: Choose one kind of {@item Gaming Set|XPHB}

items.name: Equipment:
items.entry: {@item Gaming Set|XPHB} (same as above), a lucky charm, a set of {@item fine clothes|phb}, and a belt {@item pouch|phb} containing 15 gp; or (B) 50 GP

entries.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: All you need to make a lot of gold is a little gold, except when you have no gold. Whether you're a good gambler or a bad one rarely matters, as few can predict the divine whims of Lady Luck. Sometimes you're up and sometimes you're down, but you always know that someone, somewhere, is always willing to take a bet.

Some gamble out of necessity. Others do so out of boredom. Still others become addicted to the thrill of uncertainty. Even the best gamblers are one hand away from financial ruin, and the worst gamblers are one wager away from untold fortunes. As a gambler, you are blessed by Lady Luck with an inherent need to bet, wager, and take the occasional foolhardy risk.

rows: Lady Luck whispered in my ear the first time I rolled the dice, and I've been chasing her ever since.
I grew up with nothing, and the allure of turning rags into riches was too tempting to resist.
I once bet everything on a single game—and won. Ever since, I've believed the odds are always in my favor.
The rush of outsmarting opponents and taking risks makes me feel more alive than anything else.
A fortune-teller told me that luck would guide my destiny, and gambling seemed the best way to test it.
I learned to gamble to survive, turning every coin and every game into a chance to eat another meal.
I plan for every contingency. Leave nothing to chance!
Every copper wants to be a silver. Each bet is an opportunity.
I'm one of Lady Luck's favored. Anything I try is destined to succeed.
I've lost so much to gambling that I refuse to spend money on anything anymore.
Nothing is certain. Planning is a coward's act.
I can't be sure who I've swindled, cheated, or defeated, so I keep a low profile in public.
The perfect bet is out there somewhere. I just have to keep my eyes open.
I have beaten my addiction, but all it takes is one weak moment and I'll be back at the card table.
Knowledge. Knowledge is power, and knowing which horse to back is the key to success. (Any)
Fate. Whatever happens is fated, regardless of any planning or striving. (Lawful)
Bravery. If you want to succeed, you have to take risks. (Chaotic)
Survival. You can't win if you're dead. Live to fight another day—when the odds might be more in your favor. (Any)
Reliability. When I was in need, I was able to rely on others. Now I want to be the one others rely on. (Good)
Victory. Winning is the real measure of a person. In the end, the only thing that matters is the scoreboard. (Evil)
One person in particular owes me a lot of money, and I need to keep them alive if I want to be repaid.
I'm loyal to the friend or family member who taught me how to gamble.
The person who saved me from my gambling addiction is the only reason I'm alive today.
A patron once fronted me money in exchange for a percentage of my winnings. I owe them a debt of gratitude. And a lot of cash.
A criminal syndicate I once played for isn't happy I left the game, and its enforcers are looking for me.
Urchins once helped me find marks for my games. Now I'm driven to help them escape the streets.
I don't know when to quit. Especially when everyone else is telling me to.
I save my sympathy for my friends, and I have no friends.
You think we're in trouble now? Let me tell you how bad things are likely to get!
You can loan me a little, right? I've got a sure thing. I'll double your money, guaranteed.
I was once a terribly flawed person, like you. Let me tell you how you can save yourself.
I'm a great gambler. I'm just bad at math and logic.

items.name: Equipment:
items.entry: A set of {@item leatherworker's tools|PHB}, a {@item hunting trap|PHB}, {@item fishing tackle|PHB}, a set of {@item traveler's clothes|PHB}, and a belt {@item pouch|PHB} containing 10 gp

entries.name: Feature: Confirmed Guildmember
entries: As a recognized member of the Gamekeepers' Guild, you are knowledgeable in the care, training, and habits of animals used for hunting. With 30 days' of work and at least 2 gp for each day, you can train a raptor, such as a hawk, falcon, or owl, or a hunting dog, such as a hound, terrier, or cur, to become a hunting companion. Use the statistics of an {@creature owl|MM} for the raptor and the statistics of a {@creature jackal|MM} for the hunting dog.

A hunting companion is trained to obey and respond to a series of one-word commands or signals, communicating basic concepts such as "attack," "protect," "retrieve," "find," "hide," or similar. The companion can know up to six such commands and can be trained to obey a number of creatures, other than you, equal to your proficiency bonus. A hunting companion travels with you wherever you go, unless you enter a particularly dangerous environment (such as a poisonous swamp), or you command the companion to stay elsewhere. A hunting companion doesn't join you in combat and stays on the edge of any conflict until it is safe to return to your side.

When traveling overland with a hunting companion, you can use the companion to find sufficient food to sustain yourself and up to five other people each day. You can have only one hunting companion at a time.

entries.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: You are one of the capable people who maintains hunting preserves, trains coursing hounds and circling raptors, and plans the safe outings that allow fair nobles, rich merchants, visiting dignitaries, and their entourages to venture into preserves and forests to seek their quarry. You are as comfortable hunting quarry in the forest as you are conversing with members of the elite who have an interest in hunting.

rows: Nature has lessons to teach us all, and I'm always happy to share them.
Once while out on a hunt, something happened which was very relatable to our current situation. Let me tell you about it.
My friends are my new charges, and I'll make sure they thrive.
Preparation and knowledge are the key to any success.
I've dealt with all sorts of wealthy and noble folk, and I've seen just how spoiled they can be.
I feel like my animals are the only ones who really understand me.
You can train yourself to accomplish anything you put your mind to accomplishing.
The world shows you everything you need to know to understand a situation. You just have to be paying attention to the details.
{@bold Dedication.} Your willingness to get the job done, no matter what the cost, is what is most important. (Evil)
{@bold Training.} You sink to the level of your training more often than you rise to the occasion. (Any)
{@bold Prestige.} Pride in your training, your work, and your results is what is best in life. (Any)
{@bold Diligent.} Hard work and attention to detail bring success more often than failure. (Good)
{@bold Nature.} The glory and majesty of the wild world outshine anything mortals create. (Chaotic)
{@bold Responsibility.} When you take an oath to protect and shepherd something, that oath is for life. (Lawful)
I understand animals better than people, and the way of the hunter just makes sense.
I take great pride in providing my services to the wealthy and influential.
Natural spaces need to be tended and preserved, and I take joy in doing it when I can.
I need to ensure people know how to manage nature rather than live in ignorance.
Laws are important to prevent nature's overexploitation.
I can be alone in the wilderness and not feel lonely.
Individuals can be all right, but civilization is the worst.
The wealthy and nobility are a rot in society.
Things die, either by predators or nature; get used to it.
Everything can be managed if you want it badly enough.
When you make exceptions, you allow unworthy or wasteful things to survive.
If you don't work hard for something, is it worth anything?

entries: You are at home in natural environments, chasing prey or directing less skilled hunters in the best ways to track game through the brush. You know the requirements for encouraging a herd to grow, and you know what sustainable harvesting from a herd involves. You can train a hunting beast to recognize an owner and perform a half-dozen commands, given the time. You also know the etiquette for engaging nobility or other members of the upper classes, as they regularly seek your services, and you can carry yourself in a professional manner in such social circles.

items.name: Tool Proficiencies
items.entry: One from among vehicles (land) or vehicles (water)

items.name: Equipment
items.entry: A set of common or fine clothes, a pistol, a dose of a common drug of your choice, a token from your gang, and a credit stick with 1000 credits.

entries.name: Feature: Scum Sticks Together
entries: When it comes to violent thugs and criminals, you feel right at home. You know the lingo, slang, and signs that lets you speak to the members of street gangs. They will recognize you, and have some amount of respect for you, though enemy gang members may still be hostile. Additionally, you can find someplace to buy a stolen vehicle on short notice.

entries.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: Whatever hard-knock life leads a person to join a gang, it probably isn't idyllic. Gangsters often put up a tough, intimidating front, which may or may not be feigned for appearances. They may not want to be a gangster, and could be looking for a way out. Unfortunately, most gangs tend to have unresolved abandonment issues.

rows: I'm loud and rowdy, and I know how to have a good time.
It's more satisfying to take something than to earn it.
I always look for the biggest, toughest motherfucker in the room and size them up.
My silent glare chills people to the bone.
I won't let shitheads fuck with me or mine.
I look rough, but I'm friendly to people who deserve it.
I feel alive when I'm riding something fast.
There are winners and losers, and I am a loser.
{@bold Guardian.} My community needs protection, and I'm willing to stand up for them. (Good)
{@bold Enforcer.} So long as nobody crosses the line, nobody needs to get fucked up. (Lawful)
{@bold Psycho.} It isn't a party until something gets lit on fire. (Chaotic)
{@bold Bastard.} I don't need a reason to break people. (Evil)
{@bold Survivor.} I didn't choose this life, but I'll make the best of it. (Neutral)
{@bold Chieftain.} I'll lead the gang to be the biggest, baddest motherfuckers around. (Any)
My gang got destroyed by a rival gang, and now I want revenge.
If I can scrape together enough money, I can finally find a way out of this life.
My gang will claim the most turf, and we'll go down as legends.
Bashing goon skulls just isn't enough anymore, I need a bigger challenge.
My family have lived in a shithole community for long enough, it's time that changed.
I would follow my gang leader to the grave, if they hadn't disappeared.
I'm unreliable, and responsibility scares me.
I drive recklessly and endanger others.
When I get stressed, I need to break a few bones to calm down.
I blow my money on sex and drugs.
I live in constant fear that the things I've done will catch up with me.
People insult me all the time, whether they mean to or not.

entries: The streets of the slums are stained with blood, night after night. The cycle of violence grinds down the local populace with endless turf wars, blood feuds, and revenge hits. Sometimes the only way to survive is to be tougher and meaner than you thought you ever could be. You have survived, or perhaps even thrived under these savage conditions.

For people without family, friends, or hope, a gang can come to take their place. It's a swift transition from you being recruited into a gang and taught their ways, to you recruiting others and brutally upholding the gang's code. While you might not have a long life expectancy, there's nothing quite like riding a motorcycle down a road at full speed with your gang at your back.

items.name: Tool Proficiencies:
items.entry: {@item Thieves' tools|phb}, one type of {@filter musical instrument|items|source=phb|miscellaneous=mundane|type=instrument}

items.name: Equipment:
items.entry: A battered alms box, a {@filter musical instrument|items|source=phb|miscellaneous=mundane|type=instrument}, a cast-off military jacket, cap, or scarf, a set of {@item common clothes|phb}, a belt {@item pouch|phb}, and 10 gp

entries.name: Lifestyle
entries: Poor

entries.name: Overview
entries: All traffic into and out of the City of Trade passes through the Hillsfar Gate, making it the ideal place for the destitute to gather to panhandle, busk, gossip, and pick pockets. You grew up on the streets in the shadow of that great steel edifice, which houses both Red Plumes and Guild Mages. Though you may have moved on, you still have friends among them, and that life has had a lasting impact on you.

entries.name: Feature: Red Plume and Mage Guild Contacts
entries: You made a number of friends among the Red Plumes and the Mage's Guild when you lived at the Hillsfar Gate. They remember you fondly and help you in little ways when they can. You can invoke their assistance in and around Hillsfar to obtain food, as well as simple equipment for temporary use. You can also invoke it to gain access to the low-security areas of their garrisons, halls, and encampments. Note: This feature is a variant of the Soldier feature.

rows: I appreciate the simple things in life. a song, a warm meal, a sunny day. I don't need any more.
My problems are always caused by others. I'm never to blame.
I am afraid I could wind up back on the streets any day.
I get along with everyone.
I see people as marks for a con and have difficulty feeling true empathy for them.
I have a real flair for matchmaking. I can find anyone a spouse!
I think money is the true measure of appreciation and affection. Everything else is talk or an act.
I don't like having a lot of stuff, just a few simple things I need. I don't like being tied down and tend to leave things behind when I don't need them anymore.
Loyal. I never rat out any of my friends, even when the Red Plumes or the Rogues Guild ask. (Lawful)
Adventurous. I don't like doing the same thing every day. I crave variety. (Chaotic)
Strong. Only the strong survive. I respect those who are strong and powerful. (Any)
Witty. Brains are better than brawn. I rely on my wits and respect others who do the same. (Any)
Honest. Others can do what they want, but I won't lie or steal, even to feed my family. (Good)
Ungrateful. Those who give, only do it to make themselves feel better. I steal from them. (Evil)
The Joydancers of Lliira gave me my instrument when I really needed food. I hate them for that.
Busking has taught me to love music above all else.
The Rogues Guild spared me when I did a job without cutting them in. I owe them a great debt.
I know people hate the Red Plumes, but some of them were really good to me. I help Red Plumes whenever I can, and I respect them. They're just doing what they have to do to get by in this world.
I will be wealthy some day. My descendants will live in comfort and style.
I know how hard life on the streets is. I do everything I can for those who have less than me.
Though I no longer live at the Gate, I am still always concerned about where I will get my next meal.
Years of thieving have become habit. I sometimes steal from strangers without thinking about it.
I am ashamed of my origins. I pretend I am higher-born and fear others will find out the truth.
I think people who grew up in houses are soft, spoiled, and ungrateful. I frequently tell them so.
I am still very uncomfortable wearing nice clothes, sleeping in a warm bed, and eating fine food.
I do not trust anyone who has not had a hard life.

entries: {@skill Intimidation}, {@skill Perception}

items.name: Tool Proficiency
entries: {@item Carpenter's tools|PHB} or {@item woodcarver's tools|PHB}

items.name: Distinctive Features
entries: Inquisitive, Patient

_.special: set of tools you're proficient in
metal bracelet identifying you as a geas'd conscript that cannot be removed until the end of your sentence

items.name: Skill Proficiencies
items.entry: Choose any two from {@skill Athletics}, {@skill Deception}, {@skill Insight}, {@skill Perception} and {@skill Survival}.

items.name: Tool Proficiencies
items.entry: Your choice of one artisan�s tools related to the kind of work you did in Solace as part of your geas.

items.name: Equipment
items.entry: One set of tools you're proficient in, a 10-foot pole, an official writ detailing your sentence, a metal bracelet identifying you as a geas'd conscript that cannot be removed until the end of your sentence, common clothes, pouch, 5 gp.

entries.name: Overview
entries: Convicted of a crime in Solace, you have been sentenced to dedicate a year of your life to bettering the city and improving the lives of its citizens. This punishment was imposed through the geas spell, and may have initially taken the form of either manual or martial labor, depending on your character�s talents, skills, and experience. Were you assigned to a batallion along the outer walls, defending the city from Maelstrom-born horrors alongside the Wardens? Or did you work as part of a clean-up crew duty in the Dead Ward, rebuild damaged city buildings, or some other type of duties? At this point, you�ve been reassigned to finish out the rest of your sentence in the frontier as a conscript adventurer. Was this something you had to fight for, or yet another unwanted burden imposed by city officials? What was your crime? And how much time is left on your geas? What are your plans for when your life is your own again?

entries.name: Feature: The Invisible Ones
entries: You are familiar with how the dirty parts of Solace's city infrastructure works, and as soon as people notice the bracelet on your arm, that's all they really see. As a result, you can easily gain access to the city's low- to mid-level-security military fortifications, as well as sites where city work crews are common, such as the Dead Ward and various government facilities. What's more, other geas'd conscripts are inclined to commiserate. If you spend at least 10 minutes in friendly conversation with a geas'd conscript NPC, they tend to be inclined to help you out, though not necessarily to stick their own neck out for you.

name: Geologist

_.special: a reinforced backpack that increases your carry weight by 20 lb.

items.name: Tool Proficiencies
items.entry: Mason's tools, Cartographer's tools, Excavator's Tools, and Analysis Tools

items.name: Equipment
items.entry: A shovel, a miner's pick, a hammer and chisel, a reinforced backpack that increases your carry weight by 20 lb., gemstones worth 25 gp, and an additional 10 gp in coins

entries: Geologists are those who have dedicated a portion of their lives to the study of rocks and earthly processes. They are able to see beyond the immediately obvious and interpret the landscape around them, providing valuable field knowledge.

entries.name: Feature: Eye for Faults
entries: Years of studying geology allows you to easily select weak points in rock, allowing you to break it and tunnel with ease. You have a tunnelling speed of 5 ft.

entries.name: Feature: Rock Knowledge
entries: You can identify any rocks or gemstones at a glance, and know their value.

entries.name: Rock Specialism
entries: Your previous work as a geologist has given you a type of rock that you're particularly passionate about. Roll a {@dice d8} and consult the table below or choose whichever you find most appealing.

rows: Fluvial
You love the sediments of rivers and streams and relish the opportunity to spend time wading in them. You're aware of the dangers of flooding.
Volcanic
The dramatic power of volcanoes excites you. You love to explore volcanic settings, but are wary of their dangers.
Calcareous
You love delving into natural caves, particularly those hollowed out by groundwater, but are very observant of potential cave-ins.
Shale
Deepwater sediments are your speciality. You jump at the opportunity to deep-dive into water, particularly in the ocean, and are a great swimmer.
Plutonic
You greatly enjoy walking on rolling hills, moors, and tors, and will favour taking longer routes if they take you over this terrain.
Metamorphic
You are particularly excited by sharp jagged metamorphosed rocks and can navigate them with ease.
Seams
You have a fixation on rare minerals and gemstones that can be found within rich rock seams. You will go out of your way to acquire rare gemstones.
Orogenous
You love mountains and mountain-climbing, and are very good at it. You always want to climb to the very top, if you can.

entries.name: Suggested Starting Feat and Ability Scores
entries: If you use your background to determine your ability score increases and provide a starting feat, we recommend the following:

items: {@bold Feat:} {@feat Tough} or {@feat Miner|DrDhrolinsDictionaryofDinosaurs}.
{@bold Ability Scores:} +2 Constitution or Strength, +1 Intelligence.

entries.name: Suggested Tools
entries: {@bold Excavator's Tools:} {@i Common, 5 gp, 8 lb.} These tools are used to carefully extract fossils or minerals from rock/mud/dirt. They cause your harvested gemstones to be 10% more valuable and harvested fossils to be 100% more valuable.

{@bold Analysis Tools:} {@i Common, 10 gp, 1 lb.} These tools provide a +2 to any skill check where you are examining an object small enough to fit into your hand, regardless of the skill you are using.

entries.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: Geologists come in many varieties. Below are some suggestions for traits, ideals, bonds, and flaws that a geologist may have.

entries.caption: Personality Traits
rows: Exploration is everything, I have to get out there and find new things.
I fancy myself as an adventurer, but I'm not as surefooted as I think I am.
I'm more of a bookworm, reading about other people's work and adventures.
Given the option between taking a tunnel and climbing a mountain, I'll always take the tunnel!
If it's in the ground, it's anyone's fair game!
I find anything geology related interesting and pick up little rocks everywhere I go.
I don't like clean-nosed, stuck-up scientists of other fields.
We dig rocks, then we drink lots!

entries.caption: Ideals
rows: I'm an academic at heart, I want to know everything there is about the deep past.
I'm a naturalist at heart. Look at the beauty of our world – isn't it remarkable?!
I love spelunking. There're treasures beyond measure down in the depths.
I only work as a contractor. I've got to get the job done, everything else is secondary.
I'm on the run as a lawbreaker. They'll never find me if I'm deep underground.
I'm going to find the riches of a lifetime – there's gold in them-there mountains, I can feel it.

entries.caption: Bonds
rows: My parent was a famous geologist – I'm following in their footsteps.
Our world is sacred, both in the present and past.
My mentor expects big things from me, I don't want to disappoint.
I want to see firsthand the most impressive geological events – eruptions, earthquakes, and landslides!
If I can find the biggest, most precious gem, perhaps I can finally impress the person of my dreams.
The ancient past has mesmerised me, ever since I was a child.

entries.caption: Flaws
rows: I can only sleep in total darkness, usually with my head buried under something.
I can't resist expensive gemstones. They must be mine!
I get overly obsessed with tunnelling, always wanting to dig deeper.
I'm surprisingly destructive – getting to the rocks is what matters, things in the way be damned!
I have no regard for the laws of the land when it comes to my research.
My only loyalty is to whoever is paying me for my work.
