items.entry: A set of either {@item brewer's supplies|PHB} or {@item cook's utensils|PHB}, a {@item dagger|PHB} or {@item light hammer|PHB}, {@item traveler's clothes|PHB}, and a {@item pouch|PHB} containing 20 gp

entries.name: Place of Employment
entries: Where did you work before turning to the adventuring life? Choose an establishment or roll a {@dice d6} and consult the table below. Once you have this information, think about who worked with you, what sort of customers you served, and what sort of reputation your establishment had.

rows: Busy crossroads inn
Disreputable tavern full of scum and villainy
Caravanserai on a wide-ranging trade route
Rough seaside pub
Hostel serving only the wealthiest clientele
Saloon catering to expensive and sometimes dangerous tastes

entries.name: Feature: I Know Someone
entries: In interacting with the wide variety of people who graced the tables and bars of your previous life, you gained an excellent knowledge of who might be able to perform a particular task, provide the right service, sell the perfect item, or be able to connect you with someone who can. You can spend a couple of hours in a town or city and identify a person or place of business capable of selling the product or service you seek, provided the product is nonmagical and isn't worth more than 250 gp. At the GM's discretion, these restrictions can be lifted in certain locations. The price might not always be what you hoped, the quality might not necessarily be the best, or the person's demeanor may be grating, but you can find the product or service. In addition, you know within the first hour if the product or service you desire doesn't exist in the community, such as a cold-weather outfit in a tropical fishing village.

entries.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: The day-to-day operation of a tavern or inn teaches many lessons about people and how they interact. The nose for trouble, the keen eye on the kegs, and the ready hand on a truncheon translates well to the life of an adventurer.

rows: I insist on doing all the cooking, and I plan strategies like I cook — with proper measurements and all the right ingredients.
Lending a sympathetic ear or a shoulder to cry on often yields unexpected benefits.
I always have a story or tale to relate to any situation.
There is a world of tastes and flavors to explore.
Few problems can't be solved with judicious application of a stout cudgel.
I never pass up the chance to bargain. Never.
I demand the finest accommodations; I know what they're worth.
I can defuse a situation with a joke, cutting remark, or arched eyebrow.
{@bold Service.} If we serve others, they will serve us in turn. (Lawful)
{@bold Perspective.} People will tell you a great deal about themselves, their situations, and their desires, if you listen. (Any)
{@bold Determination.} Giving up is not in my nature. (Any)
{@bold Charity.} I try to have extra coins to buy a meal for someone in need. (Good)
{@bold Curiosity.} Staying safe never allows you to see the wonders of the world. (Chaotic)
{@bold Selfish.} We must make sure we bargain for what our skills are worth; people don't value what you give away for free. (Evil)
I started my career in a tavern, and I'll end it running one of my very own.
I try to ensure stories of my companions will live on forever.
You want to take the measure of a person? Have a meal or drink with them.
I've seen the dregs of life pass through my door, and I will never end up like them.
A mysterious foe burned down my inn, and I will have my revenge.
One day, I want my story to be sung in all the taverns of my home city.
I can't help teasing or criticizing those less intelligent than I.
I love rich food and drink, and I never miss a chance at a good meal.
I never trust anyone who won't drink with me.
I hate it when people start fights in bars; they never consider the consequences.
I can't stand to see someone go hungry or sleep in the cold if I can help it.
I am quick to anger if anyone doesn't like my meals or brews. If you don't like it, do it yourself.

entries: You spent some time as an innkeeper, tavern keeper, or perhaps a bartender. It might have been in a small crossroads town, a fishing community, a fine caravanserai, or a large cosmopolitan community. You did it all; preparing food, tracking supplies, tapping kegs, and everything in between. All the while, you listened to the adventurers plan their quests, heard their tales, saw their amazing trophies, marveled at their terrible scars, and eyed their full purses. You watched them come and go, thinking, "one day, I will have my chance." Your time is now.

items.name: Equipment:
items.entry: Choose A or B: (A) {@item Book|XPHB} (prayer), {@item Holy Symbol|XPHB}, {@item Manacles|XPHB}, {@item Traveler's Clothes|XPHB}, {@item Torture Tools|SGEHPP}, and 10 GP; or (B) 50 GP

_.displayName: holy symbol of the Radiant Church
tome containing the teachings of the Radiant Church

items.name: Languages:
items.entry: {@language Common}, one of your choice between {@language Deep Speech} and {@language Primordial}, often used in your investigations or dealing with outsiders.

items.name: Equipment:
items.entry: A {@item holy symbol|phb} of the Radiant Church, a set of {@item common clothes|phb}, a set of {@item manacles|PHB}, {@item torture tools|SGttEH}, a {@item book|PHB|tome} containing the teachings of the Radiant Church, and a {@item pouch|phb} containing 10 gp

entries.name: Feature: Zealous Authority
entries: As an Inquisitor of the Radiant Church, you command a certain level of respect and fear among church members and outsiders who recognize the authority of the Church. You can leverage your authority to gain access to resources, information, or aid from those who fear the Church's wrath, revere its power, or follow its teachings.

entries.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: Your place within the Radiant Church is unique and carries with it heavy responsibilities. The pursuit of truth and the maintenance of the Church's authority guide your actions, though the means you use to achieve these ends can be unsavory.

entries.caption: Personality Traits
rows: I am fervently dedicated to my faith and the teachings of the Radiant Church.
I am often suspicious of others, especially those who do not share my beliefs.
I am stern and serious, with little time for humor or frivolity.
I am not easily swayed by emotional appeals, preferring to deal in facts and evidence.
I am meticulous and thorough in my investigations, leaving no stone unturned.
I believe that the ends justify the means when it comes to preserving the Church and its teachings.
I tend to view things in black and white, with little room for moral ambiguity.
Despite my stern exterior, I am deeply compassionate and driven by a desire to protect the innocent.

entries.caption: Ideals
rows: {@b Faith}. My faith in the Radiant Church is unwavering, and I will do whatever it takes to protect it. (Any)
{@b Order}. The laws and teachings of the Church must be upheld at all times. (Lawful)
{@b Purity}. Corruption and heresy will be purged (Lawful)
{@b Justice}. Those who harm or deceive the Church must be brought to justice. (Lawful)
{@b Power}. The Church's authority must be respected and feared. I will ensure it. (Evil)
{@b Sacrifice}. I am willing to sacrifice anything, even my life, for the Church. (Good)

entries.caption: Bonds
rows: I am loyal to a mentor or superior within the Church who has guided me on my path.
I once failed to stop a heretic, and that failure haunts me.
I have a family member or loved one who doesn't understand my dedication to the Church.
I am seeking to bring a particular heretic or enemy of the Church to justice.
The Church is my family, and I will protect it at all costs.
I seek to convert or save those who have strayed from the path.
I have killed innocents in my righteous crusade, and their screams still haunt me.
I have killed innocents in my righteous crusade, and will do so again if it is necessary.

entries.caption: Flaws
rows: My zealous devotion to the Church can make me blind to its flaws.
I am unforgiving and tend to hold grudges, especially against perceived heretics.
I can be overly suspicious, seeing threats to the Church where there are none.
I am rigid and inflexible, struggling to adapt when things don't go according to plan.
My stern demeanor often drives people away.
I sometimes resort to extreme measures in the name of preserving the Church, which can lead to unnecessary conflict.

items.name: Equipment:
items.entry: Choose A or B: (A) {@item Book|XPHB} (prayer), {@item Holy Symbol|XPHB}, {@item Manacles|XPHB}, {@item Torture Tools|sgtteh24}, {@item Traveler's Clothes|XPHB}, 3 GP; or (B) 50 GP

items.name: Equipment:
items.entry: Choose A or B: (A) {@item Club|XPHB}, {@item Navigator's Tools|XPHB}, Book Containing Holy Rites, {@item Holy Symbol|XPHB}, Interrogator's Tools, {@item Manacles|XPHB}, {@item Traveler's Clothes|XPHB}, 10 GP; or (B) 50 GP

entries: You are a servant of the Watchers of the Faithful, hunting down heretics and blasphemers within your own faith, cultists of sinister powers, or other threats to your divine order.
Divine justice does not discriminate, and you have mercilessly punished crimes both mundane and supernatural—tasks that leave scars both on body and soul.

You travel far and wide in your role, spreading the rumors of the sinful and the deviant take you. Corruption is just as likely to fester within as without, so you must be ever watchful of those who travel with you. Those found guilty, wherever they hail from and for whatever their reason, must be faced without mercy.

_.special: a wand with white paper streamers

items.name: Tool Proficiencies
items.entry: One type of {@item artisan's tools|PHB}, one type of {@item musical instrument|PHB}

items.name: Equipment
items.entry: A {@item musical instrument|PHB} (one of your choice), a {@item wand|PHB} with white paper streamers, a bottle of rice wine, vestments, a set of {@item common clothes|PHB}, and a belt pouch containing 5 gp.

entries.name: Feature: Kakuriyo Connection
entries: Your mannerisms and knowledge of kami customs are recognized by natives of the Kakuriyo, who see you as one of their own. Because of this, friendly kami spirits are inclined to come to your aid if you need help near a merge gate or shrine.

You stand in the gap between Kakuriyo and Utsushiyo, understanding both worlds. Perhaps you are an official Imperial Intercessor, or perhaps you are a Jukai Merge Keeper or even Saiba researcher, using your knowledge of kami to preserve the spirit world or to profit from it.

items.name: Equipment
items.entry: A phrasebook, identification documents, a small recording device, a set of {@item fine clothes|PHB}, and a pouch containing 10 gp

entries.name: Feature: Flawless Protocol
entries: You have memorized a vast library of basic greetings, handshaking techniques and polite gestures from a thousand different cultures. You almost always know the correct way to address unusual aliens or foreign dignitaries and can even make some educated guesses, good enough to avoid giving offense, when it comes to strange or uncontacted peoples.

entries.name: Role
entries: You could have worked in several different environments as an interpreter. Choose one or roll on the table below.

entries.caption: Ship Names
rows: Diplomatic aide
Maw station staff
Personal assistant
Protocol servitor
Interplanetary legal counsel
Document translator
Historian/antiquarian/scholar of linguistics
Naval communications officer

entries.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: Of all the people of the galaxy, very few spend more time around people than interpreters. Consequently, they tend to possess extremely refined social skills and personalities that revolve around people and relationships.

rows: I sometimes switch language mid-sentence without noticing.
I love to gossip.
Hand-written letters are my preferred means of communication.
I use long, complicated words that few people understand.
I get bored quickly when I'm on my own.
I have a fondness for puns and wordplay.
I enjoy learning about other cultures.
My typing speed is incredible.
Accuracy. I aim to be precise and clear in everything I do. (Lawful)
Neutrality. The principles of neutrality and non- interference are critical to me. (Neutral)
Diplomacy. Nothing makes me happier than brokering peace by helping people to understand one another better. (Good)
Friendship. My closest pals are always my highest priority. (Any)
Manipulation. I seek to pull on strings behind the scenes, for my own benefit. (Evil)
Comedy. I live to tell jokes and play tricks on people! (Chaotic)
I am gradually translating a massive, multi-volume work from a distant planet.
I am on a quest to find the last living speaker of an ancient language, so that it can be preserved.
I have a friend on every maw.
I did some interpreting for a famous person, and made contacts in high places.
I have been asked to act as a go-between by two warring factions.
I will do whatever my guildmaster asks.
I can't keep my big mouth shut, even about important secrets.
I get anxious if I spend too much time alone.
I am a compulsive liar.
I am often too passive and slow to take action.
I am practically innumerate.
Powerful people are out to get me.

entries: In a galaxy with hundreds of systems, thousands of worlds, and a vast array of cultures, communication is a constant challenge. On the civilized worlds, maws, and other places where disparate peoples gather, professional interpreters are almost indispensable. Without them, business and diplomacy would be impossible, and misunderstandings and conflict would surely fill the void.

Living in such vibrant places, it is only natural that interpreters should get caught up in the adventures and machinations of great people, and perhaps even rise to greatness themselves. The benefits they bring to an adventuring party, including information gathering and the ability to communicate with a wide range of individuals, are not to be sniffed at.

items.name: Equipment:
items.entry: Choose A or B: (A) {@item Ink|XPHB}, {@item Ink Pen|XPHB}, {@item Fine Clothes|XPHB}, {@item Log Keeper|DarkMatter24}, {@item Paper|XPHB} (10 sheets), 13 CR; or (B) 50 CR

entries: In a galaxy with countless cultures and languages, interpreters are indispensable. Even with {@item Universal Translator|DarkMatter24|Universal Translators} and other technological aids, the nuances of language require skilled interpreters to translate for any given language. As such, you've spent countless hours immersing yourself in galactic cultures, so as to communicate with as much of the 'Verse as possible.

name: Intrepid Investigators
entries: {@b Adventuring Company.} You are part of a group that seeks a greater understanding of the mysteries of western Immoren—explorers, ghost hunters, tomb robbers, or perhaps an expedition from Corvis University.

entries.name: Prerequisites
entries: Any character can belong, but the company must include at least one character with the Explorer, Investigator, or Seeker background, or proficiency in Investigation or Survival.

entries.name: Downtime: Exhaustive Research
entries: Before an adventure, you can spend time in archives and libraries uncovering pertinent accounts (cost: {@dice 1d6} gp per day). After 3 days, each member of your company gains one Education die (a d6). Once during the adventure, you can roll the die and add the number to one ability check, attack roll, or saving throw you make, after rolling but before the GM reveals the result.

entries.name: Company Accomplishments
entries: Prestige increases through acts such as: discovering an ancient ruin; recovering ancient treasure or an artifact worth at least 1,000 gp; observing a dangerous animal up close; confronting a powerful undead creature or grymkin; solving an antiquated mystery; or using specialized knowledge to save someone's life.

entries.name: Tier 1 – Fledgling Adventurers
entries: {@b Linguistics.} You can replace one language from your race or background with an ancient or uncommon language (e.g., ancient Caspian, Khurzic, Old Morridane, Orgoth, or a Molgur dialect), including reading and writing it.
{@b An Eye for the Abnormal.} You gain a +2 bonus to passive Wisdom (Perception) checks to notice hidden entrances, ruins, ancient inscriptions, and similar elements.

{@b Expedition Opportunities.} You begin the game with a network of scholars and travelers. If your company agrees to join an expedition, each member receives 50 gp for equipment and supplies. New expedition opportunities arrive from your network once every {@dice 1d10} days.

entries.name: Tier 2 – Notable Explorers
entries: {@b Outfitters.} You receive a 10 percent discount on adventuring gear, ammunition, equipment packs, tools, and mounts and vehicles.

{@b Sponsorship.} A sponsor (noble patron, university, or religious organization) establishes an expense account of 100 gp per month. Any unspent gold is lost at month's end. In return, your sponsor receives monthly reports and first chance to purchase significant artifacts.

entries.name: Tier 3 – Famous Investigators
entries: {@b Applied Knowledge.} Members of the company gain advantage on Dexterity saving throws to avoid traps or environmental hazards (not if blinded, deafened, or incapacitated).
{@b Noteworthy Investigators.} You gain a +2 bonus to Charisma (Persuasion) checks when interacting with explorers or wilderness tribes.

entries.name: Tier 4 – Masters of Discovery
entries: {@b Improved Sponsorship.} Your sponsor increases your expense account to 500 gp per month.
{@b Remarkable Accomplishments.} You can replace Charisma (Intimidation) or Charisma (Persuasion) checks with Intelligence (Investigation) or Wisdom (Survival) checks.

name: Investigator

_.special: piece of evidence or memento from a cold case

entries: You have dedicated your life to pursuit, revelation, and apprehension. Your training has taught you how to determine the truth of a matter through steady analysis and firm inquiry.

As an investigator, determine how you apply your skills in the world. Do you work for the government, an organization, a private business, or do you operate your own enterprise? What caused you to take up the broader mantle of an adventurer?

items.name: Skill Proficiencies
items.entry: {@skill Investigation}, and one from {@skill Insight} or {@skill Perception}

items.name: Equipment
items.entry: A set of common clothes, a traveling longcoat. official detective's documents, a piece of evidence or memento from a cold case, a notebook, and a belt pouch containing 10 gp

entries.name: Feature: Investigator's Declaration
entries: As an investigator you may declare your profession, identifying yourself as one who is determined to ascertain truth. When proclaimed this can give a civilized creature pause, encourage them to flee, or cause them to be more willing to talk to you. This declaration may be accompanied by an official sigil which permits you to operate within the bounds of your government or organization, or your very disassociation with greater authorities may curry favor with creatures you converse with.

entries.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: An investigator who takes up the life of an adventurer expands their sphere of concern to the greater world, but still applies an investigative ethos in their travels.

rows: I cannot abide injustice, and I will act out against it even when facing unfavorable odds.
I am always on the lookout for criminal activity.
I consider the facts carefully before I make any decision.
I have a fixation on determining the motives and psychology of others, even my closest friends.
My investigations have shown me enough of the world to know that I want no part of it.
I am used to helping out those who aren't as smart as I am, and I patiently explain anything and everything to others.
I like to reserve all my knowledge until the most dramatic moment, so I can display it to others and dazzle them with my brilliance.
I don't know much, but my hunches have never led me wrong in the past.
{@bold Community.} All acts must be in the interest of strengthening the welfare between people. (Good)
{@bold Greater Good.} Punishment of evil is the highest good. Procedure too often only plays the role of shackles and an excuse for inaction. (Chaotic)
{@bold Prestige.}  Everything I do is targeted at increasing and showing my standing - it's all anyone can depend on. (Evil)
{@bold Logic.} There are no coincidences because everything can be explained. (Lawful)
{@bold Truth.} Lies always obscure beauty, and finding truth is like the clear peal of a bell. (Neutral)
{@bold Challenge.} Wit, strength, and intelligence mean nothing until matched to trials of comparable power. (Any)
There is a criminal in my past that got away, and I have sworn to bring them to justice.
I became a detective to prevent a certain crime that I was the victim of in the past.
I've discovered the crime of a powerful person, and I've hidden the truth - for now.
I firmly believe in the guiding precepts of my organization.
My town or city is my home, and I will fight to defend it.
I owe everything to another detective who taught me everything I know.
I know the common people are criminals, and it is only by my harsh hand that they are controlled.
I enforce the law stringently, with no room for personal concerns or individual circumstance.
I'm not averse to accepting a bit of money on the side for my hard work.
I obsess over my current case, to the detriment to all other aspects of my life.
I would commit almost any crime to get to the bottom of a case.
I overlook simple solutions in favor of complicated ones.

name: Investigator
entries: You are a skilled detective adept in the techniques of deduction, criminology, and interrogation. In the past, you may have been a watch inspector, a former inquisitor, or a member of a military intelligence-gathering organization.

entries.name: Feature: Astute
entries: Your keen mind and sharp eyes miss very little. You can gain advantage when you make a Wisdom (Insight), Intelligence (Investigation), or Wisdom (Perception) check, but you can't use this feature again until you finish a long rest.

entries.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: Investigators are practical individuals who trust only their own eyes and try to back up their observations with other tools and methods. Discovering the truth often takes precedence over assigning blame.

entries.caption: Personality Trait
rows: I pride myself on my part in keeping things from descending into chaos.
Trust must be earned. I never give it freely.
I am fascinated by people and love to study their mannerisms and interactions.
I am blunt and to the point. I have no time for pointless exposition.
I live for the thrill of the chase. I feel free only when I'm in pursuit.
I love recounting my exploits.
I am willing to overlook crimes of necessity in order to focus on those who harm others.
If I believe someone is hiding something, I cannot concentrate on anything else until the secret is uncovered.

entries.caption: Ideal
rows: Justice. I seek justice for all who have suffered wrongdoing. (Lawful)
Responsibility. I have a responsibility to others that guides my actions. (Good)
Truth. The truth, no matter how uncomfortable, must be discovered and told. (Lawful)
People. I believe people are worth preserving, not ideals or unfeeling laws. (Neutral)
Reason. Logic, not emotion, should guide my choices and actions. (Any)
Punishment. Lawbreakers must be discovered so that I may punish them. (Evil)

entries.caption: Bond
rows: I wasn't good enough to catch someone who ended up ruining my life, but I will have justice.
I owe everything to a mentor whose ideals I strive to live up to.
If anyone learned a secret about my past, all my honor would be lost.
I always take a stand whenever I witness injustice.
I made a mistake and ended up in a crime lord's pocket.
I constantly train to be at the peak of my ability.

entries.caption: Flaw
rows: My career kept me from forming any real connections. I still have a hard time making friends.
I expect to be lied to at every turn.
I am quick to see people's flaws and can't help but point them out.
I see everything in black and white.
Things only work well when I am in full control.
The only thing I'm better at than pessimism is cynicism.

_.special: a mysterious artifact or document related to your investigation

items.name: Tool Proficiencies:
items.entry: One type of {@filter artisan's tools|items|source=phb|miscellaneous=mundane|type=artisan's tools} related to your investigative methods (e.g., {@item alchemist's supplies|PHB} for analyzing samples, or a {@item forgery kit|PHB} for examining documents)

items.name: Languages:
items.entry: You learn to read one language of your choice, which represents the case that you obsess the most over.

items.name: Equipment:
items.entry: A {@item book|PHB|notebook} and charcoal pencil, a set of {@item common clothes|PHB}, a set of {@filter artisan's tools|items|source=phb|miscellaneous=mundane|type=artisan's tools} you are proficient with, a mysterious artifact or document related to your investigation, and a {@item pouch|PHB} containing 10 gp.

entries.name: Feature: Inquisitive Mind
entries: Your constant searching for answers has trained your mind to find connections and insights where others see none. You have an uncanny knack for seeing through lies and half-truths, and people tend to reveal more information to you, either intentionally or not. You have a knack for getting people to open up to you, whether it's through kindness, intimidation, or trickery.

entries.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: You have a keen mind and a drive to uncover the truth. This passion, fueled by your curiosity and perhaps personal experiences, makes you relentless. Each new mystery is an opportunity to learn more about the city and its secrets, but it can also lead you to perilous situations.

entries.caption: Personality Traits
rows: I am relentlessly curious and always eager to learn something new.
My determination to uncover the truth sometimes leads me to take unnecessary risks.
I believe that every mystery can be solved with enough time and thought.
I tend to keep my theories to myself until I have solid evidence.
I often get lost in my own thoughts and become oblivious to my surroundings.
I am haunted by a terror afflicting Luyarnha (e.g., Scourge, cults, etc..) and its effects on people, and I won't rest until I've uncovered its origins.
I often come off as distant or cold, but I'm deeply compassionate towards those affected by the mysteries I investigate.
I have a cynical sense of humor, often making light of grim situations to keep my spirits up.

entries.caption: Ideals
rows: {@b Truth}. I will uncover the truth, no matter how grim or inconvenient it may be. (Neutral)
{@b Justice}. Those responsible for the city's plight must be brought to justice. (Lawful)
{@b Hope}. The truth could lead to salvation. We can't give up hope. (Good)
{@b Knowledge}. Knowledge is power, and I must know it all. (Any)
{@b Whistleblower}. Everyone has the right to know the truth about what's happening in the city. (Chaotic)
{@b Survival}. The mysteries I investigate are a threat to all life. Stopping them is all that matters. (Any)

entries.caption: Bonds
rows: I lost someone important to me to the Scourge. I'll do anything to prevent others from experiencing the same pain.
I was once saved by a hunter, and I owe them a debt I can never repay.
I have an old friend or mentor who has lost their way. I want to save them.
I've been bribed to look the other way before, my greed cost many their lives, never again.
I have a rival investigator who is always one step ahead of me. One day, I will outshine them.
I believe some people know more about the Scourge than they're letting on. I must uncover their secrets.

entries.caption: Flaws
rows: I am so obsessed with my investigations that I often neglect my own well-being.
I trust my theories more than the testimony of others, which can lead to conflict.
I have a hard time letting go of unsolved mysteries, even when it's necessary for my safety.
I enjoy riches, and am not above investigating wealthy individuals to blackmail them later.
I tend to see mysteries everywhere, even where they don't exist.
I have a dark secret related to my investigation that I fear others may discover.

items.name: Tool Proficiency:
items.entry: Choose one kind of {@item Artisan's Tools|XPHB} related to your investigative methods

items.name: Equipment:
items.entry: Choose A or B: (A) {@item Artisan's Tools|XPHB} (same as above), {@item Paper|XPHB} (10 sheets), {@item Traveler's Clothes|XPHB}, 32 GP; or (B) 50 GP

name: Iron Fang

_: a trophy taken from an enemy (a dagger, broken weapon, or tarnished emblem)

entries: You are a trained Iron Fang and were recently part of the mighty legions of Khador. Your grueling training and battlefield experience have made you dauntless and have inured you to the hardships of battle. Skilled at formation fighting, you feel most comfortable in action when allies are close at hand.

entries.name: Feature: Wall of Iron
entries: You are accustomed to fighting shoulder to shoulder with fellow members of the Iron Fang legions. You gain +1 AC while standing within 5 feet of an ally. Additionally, when you take the Help action to aid an ally's attack, you can make one weapon attack as a bonus action.

entries.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: Teamwork, trust, and fraternity are core values to all Iron Fangs. The regimented military life of an elite unit helps shape their ideals. Their flaws are often the byproduct of a life spent on the front lines of battle.

entries.caption: Personality Trait
rows: Trust is key if I want to ensure success.
I am quick to aid others but slow to change my opinions of them.
I am implacable unless someone disparages my military unit or my Empress.
Risk is irrelevant. Achieving the goal is the only thing that matters.
I am cold and brutal on the battlefield but warm and gregarious off it.
I do not hesitate to lend aid to someone in need—even to my enemies.
I cannot abide those who prey on others.
Take care of your equipment, and it will take care of you.

entries.caption: Ideal
rows: Comrades. My loyalties lie with my comrades in arms, not with any code of ethics. (Neutral)
Duty. I swore an oath to fight to my last breath. I will not betray it. (Lawful)
Nation. Any threats to the Motherland must be destroyed. (Any)
Victory. By defeating others, I prove my strength. (Chaotic)
Protection. My might saves others from harm. (Good)
Violence. I thrill at destroying those who dare challenge me. (Evil)

entries.caption: Bond
rows: I would die to protect my comrades in arms.
My bond to my homeland is paramount. I will do anything Khador requires of me.
I seek renown for my prowess in battle.
My unit kommander betrayed us. I will never forget this treachery.
I cannot return home until I have reclaimed my father's shield.
I intervene in any situation that seems unfair.

entries.caption: Flaw
rows: My default plan in any situation is to be stronger and tougher than the problem.
I act with haste but am slow to process information.
I can't keep out of trouble if provoked.
If everyone just did things my way, there wouldn't be any problems.
I am a coward when I am unarmed.
I regularly forget my strength and often pay a steep price for it.

items.name: Tool Proficiencies:
items.entry: One type of {@filter gaming set|items|source=phb|miscellaneous=mundane|type=gaming set}, {@filter vehicles (land)|items|source=phb;dmg|miscellaneous=mundane|type=vehicle (land)}

items.name: Equipment:
items.entry: A set of dark {@item common clothes|phb}, {@item pack saddle|phb}, {@item burglar's pack|phb}, and a belt {@item pouch|phb} containing 5 gp

entries.name: Lifestyle
entries: Poor

entries.name: Overview
entries: The Iron Route, once the primary trade route between Phlan and Zhentil Keep, used to be a site of extensive banditry until the Phlan's recent occupation. Your time as an erstwhile bandit has given you plenty of experience in the saddle and a knack for acquiring and appraising other people's mounts, pets, and vehicles among other things. This particular set of skills has become very lucrative for you by working for the underground as a horse thief for a local guild of thieves and other shadowy organizations.

entries.name: Feature: Black-Market Breeder
entries: You know how to find people who are always looking for stolen animals & vehicles, whether to provide for animal pit fights, or to supply some desperate rogues the means to get away faster on mounts during an illegal job. This contact not only provides you with information of what such animals & vehicles are in high demand in the area, but also offer to give you favors and information (DM choice) if you bring such animals & vehicles to them. Note: This is a variant of the Criminal Contact feature.

rows: If people leave their gear unsecured, they must not want it very much.
I feel more comfortable sleeping under the open sky.
I always pre-plan my escape should things go bad; I always like to have an exit strategy.
I tend to give animal owners breeding and care advice whether or not they want it.
I lost a pet as a child and sadly reflect on it to this day.
I always form a powerful, emotional bond with my mount.
I recoil at the thought of killing someone else's pet or mount.
I prefer to hang to the back of a scuffle or discussion. Better to have my enemies in front of me.
Loyalty. Never bite the hand that feeds. (Good)
Unpredictability. Keep your enemy guessing and off-balance like a confused deer. (Chaotic)
Power. I strive to become leader of the pack at all costs. (Lawful)
Freedom. I bow to no one I don't respect. (Chaotic)
Resourcefulness. Our wits are our most valuable resource in troubled times. (Any)
Unity. Lone wolves fail where the pack succeeds. (Any)
I cannot leave a harmed animal behind; I must save it or put it out of its misery.
I leave behind my own personal calling cards when I do a job.
I do not trust people who do not have a pet, mount, or furry companion.
The pelt I wear on my back was from an animal that died saving my life, I will always cherish it.
If my pet does not like you, I do not like you!
Once you've ridden with me and fought by my side, I'll be there for you odds be damned.
I talk to animals; I believe they understand me, even if they do not.
I growl at and bite anyone who gets too close to my food while I am eating.
I strongly dislike enclosed spaces and require intoxication or firm encouragement to enter them.
I robbed the wrong caravan once. The owner is a powerful merchant who holds a grudge.
I'm an inveterate gambler.
I judge people based on how well they stand their ground in a fight. I got not time for cowards...

name: Ironmaster Drummers
entries: Your ancestors were some of the best Hyerenn drummers of Wagadu. Once per day you gain advantage on a Charisma ({@skill Performance}) drumming check.

name: Irregulars
entries: {@b Adventuring Company.} Not every mercenary company in the Iron Kingdoms operates with the benefit and legitimacy of a charter. Your group might be a former military unit, charter-less mercenaries, or simply warriors who fight for themselves and those they protect.

entries.name: Prerequisites
entries: Any character can belong to an Irregulars company.

entries.name: Downtime: Sell-Swords
entries: Irregulars have a reputation for being hardy warriors who are always ready for a fight. Members of your company can spend their downtime earning a little extra coin by hiring themselves out as bodyguards, sentries, or even gladiators. For each day that you spend in this fashion, you earn {@dice 1d6} gp, but on a roll of 1, your hit point maximum decreases by 1d6 until you finish a long rest.

entries.name: Company Accomplishments
entries: Your company's prestige increases through acts such as: killing or capturing an enemy commander; routing a rival mercenary company; negotiating a contract with a warlord, noble, or military commander; saving the life of a chieftain or notable figure; capturing a warjack, warbeast, or valuable possession from a rival company.

entries.name: Quirks
entries: Many adventuring companies have quirks that set them apart. Choose a quirk or roll on the table: (1) Former irregulars unit from a nation's military; (2) Original members were deserters or criminals; (3) Former tribal warriors who were bought off; (4) Camp-movers who leave no trace behind; (5) Strict self-imposed rules about contract terms; (6) All lost someone in the Claiming; (7) Folk heroes from the same small village; (8) Known for an imposing captured battle standard; (9) New inductees take on part of a fallen founder's name; (10) Company made its name taking the bloodiest, most unwanted jobs.

entries.name: Tier 1 — Backwoods Recruits
entries: {@b Encampment.} Your ragtag group maintains a simple but effective encampment of tents, lean-tos, and natural shelters. You can stay at your encampment and maintain a poor lifestyle at no expense.

{@b Masters of None.} When you make an ability check using a skill or tool you aren't proficient with, you can add your proficiency bonus to the roll. You can use this benefit once between long rests.

{@b No Nonsense.} You can replace one proficiency gained from your background or class with proficiency in the Intimidation skill, and you add double your proficiency bonus when using Intimidation to negotiate or collect on a mercenary contract.

entries.name: Tier 2 — Ragged Soldiers
entries: {@b Ambuscade.} During the first round of combat, you have advantage on attack rolls against creatures that haven't taken an action yet that turn.
{@b Fresh Faces.} Your growing reputation attracts new recruits. You gain {@dice 1d6} hirelings with a challenge rating of 1/2 or lower.
{@b Pay Up.} When you spend downtime working as a sell-sword, you gain {@dice 1d10} gp for each day spent doing such work, rather than {@dice 1d6} gp.

entries.name: Tier 3 — Motley Militia
entries: {@b Advance Payment.} When you take on a mercenary contract, you can demand up to 200 gp in advance, depending on the total terms of the contract.
{@b Champions-at-Arms.} You gain your choice of {@dice 1d8} hirelings with a challenge rating of 1 or lower or {@dice 1d4} hirelings with a challenge rating of 2 or lower.

{@b Frontier Fortress.} You've upgraded your encampment to a fortified garrison with barracks, a smithy, and stables that can hold a warjack or warbeast. You can maintain a modest lifestyle at no expense. Creatures that attempt to attack you while you are in your fortress have disadvantage on attack rolls during the first round of combat.

entries.name: Tier 4 — Frontier Legends
entries: {@b Hard-Bitten.} Having stared death in the face on battlefields all over western Immoren, you've become inured to the hardships and dangers of your trade. Members of your company—including your hirelings—have advantage on saving throws to avoid being {@condition charmed} or {@condition frightened}.
{@b Fearsome Fighters.} You gain your choice of {@dice 1d10} hirelings with a challenge rating of 2 or lower or a steamjack, myrmidon, or warbeast with a challenge rating of 5 or lower.

_.special: sketch of the site you worked at

items.name: Tool Proficiencies
items.entry: Two sets of {@filter artisan's tools|items|miscellaneous=mundane|type=artisan's tools}, or one set of {@filter artisan's tools|items|miscellaneous=mundane|type=artisan's tools} and a {@filter gaming set|items|source=phb|miscellaneous=mundane|type=gaming set}

items.name: Equipment
items.entry: A sponge, a mop, a jar of homemade cleaning fluid, a sketch of the site you worked at, two sets of {@filter artisan's tools|items|miscellaneous=mundane|type=artisan's tools} or one set of {@filter artisan's tools|items|miscellaneous=mundane|type=artisan's tools} and a set of {@item dice set|phb|bone dice} or {@item playing card set|phb|deck of cards}, a set of {@item common clothes|phb}, and a {@item pouch|phb} containing 10 gp.

entries.name: Feature: Leave No Trace
entries: With your experience as a janitor, you can make a messy room or area look absolutely clean, as if no one has been in that area before. You can spend an hour in a room or area cleaning blood and stains, removing bodies and other suspicious objects, closing and re-locking containers, basically doing anything to make the room look undisturbed. Your DM might rule that some things are impossible to clean or fix, or might increase the time you'll spend if the area is extremely messy.

entries.name: Job Site
entries: You worked at a structure or building before. Roll or choose from the table below to determine the type of site you worked in. Also talk with your DM about the site and why you're now adventuring. Was the site destroyed? Did something in the site force you on a quest? Were you simply fired? Or do you still work there, adventuring as a side job to earn extra coins?

rows: Shrine or Temple
Statue, Sculpture, or a Museum
Royal Castle
Dungeon
Military Fortress
Academy or Library
Amphitheater
Cemetery

entries.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: Janitors are serious and hardworking people, but they relax and enjoy themselves earnestly when the work's done. They play just as or harder than they work. But, constantly working to make things clean and organized has made some janitors compulsive and germophobic.

rows: I can think of fifty ways to use a hammer.
I am constantly organizing my inventory; every pouch has a specific purpose.
I like to listen to poems when I'm done. I know more about poetry than people think.
I try to bathe at least four times a day.
Hard work is earnest work, especially if it pays.
I have (or prefer) a small vocabulary.
I'm never distracted at work. Period.
I once climbed fifteen feet to scrub a stain with my bare palms because I lost the ladder and my sponge. I'll do it again if I have to.
{@b Responsibility:} I must keep my site clean and in repair. Everyone has to do their part in society. (Lawful)
{@b Cleanliness:} Cleanliness means good health and more visitors. That makes me happy. (Good)
{@b Rebellion:} I don't deserve to do this. The owners should take care of their own sites. (Evil)
{@b Choice:} Everyone should do what they love at some point in life. (Chaotic)
{@b Site:} I'm committed to my site, not ideas or people. (Neutral)
{@b Aspiration:} I want to prove myself worthy of a better job. (Any)
I care only about my place of work.
My tools are why I'm living comfortably. Without them I'm nothing.
My site was destroyed by someone. I'll find them and get my revenge someday.
I'm housing an urchin at my site. He's/she's the world to me.
I'll never be able to thank the owner of my site.
There's an artifact at my site that I must protect above anything else.
Adventuring introduced billions of germs to my body. Now I can never be clean!
Asymmetry and out-of-place objects will distract me from important work.
I learned to smell better than most people, I hate bad smells more than anything.
I would much rather die in a clean environment.
If I notice something's missing—even if it's replaceable or worthless—I'll drop what I'm doing to search for it.
Why do adventurers never bathe? It's annoying and disguising.

entries: You've cleaned for a large portion of your life, since you were born or since you reached adulthood. Perhaps it was a habit which you grew into, rather than something that ill-circumstances forced you into. You may have tended to a structure or building in several ways: cleaning, repairs, occasionally guarding, and so forth. Maybe you were employed by evildoers to clean up their dirty work, or maybe you overheard conversations within the imperial halls where you've worked. This kind of special environment may have been a starting point for your sense of adventure; but at heart, you simply began by being the local handyman.

Types of janitor adventurers vary based on the kind of work they did and why. There are Cinderella figures, for example, who were doing chores their whole life until something prompted them to escape their life of drudgery to search for better horizons. Darker figures also exist, like the ones who run about looking for "cleaning" jobs, usually sought after by criminals to help them get rid of evidence, or even scour away their identities.

When you choose this background, work with your DM to determine the structure or building you worked at, the said structure or building's importance, what your job was like, and why you now moved to the adventuring life.

_.special: sketch of the site you worked at

items.name: Tool Proficiencies
items.entry: Two sets of {@filter artisan's tools|items|miscellaneous=mundane|type=artisan's tools}, or one set of {@filter artisan's tools|items|miscellaneous=mundane|type=artisan's tools} and a {@filter gaming set|items|source=phb|miscellaneous=mundane|type=gaming set}

items.name: Equipment
items.entry: A sponge, a mop, a jar of homemade cleaning fluid, a sketch of the site you worked at, two sets of {@filter artisan's tools|items|miscellaneous=mundane|type=artisan's tools} or one set of {@filter artisan's tools|items|miscellaneous=mundane|type=artisan's tools} and a set of {@item dice set|phb|bone dice} or {@item playing card set|phb|deck of cards}, a set of {@item common clothes|phb}, and a {@item pouch|phb} containing 10 gp.
