items.name: Equipment
items.entry: Belt {@item pouch|phb} with 10gp, a token from your former life, a tattered cloak, and a set of {@item common clothes|phb}

entries: You are a wanderer who has traversed the forsaken landscapes of Hell, cursed to roam its desolate realms. As a Lost Soul, you have endured unimaginable torment and have become hardened by your experiences.

entries.name: Feature: Infernal Resilience
entries: Your time spent surviving in the hellscape has granted you a certain resilience and a keen instinct for danger. You have an uncanny ability to detect hidden threats and navigate treacherous terrains. When traveling through hazardous terrain or when you make a Wisdom (Survival) check to track creatures or navigate difficult terrain, you are considered proficient in the Survival skill and add double your proficiency bonus to the check.

entries.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: Lost Souls vary greatly in their demeanor and outlook on life, but they often possess a certain ruggedness and a touch of cynicism, shaped by their experiences in the depths of Hell. Use the tables for the Acolyte background as a starting point, modifying them to fit the theme and flavor of a Lost Soul.

rows: I am haunted by the screams and torments of Hell, and it has made me taciturn and introspective.
I have witnessed the true face of despair and suffering, and now I strive to bring hope to others.
I am quick to find fault in others, as I have seen the depths of depravity that souls are capable of sinking to.
I am constantly on edge, expecting betrayal and danger at every turn.
I find solace in the quiet solitude of desolate places, for they remind me of the emptiness within my own soul.
I have a grim sense of humor, finding irony and dark amusement in the direst of situations.
{@b Survival.} My only goal is to stay alive and find a way out of this infernal nightmare. (Neutral)
{@b Redemption.} I am determined to find a way to redeem myself and escape the eternal torment of Hell. (Good)
{@b Vengeance.} Those who wronged me will pay, and I will make sure they suffer as I have. (Evil)
{@b Endurance.} I will endure any hardship and overcome any obstacle to prove my strength. (Lawful)
{@b Freedom.} I will not be shackled by the chains of Hell. I seek freedom above all else. (Chaotic)
{@b Acceptance.} I have come to terms with my fate and embrace the eternal damnation that awaits me. (Neutral)
I am driven by a burning desire to find a way to save the souls trapped in Hell.
I carry the guilt of a past mistake that led me to my damnation, and I seek a way to make amends.
The memory of a loved one gives me strength and hope in this desolate realm.
I am part of a group of Lost Souls, and we have formed a bond of camaraderie and mutual survival.
I hold on to a glimmer of hope, a prophecy or legend that promises a way out of Hell, and I will see it fulfilled.
I am convinced that my suffering has a purpose, and I seek to uncover the greater plan behind it all.
I am haunted by nightmares of my past sins, and they often cloud my judgment.
I am fiercely independent and struggle to trust others, as I have been betrayed too many times before.
I have grown callous and indifferent to the suffering of others, for I have seen far worse in Hell.
I am haunted by the faces of those I failed to save, tormented by the belief that I could have done more.
The horrors of Hell have left me emotionally scarred, and I have difficulty forming meaningful connections.
I am consumed by an insatiable hunger for power, willing to do anything to gain an advantage and survive.

_.special: a container holding currency from your homeworld (worth 0 gp)

items.name: Tool Proficiencies
items.entry: One set of artisan's tools and one type of gaming set

items.name: Equipment
items.entry: A token of your homeworld, {@item common clothes|PHB|a set of common clothes}, a container holding currency from your homeworld (worth 0 gp)

entries.name: Homeworld
entries: You can use the following tables to decide on the technology level of the world from which you originated and to determine how you left it. More information on how to build a world can be found in Appendix A.

entries.caption: I come from a world whose greatest technology is ___.
rows: Spears and fire
Archery, agriculture, and alchemy
Walled cities and high magic
Cannons and sailing ships
Firearms and motor vehicles
Computers and rudimentary spaceflight

entries.caption: How I Left
rows: I stowed away on a spaceship that visited (or crash-landed on) my planet.
I left through a terrible mishap with a powerful teleportation spell.
I was abducted.
I left aboard a rudimentary spacecraft which then slipped through a wormhole.
I never left; rather, I traveled in time.
I escaped my planet moments before its destruction.

entries.name: Feature: Low-World Charm
entries: You have a kinship with other low-worlders, especially in the rare cases that you meet someone from your homeworld. Other low-worlders will take a liking to you and will generally honor one reasonable favor you ask, as long as a similar favor is returned later.

entries.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: Low-worlders are as diverse as the worlds they hail from, but all are strangers to the 'verse. Each of them, however, knows that their position is utterly unique; they are among the very few from their world to have stepped out among the stars, a fact they will likely wear with pride, even as they are confused and awe-struck by their new setting.

rows: I constantly make jokes and pop-culture references to things from my own world.
I try my best to understand the technology of the 'verse, but I'm constantly out of my depth.
I'm alternately convinced that my experiences in the 'verse are just a long, convincing nightmare, or evidence of my own insanity.
Most things must be put in very simple terms for me.
I speak with a rustic accent that is almost unintelligible outside my planet.
I still wear whatever I wore when I left my planet.
I'm as arrogant as physically possible.
I'm the best in the 'verse at a highly practical skill, such as hunting or hand-to-hand combat.
Freedom. Now that I've tasted the freedom of space, I'll never return home. (Neutral)
Tyranny. I will return to my homeworld with advanced technology and conquer it. (Evil)
Adventure. I want to experience everything the 'verse has to offer. (Chaotic)
Protection. I can't let innocents come to harm. (Good)
Getting By. I just want to make a buck and eventually retire. (Neutral)
Exploration. There's a wide-open universe to see! (Neutral)
I must search the 'verse to find my home.
If I cannot find the solution to a pandemic on my homeworld, my people will go extinct.
I hope to find a long-lost family member among the stars.
I aim to prove my skills in combat across the 'verse.
I aim to seduce my way across the 'verse.
I want to find a place where I truly belong.
I don't believe that vect are any more alive than toasters are.
I'm addicted to multiple exotic substances not found on my home planet.
I refuse to use certain types of technology I see as unethical or heretical.
I harbor an unshakable contempt for the galactic factions and spacers in general.
I barely have a sense of the galactic currency.
I have an almost hilarious disregard for the safety of others.

entries: Low-worlders hail from planets that have never discovered the secrets of faster-than-light travel, planets from which the rest of the universe seems unknown and out of reach. The technology level of these planets range from as primitive as spears and bone tools, to as advanced as modern Earth. However, without the innovation of faster-than-light travel or the intervention of a galactic faction, the peoples of these planets will never join the galactic community.

Low-worlders find themselves far from home through a variety of different means. Sometimes, their journeys are purposeful, a planet's first rocketborne steps to the stars above, but most often low-worlders stumble into the wider universe by sheer accident. Mishaps with powerful dimensional or teleportation magic, abductions, and stowing away on visiting spacecraft are all common stories among low-worlders.

Universally, low-worlders are foreigners in the 'verse, discombobulated for several years as they learn the basics of their new surroundings. The dizzying array of races baffles them and the mundane prevalence of spacecraft  and other technology astounds them. Despite their naivety with technology and galactic culture, low-worlders often possess finely honed skills forgotten by much of the wider 'verse: you can find no better tracker, fletcher, cobbler, or blacksmith than those from the low worlds.

items.name: Tool Proficiency:
items.entry: Choose one kind of {@item Artisan's Tools|XPHB}

items.name: Equipment:
items.entry: Choose A or B: (A) {@item Artisan's Tools|XPHB} (same as above), {@item Backpack|XPHB}, {@item Rope|XPHB}, 10 {@item Silver|PHB} Pieces, {@item Traveler's Clothes|XPHB}, 29 CR; or (B) 50 CR

entries.name: Low-Worlders of Different Backgrounds
entries: Any 5th Edition background from another setting, such as {@background Acolyte|XPHB} or {@background Sage|XPHB}, can be used for a low-worlder character. Simply rename the background and keep the other benefits.

Low-worlders hail from planets that have yet to discover faster-than-light travel and join the galactic community at large. Perhaps you hail from a world with stone tools and ferocious megafauna, one of castles and dragons, or one humming with electricity and flashing screens.

But now, whether through a teleportation mishap or by hitching a ride on a visiting spacecraft, you've been thrust into the 'Verse. You now find yourself a fish out of water. At all times, you're surrounded by a dizzying array of species, and even the most mundane technology astounds you. The skills you cultivated in your previous life seem irrelevant in this high-tech world, but perhaps you can find a means to ply a trade or find adventure amongst the stars.

_.displayName: A book filled with nonsensical scribblings

entries: Too much time alone does the mind no favors. Left in isolation for many years, you began the long slide into madness long ago. Now wide-eyed and babbling nonsense, most you meet avoid you out of fear or shame at what you've become.

But beneath the madness, you have a cunning mind able to make leaps in logic that others cannot. Insanity is a path to reasoning that others can't hope to grasp, and gives you the power to face horrors that would drive others mad. After all, you already lost your mind.

items.name: Languages:
items.entry: Two {@table exotic languages|phb} of your choice, which you don't realize you understand

items.name: Equipment:
items.entry: A book filled with nonsensical scribblings, a small {@item bell|phb}, a threadbare {@item blanket|phb}, a set of {@item common clothes|phb}, and a belt {@item pouch|phb} containing 15 gp

entries.name: Manifestations of Madness
entries: Lunacy takes many forms. Choose an unusual behavior or roll on the table below to determine how insanity alters your behavior.

rows: You adhere to an impossibly strict routine.
You never blink, and fix people with a constant wide-eyed stare.
You constantly fidget, tap your fingers, scratch yourself, or otherwise engage in other compulsive behavior.
You do not speak. Ever.
You can't sleep without a light on.
You protect your food with your life and eat voraciously.
You snap between rage and joy like flipping a switch.
You believe every conspiracy theory you come across.
You compulsively count the seconds, minutes, hours, and days between events.
You compare everything to legends and fairy tales.
You hallucinate vividly and often, and believe your visions are real.
You laugh and shriek like a maniac in combat, unnerving your enemies.

entries.name: Feature: Madman's Ravings
entries: Even a stopped clock is right twice a day. When not in initiative, you can begin a mad, babbling stream-of-consciousness conversation about anything and everything that comes to mind. While in this state, you have advantage on all Wisdom (Perception) and Wisdom (Insight) checks to analyze others' reactions to your ravings, which often reveals secrets and hidden conspiracies. You can use this feature twice per long rest.

entries.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: The life of a lunatic is a lonely one. Insanity is a gateway to incredible talent and insight, but strange habits and ignored social graces isolate them from others. A few lunatics live a short, brilliant life, but most die alone in shame and squalor.

rows: After so long alone, I hate being left by myself.
I lash out when restrained or held back.
I don't trust doctors or healers.
I still seek knowledge, even though my findings drove me insane.
I believe myself to be an avant-garde artist. Maybe I am.
I am only pretending to be mad. Others' reactions to my behavior entertain me.
I fixate on particular individuals and try to become like them.
I am kind to my fellow madmen; far kinder than even the well-meaning sane.
{@b Conformity.} Despite my symptoms, I try oh so hard to fit into normal society. (Lawful)
{@b Sympathy.} Though I can't be cured, I do my best to aid those who can. (Good)
{@b Self-regard.} I am who I am, and I'm not ashamed. (Chaotic)
{@b Cruelty.} I use my insanity to justify sadistic acts. (Evil)
{@b Unpredictability.} Even I don't know what I'll do next. (Neutral)
{@b Restoration.} I'll do anything to be whole again. (Any)
I was driven mad by a revelation from a creature from another plane, who I seek to bring into the world.
I have an imaginary friend or enemy who I'm convinced is real. I want to prove that to others.
I have highly-specialized expertise in one area at the expense of all else.
One day, I'll make everyone else see the world my way.
I just want to watch the world burn.
I'm trapped inside my body, watching someone else take action. I need to break out!
I have no regard for the feelings, safety, or lives of others.
I bottle up my feelings until they explode, often at the worst possible moment.
I don't need any help—I'm fine just the way I am!
I destroy things to vent stress. The more valuable, the better.
I lose all composure when someone contradicts my twisted worldview.
I love being different from everyone else.

items.name: Skill Proficiencies:
items.entry: Your choice of two of the following: {@skill Arcana}, {@skill History}, or {@skill Persuasion}

items.name: Equipment:
items.entry: A set of {@item fine clothes|phb}, a student uniform, a {@item writing kit|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn} ({@item pouch|PHB|small pouch} with a quill, {@item Ink (1-ounce bottle)|PHB|ink}, {@item Parchment (one sheet)|PHB|folded parchment} and a penknife), and a belt {@item pouch|PHB} containing 10 gp

entries.name: Feature: Academic Requisition
entries: You've cleared enough lessons—and have gained an ally or two among the staff—to enable access to certain private areas within the {@book Lyceum|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|3|5. Alabaster Lyceum} and other allied universities. Whenever you're on {@book Lyceum|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|3|5. Alabaster Lyceum} grounds or at another major academic institution, you can requisition any set of {@filter tools|items|source=phb|miscellaneous=mundane|type=artisan's tools} found in the fifth edition rules. Each set of {@filter tools|items|source=phb|miscellaneous=mundane|type=artisan's tools} is magically marked to sound an alarm if they are removed from the university's grounds.

When you seek services such as spellcasting from an NPC at the {@book Alabaster Lyceum|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|3|5. Alabaster Lyceum} or a related institution, you can use those services at a 25 percent discount, at the GM's discretion.

entries.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: The {@book Alabaster Lyceum|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|3|5. Alabaster Lyceum} accepts students of all major trades, the fine arts, and the magical arts. Pupils talented and privileged enough to be accepted travel to {@book Emon|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|3|Emon, the City of Fellowship} from all over Tal'Dorei, seeking to study among some of the greatest minds and most talented arcanists in the land. If you came from a smaller city, a rural area, or Tal'Dorei's relatively uncharted wilderness, studying at the {@book Lyceum|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|3|5. Alabaster Lyceum} might have left you with a sense of culture shock, for good or for ill.

Your bond is likely associated with your goals as a student or graduate. Your ideal probably involves your hopes in using the knowledge you've gained at the {@book Lyceum|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|3|5. Alabaster Lyceum}, and your travels as an adventurer, to tailor the world to your liking.

entries.caption: Lyceum Scholar Personality Traits
rows: I can't believe I'm here! At the {@book Alabaster Lyceum|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|3|5. Alabaster Lyceum}. Oh, gods, I've dreamed of this my whole life, and now I'm here!
I can't believe I squandered all the opportunities I had at school. I was supposed to be learning good stuff, but I wasted it all daydreaming about fighting monsters.
Every night at school, I'd knock back a couple of meads and read with my pals! Just a bunch of nerds having fun, and I loved it.
Everyone at school was such a stick in the mud. Dressing the same, listening to the same bards...ugh, it's sad. Just be yourself.
I'm happiest when I've got my little party with me. At school, it was like we were a squad of heroes, slaying projects like monsters.
I'd really rather you didn't bother me. Can't you see I'm studying here?
I don't care. I just don't care about it all. The dates I had to memorize, the formulae I learned...I just want to run away and live!
I'm just...tired. All the time. Oh, adventuring, sure, that's fine, as long as I can find time to...nap...goodnight.

entries.caption: Lyceum Scholar Ideals
rows: {@b Preparedness}. I can't go out into the world unless I know what I'm up against. Study first, act later. (Neutral)
{@b Stardom}. Having a team is good and all, but you can't win a game of ball without the star charger, and you know that's me. (Evil)
{@b Individuality}. The world keeps us down by trying to put us all into little boxes. I'm tired of living in my box, and I don't care what you think about it. (Chaotic)
{@b Purpose}. I study because there are things I need to know. I'll find my place in the world, and I'll make the world better. (Good)
{@b Code of Conduct}. The student code is there to benefit all students, you know. It's the same for laws! (Lawful)
{@b Recreation}. All this studying crap wasn't worth anything if you weren't partying when you were done. Meet me down at the tavern, okay? (Chaotic)

entries.caption: Lyceum Scholar Bonds
rows: I came to the {@book Lyceum|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|3|5. Alabaster Lyceum} with no one, but I fell in love with the city of {@book Emon|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|3|Emon, the City of Fellowship}. I've finally found a place that feels like home!
Most of my professors drove me to frustration, but there's one who was kind and wise. I know they'll always have my back.
My family saved every copper piece to give me the opportunities I have now. I can't let them down.
I came to the {@book Lyceum|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|3|5. Alabaster Lyceum} with a childhood friend, but we've long been drifting apart.
Discovery is the only thing that matters to me. The topic doesn't matter. Books keep me company on my loneliest days.
The {@book Lyceum|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|3|5. Alabaster Lyceum} is my life. I'd give up anything—everything—to protect it from harm.

entries.caption: Lyceum Scholar Flaws
rows: The {@book Lyceum|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|3|5. Alabaster Lyceum} taught me to never want to leave my room. The campus was so huge, and the crowds were so horrible.
You think you're so great just because you've got muscles, and endurance, and...shut up! Read a book sometime!
Huh? What? Sorry, I was thinking about a test I need to retake when I get back to school....
I spent too much time studying. Now I don't have any friends.
If you don't match my aesthetic, I'm not interested in you. We can work together, but we won't be friends. Got it?
I'm always striving for perfection. I got top of my class, sure, but only with a 98 average. And that's. Not. Perfect.

items.name: Skill Proficiencies
items.entry: Your choice of two from among {@skill Arcana}, {@skill History}, and {@skill Persuasion}

items.name: Equipment
items.entry: A set of {@item fine clothes|phb}, a lyceum uniform, a {@item Calligrapher's Supplies|phb|writing kit}, and a belt {@item pouch|phb} containing 10 gp

entries.name: Feature: Student Privilege
entries: You've cleared enough lessons, and gained an ally or two on staff, to have access to certain chambers within the Lyceum (and some other allied universities) that outsiders would not. This allows use of any Tool Kit, so long as the Tool Kit is used on the grounds of the Lyceum and is not removed from its respective chamber (each tool kit is magically marked and will sound an alarm if removed). More dangerous kits and advanced crafts (such as use of a Poisoner's Kit, or the enchanting of a magical item) might require staff supervision. You may also have access to free crafting materials and enchanting tables, so long as they are relatively inexpensive, or your argument for them is convincing (up to the staff's approval and DM's discretion).

entries.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: Use the tables for the {@background Sage} background in the Player's Handbook as the basis for your traits and motivations, modifying the entries when appropriate to match your pursuits at the Lyceum. Your bond is likely associated with your goals as a student, and eventually a graduate. Your ideal probably involves your hopes in using the knowledge you gain at the Lyceum, and your travels as an adventurer, to tailor the world to your liking.

You most likely came up through money or a family of social prestige somewhere in the world, as tuition at the Alabaster Lyceum is not inexpensive. Your interests and pursuits have brought you to the glittering halls of Tal'Dorei's highest place of learning, soaking in all and every lesson you can to better make your mark on the world (or at least you should be, but every class has its slackers). However, the call to adventure threatens to pull you from your studies, and now the challenge of balancing your education with the tide of destiny sweeping you away is looming.

You may have come to better research and understand the history and lore of Exandria and the lands you now call home, perhaps seeking a future here at the Lyceum as a professor. You could also have been drawn by the promise of prosperity in politics, learning the inner workings of government and alliances to better position yourself as a future writer of history. Perhaps you've discovered a knack for the arcane, coming here to focus on refining your spellcraft in the footsteps of some of the finest wizards and sorcerers in days of yore.

items.name: Equipment
items.entry: A set of {@item traveler's clothes|phb}, a pocket book entitled {@i Field Guide To Auras, Nodes and Residuals}, a quill,  5 parchments, and a {@item pouch|phb} containing 10 gp.

entries.name: Feature: Reputation
entries: Your occupation has gained you infamy across the magical community whether you like it or not. All mages you encounter now believe talking to you implicates them as a target of your organization. When you are in a civilized settlement, you can invoke your position to exert influence over mages to gain information. This might include secret hideouts, meetings, pieces of lore, locations of dark artifacts, or the whereabouts of someone you might be searching for.

entries.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: Mage hunters are shaped by their organization's goals, beliefs, and traditions. The tolls of hunting mages whether you believed they were innocent or not have left a mark on you, forming most of your characteristics.

rows: I am often seen alone, walking faster, ahead of anyone else.
People often hear me drawling about how magic users all deserve long, painful deaths.
I'm described as defensive, always justifying everything I do.
You'll find me often in a library dwelling on books about evil mages I've read over and over again already.
My actions and temperament are controlled and tempered, more than what can be said for magic.
I claim to only be a little paranoid when I may be freaking out inside.
I consider violence as a last resort, and my pacifist attitude reflects that.
Preparation is everything. I am ridiculous meticulous in that regard, double checking my laces, dotting my i's and crossing my t's...
{@b Greed.} I only took this job for the money - nothing more, nothing less (Any).
{@b Righteousness.} I have a duty to protect those who cannot protect themselves. (Good)
{@b Power.} I will use all the magical secrets I've learned to kill those who get in my way. (Evil)
{@b Code of Honor.} I hold all mages accountable for their actions. (Lawful)
{@b Destruction.} As long as the job gets done, who cares if a few buildings explode? (Chaotic)
{@b People.} I help the people who help me - that's what keeps me alive. (Neutral)
I have some old colleagues that I can trade information with from time to time.
Those who fight beside me are worth dying for.
I carry an ancient artifact that must not fall into the wrong hands.
I owe my organization a great debt for forging me into the person I am today.
There is one mage who has always been one step ahead of me.
Someone I loved died because of a mistake I made. That will never happen again.
I'll do anything to get the job done, damn the consequences.
Most people scream and run when they see a demon. I stop and take notes about its anatomy.
I am in love with a person who dabbles in dark magic and I will do anything to protect them.
I have been secretly practicing the dark magic I have been fighting my entire life.
Ale and wine are the only thing that keeps me functioning anymore.
Someone powerful would do anything to have my head, so I seek to gain his or her head first.

entries: You worked for (or were raised by) an organization which specialized in tracking, investigating, and apprehending beings that had magical powers. Perhaps your organization was a school of wizards and sorcerers that had a distaste for students who practice magic outside their teachings, or for a government that had a hatred of those who dabble in the dark arts. You enforced the rules of magic - whether for a public or private interest. Work with your DM to determine what organization you were a part of and the reason you left. Perhaps you accidentally killed an innocent civilian that wasn't a magic practitioner at all, maybe you were forced into retirement, or maybe you discovered that your organization's intentions were corrupt and evil.

If you prefer a less foundational backstory, maybe you were the sole survivor of a horrific magical event which hardened your heart against magic and all its users. You strive to destroy magic and those who use it, seeing it as a force none ought to wield due to its destructive potential. Work with your DM to discuss what possible historical event or recurring phenomena involving magic could have tempered a hatred towards the arcane. Perhaps your home was ransacked by an infamous band of bloodthirsty wizards, or maybe someone dear to you was used as a sacrifice in the name of magical research.

_.special: satchel for material components and potions

b.displayName: other trinket of importance to you

items.name: Skill Proficiencies:
items.entry: Two of the following: {@skill Arcana}, {@skill Deception}, {@skill Investigation}, {@skill Perception}

items.name: Tool Proficiencies:
items.entry: Either calligraphers' supplies or alchemists' supplies

items.name: Equipment:
items.entry: A gnarled {@item wand|PHB} made of wood, a duster jacket, a satchel for material components and potions, an {@item amulet|PHB} or other {@item trinket|PHB} of importance to you

rows: My eyes are two different colours.
Whenever I cast a spell, my voice echoes and an unknown wind seems to blow around me.
My eyes glow with octarine light when I am casting spells.
I hear voices and sounds when close to magical entities, as if the magic itself speaks to me.
I have full conversations with myself out loud that occasionally can get heated.
Magic floods my mind and makes it difficult to sleep without constant nightmares and visions.
I speak to beings from other planes of existence who manifest as simple creatures before me.
I have a birthmark in a unique shape that appears every day for 2 and a half hours, then vanishes.

entries.name: Feature: Bookworm
entries: Once per day after you finish a long rest, you can spend one hour to create a spell scroll. You need only paper and ink to do so, and the level of the spell you can create equals one half your proficiency bonus (rounded down) or lower. The scroll you create must be a spell you know or have prepared. It crumbles to dust in 24 hours.

entries.caption: Suggested Characteristics
rows: I idolize one of the archmages of the Academy and hope to prove myself to them in time.
Nothing will get between me and my goals. When people say something I care about is impossible, I prove them wrong.
I am confident in my powers, and do not fear the horrors of Drakkenheim, for I can bend reality.
I am constantly reading books. The more knowledge I can obtain, the more I can outwit friends and foes alike.
I am a mage for hire and am not afraid to use my magic to get my hands dirty. A lot of people will pay top coin for a skill set like mine.
I am a sucker for a good mystery and pride myself in my ability to solve them.
Everyone is always so serious - we all die in the end, might as well enjoy the ride.
I always push myself to be the best at whatever it is I set out to do.
Respect. My powers are a blessing and a curse, and I work diligently to show people not to fear magic. (Good)
Knowledge. I left the Academy on good terms to work at one of the many historical institutes of the world, hoping that my love for books and history would be of use. (Any)
Love. I left the Academy due to love, and I plan to keep my promise to that love. (Good)
Forgiveness. I must undo the mistakes of my past by proving myself to those I care about most. (Good)
Power. Delerium is power, and I must learn all I can about its origins and properties if I am to harness that power. (Chaotic)
Independence. I stand alone from the Academy for a reason. I do not wish to be on their bad side, but I do not wish to be on their good side either. (Neutral)
It is my duty to protect the Amethyst Academy.
My life's work in the study of delerium caused my expulsion. I must continue that research to prove its value.
The mysteries of my past and my power are tied to the meteor. I need answers.
My terrible mistake was covered up by my mentor in the Academy. I owe them my life.
My nightmares have guided me to Drakkenheim. I must investigate these visions.
I come from a long line of wizards, my exit from the Academy was highly upsetting to them and I need to earn my way back into their favour, even if it means risking my life in Drakkenheim.
I walk straight into danger. What's the worst that could happen?
I believe my plan is always far superior to everyone else's.
I am distracted by possibilities of gaining knowledge or power, regardless of the cost or danger.
I overcomplicate most situations with small details and over analyzing simple things.
I get angry quickly, and cause more harm than good with my magic when I get mad.
I can't get enough delerium. I want the power for myself.

items.entry: {@skill Arcana} and your choice of {@skill Perception} or {@skill Performance}

items.entry: One tool set or kit of your choice.

items.entry: One set of tools with which you are proficient, a few pages torn from a user manual for an obscure piece of magitech, common clothes, and a belt pouch with 10 gp.

entries.name: Overview
entries: In Solace, magic is a tool that's incorporated into many jobs. There are entirely magical careers, such as the medium or oracle. But much of the time, mundane skill and magic are combined together. A lamplighter can work with mundane lanterns, but also learns the vagaries of of maintaining the everbright lanterns that light the city's streets. Chefs often heat and flavor food with a cantrip. A locksmith may learn to cast arcane lock, and an actor may learn thaumaturgy to help project their voice or create stage effects. If you take this background, it is recommended that you play either some sort or caster and/or take Magic Initiate as your free feat, choosing a few spells that would have served you in your line of work. What was your profession? How did your grasp of magic aid you? And how did your work influence the rest of your life. What district did you live in? Did your work earn you the respect or contempt of your family, friends, neighbors, and colleagues?

entries.name: Feature: Arcane Knack.
entries: You are you skilled in the practical application of magic to mundane skills and pursuits. You may use Intelligence (Arcana) when attempting to discern how to use, disable or bypass an otherwise mundane object to, at the discretion of the DM, come up with a novel magical solution to the challenge facing you, involving one of your known or prepared spells, or a magic item or piece of magitech that you have on you or otherwise have access to.

items.name: Skill Proficiencies
entries: {@skill Acrobatics}, {@skill Athletics}

items.name: Tool Proficiency
entries: {@item Carpenter's tools|PHB}

items.name: Distinctive Features
entries: Eager, Lordly

_.special: which can be used on equipment needed to match your victim's identity

items.name: Tool Proficiencies
items.entry: {@item thieves' tools|PHB}, {@item poisoner's kit|PHB}, or {@item forgery kit|PHB}

items.name: Equipment
items.entry: A seashell, a set of {@item traveler's clothes|PHB}, and a purse containing 30gp, which can be used on equipment needed to match your victim's identity.

entries.name: Feature: Stolen Identity
entries: As a malenti, you've assumed the identity and memories of a dryskin, and this provides you with the benefits of their position. Choose one of the following background features: By Popular Demand ({@background entertainer}), Criminal Contact ({@background criminal}), Military Rank ({@background soldier}), Position of Privilege ({@background noble}), or Shelter of the Faithful ({@background acolyte}). Once made, you cannot change this choice. This is who you are now, and the background feature suggests what people will expect of you. If you have Shelter of the Faithful, it's because you've taken the place of an acolyte, and people of your assumed faith expect you to live up to that role.

entries.name: Variant Feature: Aquatic Adaptation
entries: If your character has the malenti background, your DM may allow you to select this background feature instead of Stolen Identity.

Your assumed form has no particular reputation or influence. But you were magebred to operate both above and below the water, and possess the ability to breathe underwater. This is granted by gills set along your ribs, which are clearly not normal for your apparent species. If your torso is exposed, this will certainly draw attention.

entries.name: Tour of Duty
entries: As a malenti, you've stolen the identity of a surface dweller. But when did this occur? How long have you been playing this role and how comfortable are you with it?

rows: You replaced your victim in their youth, and have a well-established relationship with family and friends.
You replaced your victim during the Last War, and may have fought in some of the battles yourself.
Your victim was lost at sea years ago and presumed dead; you have only just "miraculously" returned.
Your victim's parents or siblings also been replaced by malenti, and are serving as spies in a major city
You replaced your victim only a month ago, as they returned from a trip to Stormreach.
You replaced your victim a year ago, but the circumstances were difficult and some of your old acquaintances are still suspicious.

entries.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: Malenti are deep cover spies. Becoming a malenti means sacrificing the sahuagin world you've known your whole life; it requires strong will and devotion. But malenti are a blend of sahuagin spy and the person they appear to be; they still have the memories and the mannerisms of the victim, and this can cause the sahuagin personality to erode or evolve.

rows: I love to eat and I'm always eager to try new forms of food and drink.
I express many concepts using aquatic metaphors.
I won't indulge weakness, especially in myself.
When it comes to romance, I'm a fish out of water.
I'm insatiably curious and always asking questions.
I love the water and never pass up a chance for a swim.
I'm always taking notes on the people I meet and things I see.
I consider the people of Khorvaire to be primitive barbarians. Even though I'm one of them. Really.
Victory. I'll use any means necessary to defeat my enemy. (Neutral to Evil)
The Mission. My mission means more to me than my friends or my life. (Lawful)
Strength. Life is a struggle, and only the strong will survive. I must be strong. (Any)
Commitment. Once I commit to a task, I always see it through. (Lawful)
Knowledge. I've given up my previous life to gain information for my people. (Neutral)
Victim's Ideals. I find myself drawn to the ideals of my victim, which could include strange ideas of honor or compassion. (Any)
I need to learn as much as possible about the nations and cultures of the surface.
I'm supposed to protect and observe one of the other player characters, but I don't know why.
I'm searching for information on one of the fiendish overlords and fighting its agents.
I want to study all ancient surface civilizations, like the giants, demons, and goblins.
I want to study the magical capabilities of the Five Nations and to investigate the Mourning.
I'm interested in manifest zones and planar exploration.
I don't understand the concepts of charity or mercy.
I have trouble expressing gentle emotions.
I view everyone as a possible enemy and am always considering ways to defeat them.
I often need to help my victim's family or friends.
I feel torn between my loyalty to the Dominion and the values of my victim.
I've inherited the consequences of my victim's terrible mistakes.

entries: You were born a sahuagin in the Eternal Dominion of the Thunder Sea, but ritual magic and the blood of the kar'lassa allowed you to consume and replace a surface dweller. You can never regain your original form; for all intents and purposes, you are who you appear to be. You're physically indistinguishable from them, and you have enough of their memories to fool even their family and friends. But you have the mind of a sahuagin, and you're loyal to the Dominion.

As a malenti, the first question is why the Dominion chose to replace this particular person, and how your mission relates to your activities as an adventurer. It's possible that your only mission is to observe the dryskins and occasionally provide information to a sahuagin spymaster, or you might have a specific goal that drives your actions during your adventures. The Suggested Characteristics tables provide information about your mission.

You're physically identical to the creature you appear to be; you are an elf, or a kalashtar, or whatever race you replaced. It is up to you and your DM to decide how widespread malenti are in Khorvaire. It could be that the Dominion has placed many malenti in the Five Nations, or you might be one of the first. If this is the case, you may be the first malenti to duplicate a creature of this particular race or species. This could be particularly interesting with a kalashtar—you've inherited the spiritual bond with a quori, but what does that mean for you? Will the tie to the alien spirit change you? Similarly, if you possess a dragonmark, it seems to function normally, but will there be strange consequences in your future?

It's possible that your abilities reflect additional Dominion magebreeding or skills from your sahuagin side. If you're a barbarian, does your rage reflect the blood frenzy of the sahuagin? If you're a sorcerer, is spellcasting a gift your victim already possessed, or is it the result of sahuagin modification? And how has the integration of the new personality affected you? Are you still a true sahuagin, devoted to the Dominion? Or are the victim's memories and experiences causing you to question your mission?

a.special: The equipment of a background related to the person you consumed

You can never regain your original form; for all intents and purposes, you are who you appear to be. You're physically indistinguishable from them, and you have enough of their memories to fool even their family and friends. But you have the mind of a {@race Sahuagin|ExploringEberron24}, and you're loyal to the Dominion.

As a Malenti, the first question is why the Dominion chose to replace this particular person, and how your mission relates to your activities as an adventurer. It's possible that your only mission is to observe the dryskins and occasionally provide information to a {@race Sahuagin|ExploringEberron24} spymaster, or you might have a specific goal that drives your actions during your adventures.

items.entry: {@skill Arcana}, plus one from among {@skill History}, {@skill Investigation}, {@skill Nature} and {@skill Survival}

items.name: Equipment:

entries.name: Feature: Ley Touched
entries: You gain the {@feat Ley-Touched|CoH-LLN} feat.

In addition, work with your GM to establish connections with one organization in your world that studies Ley Lines and Nexuses. Members of that organization will provide you free, modest lodging and food at any of their establishments. In Kyrmoria, two such organizations are:

items: The Acolytes of the Veil, historians, lore-keepers and guardians of wild, natural magic. Their base of operations is in the Prismatic Mountains, but they have other settlements and agents throughout the land.

The Cabal, an illegal organization of mages running the underground citadel of Dhen Rahzeem and profiting from its vast black market as well as mana geode trade with the Kyrmorian Republic and the flying cities of the Shifting Barrens.

entries.name: Building a Manascarred Character
entries: Manascarred characters are typically spellcasters, finding that their innate connection with the magic of the land favors the path of a druid, sorcerer, warlock, weaveknight or wizard, regardless of specialization. Bards and rangers also find this connection enhancing their arsenal, while a lot of clerics and paladins view the mark as a blessing from a deity or other higher power. Additionally, barbarians, fighters, monks and rogues often find that being marked by mana can enhance their physical capabilities, allowing them to perform unique tasks none of their peers are able to.

entries.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: To have a mark left on you by the mana has various benefits and drawbacks. You could have experienced people treating you favorably and embracing you, or you could have been discriminated against due to fear and uncertainty, making you reluctant to connect with others. The Manascarred Personality Traits table suggests traits you might adopt for your character.

entries.caption: Manascarred Personality Traits
rows: The scar is a curse, and I won't rest until it's lifted.
I bear my scar with pride because it made me who I am today.
I believe I've been blessed with a great destiny.
I want to seek out and connect with others sharing marks of the mana.
I am not a monster regardless of how people see me, and I will prove it.
I will harness this gift and acquire great power.

entries.name: Manascar Event
entries: When you make your character, consider what event left the magical scar on you. The Manascar Event table below provides suggestions on determining how you came to acquire such a mark. In addition, work with your GM to determine what the mark looks like; your eyes might shed a soft spectral glow, weird markings may have manifested on your body, or the mark could even take the form of an actual unearthly looking scar.

entries.caption: Manascar Event
rows: You were born at the same moment a nexus manifested.
You were struck by a Ley Line's essence when it was shifting.
The residual magic of a Nexus marked you when you wandered too closely.
You once tried to tap into a ley line unsuccessfully, and it left you with a Manascar.
You were experimented upon by an organization looking to produce super soldiers.
You survived a manaburn explosion.

entries: When you were born, or at some point in your life, the raw magic of the land influenced your very being through a dramatic event, and left you with a mark. After that, you've found yourself having a unique connection with mana, the building blocks of magic, and you've set out to learn more about that connection.

In Kyrmoria, the ley lines running inside the earth and the Nexuses that manifest at their interconnecting points often exert enough influence for someone close to them to manifest some sort of mark. These extraordinary individuals, who are often looked at with awe or fear, are called Manascarred. Some choose to live quiet lives, while others are approached by organizations that show interest in them, but they are nonetheless unique in the world.

name: Maritime Order of the Trident

_: an insignia of rank in the Ordic navy

entries: Your early years were spent training as an arcanist working in concert with the Ordic navy. Although your service recently ended, you likely still serve in an auxiliary capacity alongside the kingdom's naval forces.

entries.name: Feature: Ordic Veteran
entries: You spent your early years as a member of the Ordic Royal Navy. Whether you left on good terms or less favorable ones, you still have many friends who serve. At the GM's discretion, you can secure passage on an Ordic ship if one of your friends has enough sway or is the vessel's captain.

entries.name: Feature: Magus-at-Arms Training
entries: {@b Prerequisite:} Spellcasting, Warcaster Magic, or Pact Magic class feature.
Add the spells on the Magus-at-Arms Training Spells table to the spell list for your spellcasting class. If you are a multiclass character with multiple spell lists, add these spells to all of them.

entries.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: Members of the Maritime Order of the Trident are comfortable living a wanderer's life. Despite their seemingly chaotic bent, the Order instills a sense of patriotic duty, military ethic, and courage.

entries.caption: Personality Trait
rows: I always feel at home when I'm on or around the sea.
Performing my duties precisely is extremely important to me.
I love telling tall tales of the sea.
Simple solutions to problems are often the best.
I try to prepare for any and all contingencies.
I often talk at length about the intricacies of sailing to anyone who will listen—and a few who won't.
I love vulgar banter, even if I'm the subject.
I am a very reliable friend.

entries.caption: Ideal
rows: Crew. I am committed to my crew, not to ideals. (Chaotic)
Exploration. I use my abilities to guide myself and others to undiscovered places. (Any)
Independence. This life allows me to change course whenever I feel like it. (Chaotic)
Protection. My abilities allow others to safely return home from the sea. (Good)
Duty. I have a duty to protect my nation's assets. (Lawful)
Greatness. I'll use my powers to sink anyone who tries to impede my rise to greatness. (Evil)

entries.caption: Bond
rows: My first captain and I enjoyed a great relationship and have become lifelong friends.
When the day comes to an end, I'm the first one to the tavern.
I was knocked out during a brutal storm and fell into the sea. I owe my life to the person who saved me.
I successfully thwarted a pirate raid years ago, and that crew has had it in for me ever since.
A strict hierarchy is extremely important. My allegiance is to the captain first and the crew second.
I lost a great deal of money gambling in a particular port and then skipped town to avoid paying my debt.

entries.caption: Flaw
rows: I follow orders from my superiors even when I know full well they are wrong.
I have little respect for those who have not earned their sea legs.
I have been known to act somewhat wildly during shore leave.
My great pride in myself borders on hubris.
I enjoy starting a rousing sea shanty. Anyone who grumbles for me to stop had best grumble in tune.
I often pocket small trinkets I find interesting.

items.name: Equipment:
items.entry: Choose A or B: (A) {@item Dagger|XPHB}, {@item Flare|SGEHPP}, 50 sheets of {@item Paper|XPHB}, {@item Sacrificial Brand|SGEHPP}, {@item Traveler's Clothes|XPHB}, and 40 GP; or (B) {@item Sacrificial Brand|SGEHPP} and 50 GP

_.displayName: journal detailing your experiences since rebirth

items.name: Equipment:
items.entry: A {@item flare|SGttEH} (used to indicate your position during hunts), a set of {@item common clothes|PHB}, a small knife for carving runes, a {@item book|PHB|journal} detailing your experiences since rebirth, and a {@item pouch|PHB} containing 10 gold pieces. The {@item Sacrificial Brand, Scarified|SGttEH|Sacrificial Brand Eldritch Carving is scarified} on your body.

entries.name: Feature: 6th Sense
entries: Not only were you brought back from the dead by the Blood Moon, but you also survived the horde of beasts that were brought back with you, despite their ability to track you. Your senses are honed beyond mortal comprehension. You can sense the presence and general direction of powerful eldritch energies and artifacts within a 1-mile radius, particularly if they are connected to the {@card Blood Moon of Rebirth|Eldritch Moons Deck|SGttEH} or the {@creature Goat Mother's Avatar|SGttEH|Mother of a Thousand Young}.

entries.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: Your experiences with death and resurrection have profoundly impacted your personality and outlook on life. You might be driven to uncover the secrets of the eldritch forces that brought you back, or you may feel a sense of duty to protect the living from the horrors that lurk beyond the veil.

entries.caption: Personality Traits
rows: I am extremely cautious, having learned the fragility of life firsthand.
I am fascinated by the mysteries of life, death, and the forces that bind them.
I feel a deep connection to the moon, often seeking solace in its light.
I am driven to uncover the purpose behind my resurrection.
I am haunted by the memories of my past life and the circumstances of my death.
I am fiercely protective of those I care about, as I know the pain of loss.
I believe that my resurrection has given me a second chance to make a difference in the world.
I have become detached from the everyday concerns of the living.

entries.caption: Ideals
rows: {@b Balance}. Life and death are part of a delicate cosmic balance that must be maintained. (Neutral)
{@b Knowledge}. Understanding the mysteries of the cosmos is the key to mastering life and death. (Any)
{@b Protection}. I will do everything in my power to protect the living from the horrors beyond the veil. (Good)
{@b Vengeance}. I seek the power to destroy the eldritch forces that toy with life. (Lawful)
{@b Power}. I have been given a rare opportunity, and I will use it to seize control. (Evil)
{@b Freedom}. This new life is a chance to break free from the constraints of my past. (Chaotic)

entries.caption: Bonds
rows: I feel a strong connection to others who bear the Sacrificial Brand.
I owe my resurrection to the Blood Moon, and I am determined to uncover its secrets.
I left behind loved ones in my past life, and I will do anything to protect them from harm.
I am haunted by a vision or prophecy that I received during my resurrection.
I am hunted by Death and must escape its clutches.
I am determined to prevent others from experiencing the pain and confusion that I have endured.

entries.caption: Flaws
rows: I am paranoid, fearing that my resurrection has attracted the attention of sinister forces.
I struggle with feelings of guilt and shame from my past life, making it difficult for me to trust myself and others.
I am obsessed with uncovering the secrets of my resurrection, sometimes to the detriment of my relationships and goals.
I have difficulty forming new relationships, as I am still mourning the loss of my previous life and connections.
I am prone to bouts of rage and anger, fueled by the knowledge of my impending doom.
I am reckless in the face of danger, believing that I have already cheated death once and can do so again.

items.name: Equipment:
items.entry: Choose A or B: (A) {@item Dagger|XPHB}, {@item Flare|SGttEH24}, {@item Paper|XPHB} (50 sheets), Sacrificial Brand Eldritch Carving (Scarified), {@item Traveler's Clothes|XPHB}, 44 GP; or (B) Sacrificial Brand Eldritch Carving (Scarified), 50 GP

bill of sale for a number of tools
