items.entry: Tinker's Tools, one type of artisan's tools

items.name: Equipment
items.entry: Tinker's tools, a supply of mundane parts (kept with your tools), a bill of sale for a number of tools, welding goggles, and a belt pouch containing 10 gp.

entries: Whether or not you were formally trained, mechanical things come second nature to you. When the moving, physical bits of magitech, especially constructs, break down or malfunction, you're called to do the repairs.

You're familiar with the makes and models of perhaps hundreds of models of magitech gear, and carry with you tools to do most types of mundane repairs. Your skills do not go as far as smithing new parts, nor are you trained in enchanting or imbuing mundane constructs with motion, but you are excellent at keeping things running.

entries.name: Feature: Trade Ring
entries: Among the streets of the bustling marketplace, you have a small network of vendors from whom you can purchase almost any magitech component, even illegal ones, and often at a marginal discount. This networks consists of a tight-knit group of experts and hobbyists, allied in both common interest and trade. Your merchants would never sell you out; so neither should you.

entries.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: Mechanics spend so much time working on machines, their minds often work quite mechanically. Dedicated mechanics find a great deal of enjoyment in experimenting with and constructing small projects as fits their fancy.

entries.caption: Personality Trait
rows: I compulsively use long words and jargon, even when inappropriate.
I am constantly covered in oily splotches and grease. I do not know the definition of formal-wear.
I never leave home without at least one complete toolkit.
When I start working on a machine, I whistle the same (incredibly annoying) tune.
When I buy something, I take it apart to understand how it works and try to put it back together.
I love a good riddle, but I'm rubbish at understanding jokes.
I'm fascinated by ancient machines and traps. I copy these designs into my notebook.
I always have a good anecdote about my dwarven uncle (even if I'm not a dwarf.)

rows.name: Innovation
entries: Elegant solutions are a thing of beauty (Lawful)

rows.name: Workmanship
entries: A man's worth can be judged by his skill (Neutral)

rows.name: Experimentation
entries: I believe in discovery for discovery's sake. (Neutral)

rows.name: Progress
entries: The way forward lies through advancing technology. (Good)

rows.name: Greed
entries: I'm only in it for the money. (Evil)

rows.name: Aspiration
entries: I work hard to be the best there is at my craft. (Any)

entries.caption: Bond
rows: I am constantly working on a mechanical pet project. It's ambitious, and maybe a little crazy, but I'm constantly shopping around for the parts to make it work.
Getting a robotic limb installed would be pretty cool.
I possess the diagram of an ancient device, devised by a civilization long past, and I seek to discover its purpose.
I want to accrue enough wealth that I can open my own machine shop.
I owe a great debt to a wealthy noble family due to an accident involving a construct I repaired.
I seek immortality by means of a new construct body.

entries.caption: Flaw
rows: Frustration over a broken machine or a tough to solve problem tends to provoke my explosive temper.
I have trouble breaking information down to make it understandable for other people.
When I design a new nonlethal trap, I tend to try it out on my companions.
A bad experience has left me with a crippling fear of very small constructs.
I am paranoid of constructs rising up and taking over the world.
I horde broken and/or damaged magitech components in the hopes that they'll one day be useful.

name: Mechanic

items.name: Tool Proficiencies:
items.entry: You gain proficiency in three {@item Artisan's Tools|PHB} of your choice.

items.name: Equipment:
items.entry: An {@item abacus|PHB}, ball bearings (1000), {@item block and tackle|PHB}, {@item flask|PHB} of oil, an unfinished mechanical {@item trinket|PHB}, and 15 gold flowers.

entries: You've spent most of your life working on mechanisms and machines. For you, understanding both new and old technology requires a more hands on approach. Through trial and error, you have learned to create, repair, and modify all things mechanical and electronic, and you have honed your eye to recognize useful parts among the scattered bits of technology that are found throughout the island.

entries.name: Feature: Machine Whisperer
entries: You have a knack for machines and can tell what state one is in by spending a few minutes with it. Machines that have been sundered are unusable and should be scrapped for parts. Machines in disrepair could potentially function again if someone fixed them up, and functioning machines do just that. Function!

items.name: Tool Proficiencies
items.entry: {@item Tinker's tools|phb} and one type of vehicle

items.name: Equipment
items.entry: A set of grease-stained common clothes, a set of tinker's tools, and a credit stick with 1000 credits.

entries.name: Feature: Mechanic Specialty
entries: While you're pretty familiar with a variety of machinery and technologies, you specialize in a certain tradecraft. You may be a member of a union for your trade. You can select your specialty from the table below or roll to select it randomly.

rows: Automotive
Aircraft
Robotics
Manufacturing
Explosives
Electronics
Weapons
Plumber

entries.name: Feature: Grease Monkey
entries: You always know where you can get access to a car garage, a machinist shop, a robotics lab, or other similar facilities. When you work on a machine or vehicle with other mechanics nearby, they will speculate about what's broken, tell you about mistakes you're making, and assist you with the project. You always know where to find the parts needed for vehicle modifications, weapon accessories, and other equipment, no matter how obscure.

entries.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: Mechanics are typically a level-headed bunch willing to get their hands dirty in order to get the job done. They are resourceful, inventive, and capable of approaching problems from different angles.

rows: I see a problem and I immediately want to fix it.
People can't be trusted, not like machines.
I speak in a lot of jargon that most people don't understand.
Like me, my machines have a lot of 'character'.
I speak slowly because there's no need to rush.
A machine's design can always be improved, just like myself.
I'm proud of my work, so I can't help showing off.
I don't mind getting a little dirty, or even a lot.
{@bold Scale.} Always build it bigger, stronger, and more badass. (Chaotic)
{@bold By the Books.} Safety first isn't just a motto, it's a way of life. (Lawful)
{@bold Cooperation.} Together, we can build a better world for all. (Good)
{@bold Automation.} The world would run more smoothly if machines ran everything. (Lawful)
{@bold Determination.} Hard work and a can-do attitude will get you anywhere. (Any)
{@bold Fail Forward.} A catastrophic malfunction is just another opportunity to learn. (Chaotic)
Someone sabotaged a machine I built and caused a disaster.
A family member taught me everything that I know, but they vanished without warning.
A machine I created magically gained sentience, and now is on a rampage. I must stop it.
I'm deep in debt and I won't breathe easy until I'm free of it.
I stole my greatest designs, and I can't risk anyone knowing.
People don't realize it yet, but they need my new invention to perfect their lives.
I approach people and machines in the same way.
When something doesn't work the way it should, I get mad.
I refuse to accept that I may have made a mistake.
I need to break things open to see how they work.
I'm a perfectionist to the extreme.
I refuse to let other people help me, whether I need it or not.

entries: The world is built and run by machines, and the machines are run by you. You are the grease in the vast clockwork that keeps modern society functioning smoothly. Without you, society crumbles to dust. Or someone just hires your replacement. After all, you're just as replaceable as any piece of equipment.

items.name: Equipment:
items.entry: Choose A or B: (A) {@item Healer's Kit|XPHB}, 2 {@item Hypodermic Needle|DarkMatter24|Hypodermic Needles}, {@item Log Keeper|DarkMatter24}, {@item Traveler's Clothes|XPHB} (scrubs), 32 CR; or (B) 50 CR

entries: During your education, you diligently studied xenoanatomy textbooks and learned a dozen different ways to patch up blaster wounds. Perhaps you took a position as a shipboard doctor, a nurse in a megacity trauma center, or as a battlefield medic alongside a mercenary company. You've saved lives by the barest margin and watched others flatline in your arms. One thing is certain: saving others is your life's calling, and plenty of people among the stars need your particular skills.

items.name: Languages:
entries: One of your choice between the standard languages.

items.name: Equipment:
items.entry: A set of {@item fine clothes|phb}, an official identity document, a scroll of pedigree, and a {@item pouch|phb|purse} containing 15 gp

entries.name: Feature: Protector of the Land
entries: Your ancestors have gone to great lengths and fought countless battles to protect these lands from invading humanoids and monsters alike. You know the land and can use it to your benefit. You know the most advantageous positions for combat in the area and you have advantage on checks to find your way when in the wilds of Unified Caldar.

name: Mercenary

_.special: one other pack of your choice

entries: You are a mercenary for hire, a skilled freelancer capable of completing a variety of difficult missions. You've spent a lot of time on such missions and are used to dangerous scenarios. You may specialize in a particular area, such as body guarding, infiltration, or hit jobs, but you'll often take whatever you can get.

items.name: Skill Proficiencies:
items.entry: Two of your choice among {@skill Acrobatics}, {@skill Athletics}, {@skill Intimidation}, {@skill Perception}, {@skill Stealth}, and {@skill Streetwise|ccg}.

items.name: Tool Proficiencies:
items.entry: Any one type of vehicle ({@filter land|vehicles|terrain=land}, {@filter water|vehicles|terrain=sea}, or {@filter air|vehicles|terrain=air}) or {@item thieves' tools|ccg}.

items.name: Gear Packs:
items.entry: {@item Pathfinding gear|ccg} or a set of {@item thieves' tools|ccg}, as well as {@filter one other pack of your choice|items|type=regular gear pack;tool gear pack}.

entries.name: Feature: Freelancer
entries: Through your experience on missions, you've met many others in your line of work. You have connections to other mercenaries and fixers who may aid you with obscure information or recommended you for high paying missions.

items.name: Equipment:
items.entry: Choose A or B: (A) {@item Bandolier|DarkMatter24}, {@item Igniter|DarkMatter24}, {@item Tactical Vest|DarkMatter24}, {@item Traveler's Clothes|XPHB} (fatigues), Utility Axe, 15 CR; or (B) 50 CR

entries: When you were low on Credits or boredom swelled, you learned that you can pick up a blaster and get paid for it. Mercenary work has been your way of life ever since. Most of the time, you stood around in the sweltering heat keeping an eye on things, but very occasionally you got to step into your element: ducking behind cover, exchanging blaster fire, breaking bones, and emerging victorious. Your line of work took you to exotic locales and let you meet exciting people, but it's hardly worth life or limb.

name: Mercenary
entries: The long history of bloody conflict in the Iron Kingdoms has created an endless opportunity for those willing to commit violence for coin. You are a mercenary: a soldier of fortune generally loyal only to whichever paymaster is currently filling your pockets.

entries.name: Feature: The Charter
entries: A long-standing code of conduct called simply "the Charter" defines the rules and strictures under which mercenaries operate. It clarifies how mercenaries are expected to treat employers, civilians, opposing and allied militaries, prisoners, and other mercenary companies. When interacting with other mercenaries or potential employers, you can expect them to understand the Charter's basics and not to impede your fulfillment of a contract unless it actively goes against their interests.

Additionally, you have advantage on Charisma (Persuasion) or Charisma (Intimidation) checks related to haggling over a contract, negotiating with a kingdom's military personnel, or interacting with anyone in a way that directly relates to your fulfillment of a contract.

entries.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: Although mercenaries might seem like nothing more than soldiers for hire, they are often far more complex. Because they are so well traveled, they often lack biases common among soldiers of national militaries.

entries.caption: Personality Trait
rows: I tend to be rather selfish.
Combats and contracts are to be taken seriously; everything else is trivial.
Even though many see me as an unethical mercenary, I hold dear to my faith and its tenets.
I am slow to trust even my comrades in arms.
I live every day as if it might be my last. In this profession, it just might be.
I am deeply dedicated to my martial training.
I enjoy the work of calculating numbers, but only when it comes to making money.
Some have called me a conniver, and they aren't exactly wrong.

entries.caption: Ideal
rows: Gold. I kill people for coin. It's nothing personal. (Neutral)
Might. In battle, I can prove to others how strong I truly am. (Any)
The Charter. I follow my contracts to the letter. If you wanted something else, you should have negotiated better terms. (Lawful)
Protection. Though I fight to get paid, I go out of my way to defend the helpless. (Good)
Freedom. The mercenary life allows me to live how I choose. (Chaotic)
Battle. I feel truly alive only when I'm cutting down someone else. (Evil)

entries.caption: Bond
rows: One of my parents taught me arithmetic. It's turned out to be very important to me, but they aren't exactly pleased with how I use it.
I recently struck out on my own, but my old mercenary company will always be my home.
A retired mercenary taught me the ropes. I still look up to my mentor as a parental figure.
I burned a bridge with a particular mercenary group when I was forced to flee from a fight.
I have become acquainted with a Thamarite cleric who oddly shows up from time to time during my journeys.
I once saved the life of a merchant who hired me as a bodyguard. Now that word has spread, merchants are always trying to hire me for similar jobs.

entries.caption: Flaw
rows: When combat begins to turn in an even slightly unfavorable direction, I am the first to run.
I have become too jaded by the callous nature of those who pay others to fight their battles.
Violence is the only language I truly understand.
If the coin is good, I'm willing to get my hands dirty working jobs that are considered questionable even by those in my profession.
I'm disillusioned with the mercenary life, but I can't afford to walk away.
Battle has scarred me physically and mentally, and I will never be the same again.

name: Mercenary Charter
entries: {@b Adventuring Company.} You and your fellow characters represent a recognized mercenary company with a charter sanctioned by most nations and authorities in the Iron Kingdoms.

entries.name: Prerequisites
entries: Any character can belong to a Mercenary Charter company.

entries.name: Downtime: Guard Duty
entries: Between contracts, you can earn extra funds by keeping watch over a client's property. For each day spent on guard duty, each member receives {@dice 2d4} gp.

entries.name: Company Accomplishments
entries: Prestige increases through acts such as: winning a battle against overwhelming odds; defending a village, stronghold, or military asset; negotiating a favorable contract; acquiring a warjack; destroying a warjack under enemy control; or capturing an enemy commander.

entries.name: Tier 1 – Freelance Fighters
entries: {@b Mercenary Charter.} Your company holds a mercenary charter that outlines conduct, looting, and contract obligations. Common stipulations include: civilians must not come to undue harm; loot is distributed evenly; no obligation to follow laws that violate natural law; 30-day non-compete clause after completing a contract.
{@b Military Supplier.} You can purchase weapons and armor at a 10 percent discount.

{@b Contracts.} Members can hit the streets to gather information about potential contracts (downtime activity, cost: {@dice 1d4} gp per day, takes at least {@dice 1d4} days to find a lead). Tier 1 contracts are worth up to 200 gp.

entries.name: Tier 2 – Soldiers of Fortune
entries: {@b Fresh Recruits.} You gain {@dice 1d10} hirelings (CR 1/4 or lower) to act as privates and support staff.
{@b Garrison.} Your company gains a modest chapter house with a barracks, mechanik's workshop, muster field, smithy, and stables. You can maintain a modest lifestyle there at no expense.

entries.name: Tier 3 – Professional Soldiers
entries: {@b Better Negotiators.} When beginning negotiations for a new contract, one character can barter for improved pay with a Charisma (Persuasion) check (DC 12 + 2 for each 100 gp over standard pay). Success means the extra gold is paid as an advance.
{@b Improved Recruits.} You gain your choice of {@dice 1d10} hirelings (CR 1 or lower) or {@dice 1d4} command staff (CR 2 or lower).

entries.name: Tier 4 – Lords of War
entries: {@b Fearsome Reputations.} You gain a +2 bonus on Charisma (Intimidation) checks involving enemy forces and Charisma (Persuasion) checks involving friendly forces.
{@b Superior Recruits.} You gain your choice of {@dice 1d10} hirelings (CR 2 or lower) or {@dice 1d4} command staff (CR 4 or lower).

_.special: a {@item signet ring|PHB} emblazoned with the symbol of your family's free company,

items.name: Tool Proficiencies:
items.entry: One type of {@filter gaming set|items|source=phb|miscellaneous=mundane|type=gaming set}, one type of {@filter musical instrument|items|source=phb|miscellaneous=mundane|type=instrument}

items.name: Equipment:
items.entry: A {@item backpack|PHB}, a {@item signet ring|PHB} emblazoned with the symbol of your family's free company, a {@filter musical instrument|items|source=phb|miscellaneous=mundane|type=instrument} of your choice, a {@item mess kit|PHB}, a set of {@item traveler's clothes|PHB}, and a belt {@item pouch|PHB} containing 20 gp

entries.name: Mercenary Company Reputation
entries: Your family is part of or associated with a mercenary company. The company has a certain reputation that may or may not continue to impact your life. Roll a {@dice d8} or choose from the options in the Mercenary Company Reputation table to determine the reputation of this free company.

rows: {@bold Infamous.} The company's evil deeds follow any who are known to consort with them.
{@bold Honest.} An upstanding company whose words and oaths are trusted.
{@bold Unknown.} Few know of this company. Its deeds have yet to be written.
{@bold Feared.} For good or ill, this company is generally feared on the battlefield.
{@bold Mocked.} Though it tries hard, the company is the butt of many jokes and derision.
{@bold Specialized.} This company is known for a specific type of skill on or off the battlefield.
{@bold Disliked.} For well-known reasons, this company has a bad reputation.
{@bold Famous.} The company's great feats and accomplishments are known far and wide.

entries.name: Feature: The Family Name
entries: Your family name is well known in the close-knit world of mercenary companies. Members of mercenary companies readily recognize your name and will provide food, drink, and shelter with pleasure or out of fear, depending upon your family's reputation. You can also gain access to friendly military encampments, fortresses, or powerful political figures through your contacts among the mercenaries. Utilizing such connections might require the donation of money, magic items, or a great deal of drink.

entries.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: The turmoil of war, the drudgery of the camp, long days on the road, and the thrill of battle shape a Mercenary Company Scion to create strong bonds of loyalty, military discipline, and a practical mind. Yet this history can scar as well, leaving the scion open to guilt, pride, resentment, and hatred.

rows: I am ashamed of my family's reputation and seek to distance myself from their deeds.
I have seen the world and know people everywhere.
I expect the best life has to offer and won't settle for less.
I know stories from a thousand campaigns and can apply them to any situation..
After too many betrayals, I don't trust anyone.
My parents were heroes, and I try to live up to their example.
I have seen the horrors of war; nothing disturbs me anymore.
I truly believe I have a destiny of glory and fame awaiting me.
{@bold Glory.} Only by fighting for the right causes can I achieve true fame and honor. (Good)
{@bold Dependable.} Once my oath is given, it cannot be broken. (Lawful)
{@bold Seeker.} Life can be short, so I will live it to the fullest before I die. (Chaotic)
{@bold Ruthless.} Only the strong survive. (Evil)
{@bold Mercenary.} If you have gold, I'm your blade. (Neutral)
{@bold Challenge.} Life is a test, and only by meeting life head on can I prove I am worthy. (Any)
My parent's legacy is a tissue of lies. I will never stop until I uncover the truth.
I am the only one who can uphold the family name.
My companions are my life, and I would do anything to protect them.
I will never forget the betrayal leading to my parent's murder, but I will avenge them.
My honor and reputation are all that matter in life.
I betrayed my family to protect my friend who was a soldier in another free company.
I have no respect for those who never signed on to a mercenary company or walked the battlefield.
I cannot bear losing anyone close to me, so I keep everyone at a distance.
Bloody violence is the only way to solve problems.
I caused the downfall of my family's mercenary company.
I am hiding a horrible secret about one of my family's patrons.
I see insults to my honor or reputation in every whisper, veiled glance, and knowing look.

entries: You descend from a famous line of free company veterans, and your first memory is playing among the tents, training yards, and war rooms of one campaign or another. Adored or perhaps ignored by your parents, you spent your formative years learning weapons and armor skills from brave captains, camp discipline from burly sergeants, and a host of virtues and vices from the common foot soldiers. You've always been told you are special and destined to glory. The weight of your family's legacy, honor, or reputation can weigh heavily, inspiring you to great deeds, or it can be a factor you try to leave behind.

_.special: A letter of introduction from an old teacher

items.name: Equipment:
items.entry: A letter of introduction from an old teacher, a {@filter gaming set|items|source=phb|miscellaneous=mundane|type=gaming set} of your choice, {@item traveler's clothes|PHB}, and a {@item pouch|PHB} containing 10 gp

entries.name: Feature: Theoretical Experience
entries: You have an encyclopedic knowledge of stories, myths, and legends of famous soldiers, mercenaries, and generals. Telling these stories can earn you a bed and food for the evening in taverns, inns, and alehouses. Your age or inexperience is endearing, making commoners more comfortable with sharing local rumors, news, and information with you.

entries.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: Recruits are eager to earn their place in the world of mercenaries. Sometimes humble, other times filled with false bravado, they are still untested by the joys and horrors awaiting them. Meaning well and driven to learn, recruits are generally plagued by their own fears, ignorance, and inexperience.

rows: I am thrilled by the thought of an upcoming fight.
Why wait until I'm famous to have songs written about me? I can write my own right now!
I know many stories and legends of famous adventurers and compare everything to these tales.
Humor is how I deal with fear.
I always seek to learn new ways to use my weapons and love sharing my knowledge.
The only way I can prove myself is to work hard and take risks.
When you stop training, you sign your own death notice.
I try to act braver than I actually am.
{@bold Respect.} To be treated with honor and trust, I must honor and trust people first. (Good)
{@bold Discipline.} A good soldier obeys orders. (Lawful)
{@bold Courage.} Sometimes doing the right thing means breaking the law. (Chaotic)
{@bold Excitement.} I live for the thrill of battle, the rush of the duel, and the glory of victory. (Neutral)
{@bold Power.} When I achieve fame and power, no one will give me orders anymore! (Evil)
{@bold Ambition.} I will make something of myself no matter what. (Any)
My first mentor was murdered, and I seek the skills to avenge that crime.
I will become the greatest mercenary warrior ever.
I value the lessons from my teachers and trust them implicitly.
My family has sacrificed much to get me this far. I must repay their faith in me.
I will face any danger to win the respect of my companions.
I have hidden a map to an amazing and powerful magical treasure until I grow strong enough to follow it.
I do not trust easily and question anyone who attempts to give me orders.
I ridicule others to hide my insecurities.
To seem brave and competent, I refuse to allow anyone to doubt my courage.
I survived an attack by a monster as a child, and I have feared that creature ever since.
I have a hard time thinking before I act.
I hide my laziness by tricking others into doing my work for me.

entries: Every year, the hopeful strive to earn a place in one of the great mercenary companies. Some of these would-be heroes received training from a mercenary company but needed more training before gaining membership. Others are full members but were selected to venture abroad to gain more experience before gaining a rank. You are one of these hopeful warriors, just beginning to carve your place in the world with blade, spell, or skill.

items.name: Specialty
entries: Every merchant needs a specialty, and some merchants belong to guilds. Work with your DM to determine the nature of your merchant business, and if you are a member of a merchant guild. You can select your merchant business from the table below or roll randomly.

rows: Alchemists and apothecaries
Armorers, locksmiths, and finesmiths
Brewers, distillers, and vintners
Calligraphers, scribes, and scriveners
Carpenters, roofers, and plasterers
Cartographers, surveyors, and chart-makers
Cobblers and shoemakers
Cooks and bakers
Glassblowers and glaziers
Jewelers and gemcutters
Leatherworkers, skinners, and tanners
Masons and stonecutters
Crabbers and fishmongers
Potters and tile-makers
Shipwrights and sail-makers
Smiths and metal-forgers
Tinkers, pewterers, and casters
Wagon-makers and wheelwrights
Weavers and dyers
Woodcarvers, coopers, and bowyers

items.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: You were apprenticed to a trader, caravan master, or shopkeeper, learning the fundamentals of commerce. You traveled broadly, and you earned a living by buying and selling the raw materials artisans need to practice their craft or finished works from such crafters. You might have transported goods from one place to another (by ship, wagon, or caravan) or bought them from traveling traders and sold them in your own shop.

rows: I inherited the family business, for better or for worse.
I helped a big shot merchant, and they took me in as an apprentice.
One of my family members who belonged to the guild made a place for me (nepotism).
I was always good at sales, so it just made sense.
I truly enjoy analyzing profit and loss statements.
I learned the essentials of my craft from a mentor but had to join a guild to finish my training.
I see trade as an art form, and I'm the artist.
I can't resist sharing stories of my greatest sales or shrewdest deals.
I am distrustful of anyone who doesn't understand the value of a good bargain.
I keep meticulous records of all my transactions, even the smallest ones.
I'm rude to people who lack my commitment to hard work and fair play.
I like to talk at length about my profession.
I don't part with my money easily and will haggle tirelessly to get the best deal possible.
I view every social interaction as a potential business negotiation.
Prosperity. Everyone prospers when trade flows freely. (Good)
Monopoly. The market belongs to those bold enough to seize it. (Evil)
Independence. I thrive on the freedom to make my own way in the world. (Chaotic)
Order. Markets must be regulated to ensure fairness and stability. (Lawful)
Legacy. My name will be remembered as the greatest merchant of all time. (Neutral)
Ambition. Trade is the path to influence and power. (Any)
I will do whatever it takes to protect my most loyal customers and suppliers.
A rival merchant wronged me, and I will see their business crumble.
I owe my guild a great debt for forging me into the person I am today.
I pursue wealth to secure someone's love.
The ledger of my first sale is my most prized possession.
I will get revenge on the evil forces that destroyed my place of business and ruined my livelihood.
I am obsessed with acquiring a specific rare item, no matter the cost..
I cut corners to maximize profit, even if it means skirting the law.
No one must ever learn that I once stole money from guild coffers.
I'm never satisfied with what I have—I always want more.
I would kill to acquire a noble title.
I have trouble trusting people, always suspecting hidden agendas.

name: Metal Healers
entries: Your ancestors were Ironmaster healers of the highest order. Once per day, a success in stabilising someone with a Wisdom ({@skill Medicine}) check can heal {@dice 1d8} + lvl hit points. You need to carry at least 50 cowries worth of metal items with you for this to work.

_.special: an insignia deatiling your rank within a military organization

_.displayName: a hip flask of hard liquor

items.name: Skill Proficiencies
entries: {@skill Intimidation}, Choose one from {@skill Animal Handling}, {@skill Athletics}, {@skill Insight}, {@skill Perception}, {@skill Survival}

items.name: Tool Proficiencies
entries: One type of {@filter gaming set|items|source=phb|miscellaneous=mundane|type=gaming set}

items.name: Equipment
entries: a {@filter gaming set|items|source=phb|miscellaneous=mundane|type=gaming set} you are proficient with, an insignia detailing your rank within a military organization, moleskin gloves, grappling {@item net|phb}, a hip {@item flask|phb} of hard liquor and 10 gp.

Militarists either work within a formal military structure, or fight for pay on an individual basis. Militarists are often respected or feared, depending on the nature of their organisation. High-ranking Militarists are often paid handsomely, as their skills can decide battles or even wars. Lower-level Militarists make great warriors, mercenaries, and guards.
It is not unheard of for militaristic individuals to accompany adventurers on dangerous missions. These tasks are said to keep the mind sharp and skills honed, especially in times of relative peace.

entries.name: Free Sword
entries: Free Swords are commonly referred to as mercenaries, taking jobs that the local forces can't handle. Mercenaries may be the only hope of villages looking for defenders against raiders, overextended sheriffs chasing powerful fugitives, and small merchants traveling Etharis's dangerous byroads. Larger mercenary companies win wars on behalf of cities and kings. They fight for coin above all else, exacting little honor from the contracts they accept.

entries.name: Independant Contractor
entries: Upon spending an hour loitering within a town, and succeeding on a medium DC-Charisma ({@skill Intimidation}) check, your intimidating presence draws offers of employment to you. As long as you are not trying to conceal your presence, jobs befitting a Free Sword Mercenary will find you. You can find mercenary and adventuring jobs only available to Free Sword licence-holders. These jobs typically pay more than a standard contract of their type. Free Sword guilds take a 5% cut as a guild fee.

entries.name: Rank 1 - Hireling
entries: You have been trained in combat by a group of mercenaries with a Free Sword licence. After many tedious years of combat drills and shooting at straw targets, you are close to receiving your very own license.

entries.name: Holdings
entries: Lodging at any Free Sword's guild house and use of Free Sword's training grounds and facilities.
The contract for a dangerous bounty that your mentor died trying to complete.

entries.name: Progression
entries: Complete a contract with a guild member who has a Free Sword licence.

entries.name: Rank 2 - Sellsword
entries: After proving your competence and trustworthiness, you have become a guildlicensed Sellsword. You start to receive specific requests for jobs as your reputation grows.

entries.name: Holdings
entries: A Free Sword licence, which allows you to accept your own contracts as a mercenary and collect the rewards.
Access to hirelings belonging to the Free Swords guild, who you can contract for a small fee.

entries.name: Progression
entries: Lead a team successfully through several highstakes encounters during mercenary contracts.

entries.name: Rank 3 - Sword Commander
entries: You have proven your combat prowess and command of battlefield tactics. Special requests for your services are becoming more frequent, often from people or groups of higher social status. The mercenary companions who accompany you on your jobs have matured into disciplined soldiers who trust you as their commander.

entries.name: Holdings
entries: Your own private room in a guild house and a retainer who can either take care of business for you at the guild house or accompany you on your travels.
Command authority over lower ranks and the power to employ them for jobs.
Access to restricted jobs that depend on sensitive information or extraordinary risk.

entries.name: Progression
entries: Successfully complete a restricted job for a highprofile client.

entries.name: Rank 4 - Battlelord
entries: You have been elected by the members of your Free Swords guild to lead them forward to greater power and acclaim. What type of commander are you going to be? Will you lead by example and rush into the fray during combat, or retire the sword and pick up the pen?

entries.name: Holdings
entries: Command of the Free Sword's guild and its members, including managing contracts, and overseeing the training of hirelings.
A guild chapterhouse, which includes housing for you and your lieutenants as well as an extensive armoury for guild members.

_.special: an insignia deatiling your rank within a military organization

items.name: Skill Proficiencies
entries: {@skill Perception}, Choose one from {@skill Animal Handling}, {@skill Athletics}, {@skill Insight}, {@skill Intimidation}, {@skill Survival}

items.name: Tool Proficiencies
entries: One type of {@filter gaming set|items|source=phb|miscellaneous=mundane|type=gaming set}

items.name: Equipment
entries: a {@filter gaming set|items|source=phb|miscellaneous=mundane|type=gaming set} you are proficient with, an insignia detailing your rank within a military organization, {@item manacles|phb}, pipe and tobacco box, a badge of office, and 10 gp.

Militarists either work within a formal military structure, or fight for pay on an individual basis. Militarists are often respected or feared, depending on the nature of their organisation. High-ranking Militarists are often paid handsomely, as their skills can decide battles or even wars. Lower-level Militarists make great warriors, mercenaries, and guards.
It is not unheard of for militaristic individuals to accompany adventurers on dangerous missions. These tasks are said to keep the mind sharp and skills honed, especially in times of relative peace.

entries.name: Guard
entries: Public officers of the law in cities and large settlements, Guards protect the populace from the dangers both inside and outside the walls. If it looks like guards spend their time loitering and playing cards, its because most of the time the mere presence of a guard is enough to make petty criminals move along. Guards occupy a variety of stations, ranging from lowly bar bouncers to royal men-at-arms who protect the royal family and their most prized possessions.

entries.name: Informant
entries: Upon spending an hour asking around, and succeeding on a medium-DC Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check, you can find a contact within the local constabulary or guard hierarchy. This contact begins as friendly to you and will answer questions you have regarding local wanted criminals, law enforcement, and ongoing or previous investigations.

entries.name: Rank 1 - Town Militia
entries: You have joined the local town militia out of necessity or desire. Either way, your duties have included many sleepless nights on watch, and many tedious days spent idly standing guard.

entries.name: Holdings
entries: A bunk bed to sleep in at your stationed guardhouse.
Sensitive information relating to an unsolved murder that you have not told anyone about.

entries.name: Progression
entries: Solve a crime or uncover a major smuggling route.

entries.name: Rank 2 - Captain of the Watch
entries: Your dedication to your city has not gone unnoticed, and you have been promoted to Captain of the Watch. You now lead a small detail of guards who follow your orders.

entries.name: Holdings
entries: Access to the keys to the city gates.
A group of militia guards to train and organise as you see fit.

entries.name: Progression
entries: Catch a renowned criminal before they can escape the city, or another act worthy of a promotion.

entries.name: Rank 3 - Palace Guard
entries: You have shown initiative and critical thinking under strain in leading your guard detail, and have been suitably promoted to the rank of Palace Guard. Your loyalty is highly valued, and your discretion is even more so.
Your focus has shifted from keeping the peace to protecting the most important places and people in the city.

entries.name: Holdings
entries: Free lodging on the grounds of the palace or other place of work.
Unquestioned access to restricted areas of the city.
Permission to view the casefiles of ongoing investigations and past crimes. You can also access documents detailing guard routes and rosters.

entries.name: Progression
entries: Save a VIP from an assasination attempt, rescue a kidnapped princess, or anything of equal import to be promoted.

entries.name: Rank 4 - Lord Commander
entries: You now command the entire law enforcement system of your area, with accompanying fortresses and militia. You stand as the final authority for most executive and judicial problems in your region, making you the physical embodiment of the law. When the leaders of your city need protection or want a crime investigated, they go through you.

entries.name: Holdings
entries: Command of the entire guard hierarchy within your area, with the authority to conscript new militia and impose martial law within a region or town.
Command of a fortress within a major town or city, granting you access to weapons, defensive siege equipment, and squadrons of guards under your command.
You report directly to the highest officials, and have the ear of the monarch on matters of the city's defences.

_.special: an insignia deatiling your rank within a military organization
letter from your family or loved one

items.name: Skill Proficiencies
entries: {@skill Athletics}, Choose one from {@skill Animal Handling}, {@skill Insight}, {@skill Intimidation}, {@skill Perception}, {@skill Survival}

items.name: Tool Proficiencies
entries: One type of {@filter gaming set|items|source=phb|miscellaneous=mundane|type=gaming set}

items.name: Equipment
entries: a {@filter gaming set|items|source=phb|miscellaneous=mundane|type=gaming set} you are proficient with, an insignia detailing your rank within a military organization, a trophy from your first battle, a letter from your family or a loved one, standard issue soldier's garb, service medallion signifying rank, and 10 gp.

Militarists either work within a formal military structure, or fight for pay on an individual basis. Militarists are often respected or feared, depending on the nature of their organisation. High-ranking Militarists are often paid handsomely, as their skills can decide battles or even wars. Lower-level Militarists make great warriors, mercenaries, and guards.
It is not unheard of for militaristic individuals to accompany adventurers on dangerous missions. These tasks are said to keep the mind sharp and skills honed, especially in times of relative peace.

entries.name: Soldier
entries: Getting into the army isn't the hard part, staying alive is. Every nation and culture has their own notions about what makes a good soldier, and who they look to to fill their ranks.

As a soldier, you don't just know fighting–you know war. Being a soldier involves much more than individual combat prowess. Winning a battle depends on discipline, teamwork, tactics, and a great deal of marching and logistical work that the epics rarely mention.

entries.name: Combat Drills
entries: Upon spending an hour, and succeeding on a medium-DC Strength ({@skill Athletics}) check, you can run training drills and gain an accurate estimate of the drilled humanoids' combat capabilities, as well as any equipment or fortifications they use.
You determine the most suitable strategy to improve their capabilities in the short term as well as the best way to train them for the long term.

entries.name: Rank 1 - Foot Soldier
entries: Many Foot Soldiers are conscripts. Others fight for the honour of their king and country, and still others for the steady paycheck. Regardless of your reason for joining the military, the food was usually warm and the tents kept you dry during the long nights. Your time in the military has taught you the value of the regimented early mornings and working yourself to exhaustion.

entries.name: Holdings
entries: A tent to sleep in and free food when in an encampment of your military.
A letter from a fallen enemy messenger that you either killed or found.

entries.name: Progression
entries: Distinguish yourself. Bring vital information about an enemy encampment or movement that will help win a battle or prevent a defeat. Or perform exceptionally well in battle, turning the tide or capturing an enemy banner.

entries.name: Rank 2 - Sergeant
entries: Your superiors have promoted you to the rank of Sergeant. This brings new challenges in training and commanding the new conscripts who have been assigned to you. How do you train them–on training grounds or in the wilds of Etharis? Or do you let them fend for themselves?

entries.name: Holdings
entries: Command over a small unit of Foot Soldiers.
A valet who attends to your personal needs in the field and relays important messages when required.

entries.name: Progression
entries: Maintain your troops' discipline through multiple skirmishes.

entries.name: Rank 3 - Lieutenant
entries: Several Sergeants have been placed under your command so that you can coordinate their movements in and out of battle. You maintain an air of command about you, and instill confidence in those you command. You have also proven adept with battle tactics, knowing how to read an encounter and when to deploy reserves.

entries.name: Holdings
entries: Command over a brigade of soldiers.
A command tent that serves as your headquarters for battlefield operations.

entries.name: Progression
entries: Decisively win an even battle or win a battle against the odds.

entries.name: Rank 4 - Field Marshal
entries: Your recent promotion to Field Marshal has been foreseen by many and scorned by few. You command whole armies at a time. Whether you are an artist with your masterful maneuvering of battlelines, or utterly brutal in your encounters, none can deny your efficiency in war.

entries.name: Holdings
entries: Command over the region's military.
A seat at any council meetings relevant to military matters of the kingdom.
Residence in a manor close to the training grounds in the capital city.

items.name: Equipment:
items.entry: Choose A or B: (A) 2 {@item Flashlight|DarkMatter24|Flashlights}, {@item Rope|XPHB}, {@item Shovel|XPHB}, {@item Traveler's Clothes|XPHB} (overalls), 25 CR; or (B) 50 CR

entries: Interplanetary mining isn't a job for the faint of heart. You worked long hours, operated antiquated heavy machinery, and dealt with ferocious space creatures. More than one of your former coworkers has been buried underneath tons of rubble when a job went awry. Though you no longer crack open asteroids for a living, you retain every ounce of brawn and persistence that saw you through the work day.

items.name: Equipment
items.entry: A set of miner's tools, a {@item block and tackle}, a {@item climber's kit}, a set of common clothes, and a belt pouch containing 5 gp.

entries.name: Overview
entries: You have spent a great deal of time in the mines of the Underward searching for hidden veins of ore, gems, and mineral wealth. As such, you know well the thrill of following the geologic clues hidden in bands of rock and soil to pockets of precious metals or gemstones. You have also cried tears of frustration when the vein of ore that could make you rich and famous petered out after only a few feet, yielding barely enough wealth to pay for repairing your tools before moving on to search another promising claim.

entries.name: Feature: Rustic Hospitality.
entries: Since you come from the ranks of the common folk, you fit in among them with ease. You can find a place to hide, rest, or recuperate among other commoners, unless you have shown yourself to be a danger to them. They will shield you from the law or anyone else searching for you, though they will not risk their lives for you.

name: Miner
entries: You have spent countless hours in caverns and tunnels, excavating and searching for rare minerals, ores, and gems. You not only know how to identify the most valuable of substances, but you are also familiar with surviving cave-ins and other potential catastrophes.

Your work is simple but rewarding. You're confident in your abilities and your experience sets those around you at ease. Perhaps you always wanted this life, perhaps it's something you learned to love, or maybe you're just waiting for the chance to do something, anything, else.

items.name: Equipment
items.entry: A set of common clothes, a small gem worth 30 gp, a pickaxe, and a pouch containing 10 gp.

entries.name: Feature: Stomecutter's Eye
entries: Your eye for value is useful not only in the mines, but also in your interactions with others. Whenever you interact with others, you know which visible possession that they carry has the most value.

entries.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: The personalities of miners vary widely. Roll or choose one characteristic on each of the following tables.

rows: I can instantly set others at ease with a calm smile and a few simple words.
I like a good working song almost as much as I like a good drinking song.
I whistle when I'm nervous.
I am extremely superstitious.
I have a pet rock... and I'd kill someone if anything happened to it.
I hate being alone.
Unexpected loud noises frighten me.
I always have another mining story to tell.
Camaraderie. My friends are the most important thing in the world to me. (Any)
Safety. Everything I do, I do to keep others safe. (Good)
Wealth. I will find the motherload one day, and when I do, I'll be able to buy anything I want! (Any)
Recognition. I have big ideas, and someday they'll help me revolutionize the industry and gain the recognition I deserve. (Any)
Power. Wealth is the path to power. (Evil)
Tradition. My family has mined the same mountain for generations, and I'm not going to be the one who breaks that chain. (Any)
I found the motherload, but it was blocked off by a cave-in, and I've spent years searching to find it again.
I barely escaped a cave-in with my life, but my best friend wasn't so lucky.
My forefathers were all miners, and they expect me to live and die as one too.
I can't bring myself to enter a particular tunnel where we lost a group of miners a few years back.
I have a rivalry with another miner to see who can consistently find the best valuables.
I can't actually mine very well – I met a friendly creature that I trained to do it for me.
I smuggle liquor into the caves and spend my mining days drunk.
I have no concept of personal hygiene
I pretend the blasting has damaged my hearing so I can eavesdrop on other people's conversations.
In almost every circumstance, I can make an analogy to mining...and they're all terrible.
I spend money as fast as I make it.
I'll go without food or sleep for days when I find a new vein.

name: Monster Hunter
entries: You are an experienced hunter of monsters in the Border Kingdoms, both to eliminate and to capture for clients. You have become familiar with their favored lairs, feeding and watering areas, habits, and territories, and so have a good idea of where to find them. Many Borderers know and repeat tavern-tales about the maraudings and cunning of monsters; you have learned what is truth and what is exaggeration in most of these tellings, and the precautions to take if success—and your survival of a hunt—is to be likely.

items.name: Equipment
items.entry: Herbalism kit, hunting trap, a set of traveler's clothes, and a pouch containing 5 gp

entries.name: The Hunt
entries: You have spent your days mastering the craft of hunting animals and monsters, or pursuing or tracking them with the intent of doing so. Most of your hunting has been for procuring food or to remove predators in your community in which you live. You also have been hired as a guide to track and help kill some of the most dangerous monsters in the Border Kingdoms.

entries.name: Feature: Tracker/Hunter
entries: You are extremely familiar with the flora, fauna, and terrain of the Border Kingdoms. While in the Border Kingdoms, you can automatically identify the tracks of any beasts native to that region; similarly, you can know what foliage is safe to eat in the Border Kingdoms. Finally, given at least an hour in any wilderness setting in the Border Kingdoms, you can complete a successful hunt producing enough to eat for up to five other people each day.

entries.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: Monster hunters are a diverse and colorful group who are experts on the flora and fauna of the wilds of the Border Kingdoms. They tend to be solitary, but not universally so. Their individual motivations can range from conservation to trophy hunting. All Monster Hunters are self reliant and very capable naturalists. Use the tables below, either making specific selections or rolling randomly, as the basis for your traits and motivations, modifying the entries when appropriate to suit your identity.

rows: I will pursue and catch my quarry no matter the cost.
I am privileged to be able to share the beauty of the Border Kingdoms with my clients.
I will not rest until each and every monster in the Border Kingdoms is eliminated.
I love the thrill of the hunt.
I am not one to let property rights and other legalities get in the way of a good hunt.
I am all about getting paid. If you pay me enough, I will get you a kill.
Independence. I am a free spirit—no one tells me how to run a hunt. (Chaotic)
Order. Monsters are a scourge upon us all and must be destroyed. (Lawful)
Safety. Protecting the innocent from the depredations of monsters is the highest calling. (Good)
Pragmatism. When it comes to a hunt, by any means necessary is the only rule. (Chaotic)
Friendship. Material goods come and go. Bonds of friendship last forever. (Good)
Glory. I'm determined to be known as the foremost hunter in the Border Kingdoms (Any)
A close call with an owlbear taught me early on the importance of respecting the dangers in nature.
I was taught everything I know by a salty old trapper and everything I do now honors his memory.
The beauty of the natural world informs everything that I do, and I want to share this understanding with as many folk as possible.
I grew up in a city, but that was not the life for me. Wilderness and the thrill of the hunt is everything to me.
I lost someone very close to me at the claws of a troll. I will do everything in my power to see that this never happens to anyone else.
I made a mistake while taking a client on a hunt resulting in her death. It was my fault and the memory of my failure haunts me everyday.
Once started, I cannot stop a hunt.
I am not interested in coddling anyone's feelings. When on a hunt, my way is the only way.
I am convinced that I am the best, and am not interested in hearing anyone else's views of tactics, techniques, or locales when it comes to a hunt.
I often take unnecessary and foolish risks when on a hunt.
When pursuing a monster, laws were meant to be broken.
Animals and monsters are beneath our deepest contempt and are meant to be killed.

_.special: a trinket from your life before you were adopted
a collection of bones, shells, or other natural objects

items.name: Languages:
items.entry: One language of your choice, typically your adopted parents' language (if any)

items.name: Equipment:
items.entry: A {@item club|PHB}, {@item handaxe|PHB}, or {@item spear|PHB}, a trinket from your life before you were adopted, a set of {@item traveler's clothes|PHB}, a collection of bones, shells, or other natural objects, and a belt {@item pouch|PHB} containing 5 gp

entries.name: Adopted
entries: Prior to becoming an adventurer, you defined your history by the creatures who raised you. Choose a type of creature for your adopted parents or roll a d10 and consult the table below. Work with your GM to determine which specific creature of that type adopted you. If you are of a particular race or species that matches a result on the table, your adopted parent can't be of the same race or species as you, as this background represents an individual raised by a creature or in a culture vastly different or even alien to their birth parents.

rows: Humanoid (such as gnoll, goblin, kobold, or merfolk)
Aberration (such as aboleth, chuul, cloaker, or otyugh)
Beast (such as ape, bear, tyrannosaurus rex, or wolf)
Celestial or fiend (such as balor, bearded devil, couatl, deva, or unicorn)
Dragon (such as dragon turtle, pseudodragon, red dragon, or wyvern)
Elemental (such as efreeti, gargoyle, salamander, or water elemental)
Fey (such as dryad, green hag, satyr, or sprite)
Giant (such as ettin, fire giant, ogre, or troll)
Plant or ooze (such as awakened shrub, gray ooze, shambling mound, or treant)
Monstrosity (such as behir, chimera, griffon, mimic, or minotaur)

entries.name: Feature: Abnormal Demeanor
entries: Your time with your adopted parents taught you an entire lexicon of habits, behaviors, and intuitions suited to life in the wild among creatures of your parents' type. When you are in the same type of terrain your adopted parent inhabits, you can find food and fresh water for yourself and up to five other people each day. In addition, when you encounter a creature like your adopted parent or parents, the creature is disposed to hear your words instead of leaping directly into battle. Mindless or simple creatures might not respond to your overtures, but more intelligent creatures may be willing to treat instead of fight, if you approach them in an appropriate manner. For example, if your adopted parent was a cloaker, when you encounter a cloaker years later, you understand the appropriate words, body language, and motions for approaching the cloaker respectfully and peacefully.

entries.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: When monstrous adoptees leave their adopted parents for the wider world, they often have a hard time adapting. What is common or usual for many humanoids strikes them as surprising, frightening, or infuriating, depending on the individual. Most make an effort to adjust their habits and imitate those around them, but not all. Some lean into their differences, reveling in shocking those around them.

When you choose a creature to be your character's adopted parent, think about how that might affect your character. Was your character treated kindly? Was your character traded by their birth parents to their adopted parents as part of some mysterious bargain? Did your character seek constant escape or do they miss their adopted parents?

rows: I don't eat my friends (at least not while they are alive). My foes, on the other hand ...
Meeting another's gaze is a challenge for dominance that I never fail to answer.
Monsters I understand; people are confusing.
There are two types of creatures in life: prey or not-prey.
I often use the growls, sounds, or calls of my adopted parents instead of words.
Inconsequential items fascinate me.
It's not my fault, I was raised by [insert parent's type here].
I may look fine, but I behave like a monster.
{@bold Wild.} After seeing the wider world, I want to be the monster that strikes fear in the hearts of people. (Evil)
{@bold Insight.} I want to understand the world of my adopted parents. (Neutral)
{@bold Revenge.} I want revenge for my lost childhood. Monsters must die! (Any)
{@bold Harmony.} With my unique perspective and upbringing, I hope to bring understanding between the different creatures of the world. (Good)
{@bold Freedom.} My past away from law-abiding society has shown me the ridiculousness of those laws. (Chaotic)
{@bold Redemption.} I will rise above the cruelty of my adopted parent and embrace the wider world. (Lawful)
I want to experience every single aspect of the world.
I rely on my companions to teach me how to behave appropriately in their society.
I have a "sibling," a child of my adopted parent that was raised alongside me, and now that sibling has been kidnapped!
My monstrous family deserves a place in this world, too.
I'm hiding from my monstrous family. They want me back!
An old enemy of my adopted parents is on my trail.
What? I like my meat raw. Is that so strange?
I like to collect trophies from my defeated foes (ears, teeth, bones, or similar). It's how I keep score.
I usually forget about pesky social conventions like "personal property" or "laws."
I am easily startled by loud noises or bright lights.
I have trouble respecting anyone who can't best me in a fight.
Kindness is for the weak.

entries: Songs and sagas tell of heroes who, as children, were raised by creatures most view as monsters. You were one such child. Found, taken, left, or otherwise given to your monstrous parents, you were raised as one of their own species. Life with your adopted family could not have been easy for you, but the adversity and hardships you experienced only made you stronger. Perhaps you were "rescued" from your adopted family after only a short time with them, or perhaps only now have you realized the truth of your heritage. Maybe you've since learned enough civilized behavior to get by, or perhaps your "monstrous" tendencies are more evident. As you set out to make your way in the world, the time you spent with your adopted parents continues to shape your present and your future.

entries.name: "Monstrous" Parents
entries: This background leans into the fantastical trope of a child raised by wild animals who returns to civilization as an adult. This trope is seen in real-world stories such as Tarzan of the Apes or the founders of Rome, Romulus and Remus, who were said to have been raised by a wolf. This background, its feature, and its suggested characteristics were written with these tropes and a more "monstrous" parent, such as a wolf or griffon, in mind. However, other typically less "monstrous" creatures are also included in the list of possible adoptive parents.

If you play a character raised by a less monstrous parent, some of the suggested characteristics might not be applicable to your character. You can use these suggested characteristics as written, adjust them to fit your character, or use them as inspiration for writing your own characteristics unique to your character.

items.name: Tool Proficiencies
items.entry: Choose two from among {@item navigator's tools|PHB}, {@item poisoner's kit|PHB}, and {@item weaver's tools|PHB}

items.name: Equipment
items.entry: A {@item riding saddle|PHB}, 10 days of animal feed, a pair of goggles, a set of {@item traveler's clothes|PHB}, and a belt pouch containing 10 gp

entries.name: Feature: Eiganjo Moth
entries: Over the years, you have befriended an {@creature imperial moth|PS-Kg}. The moth acts independently of you, but regards you as an ally. If you are incapacitated or absent, the moth flees. If the moth dies, you have advantage on any Wisdom (Animal Handling) or Charisma check you make to befriend another {@creature imperial moth|PS-Kg}.

You have been given the training of the Eiganjo Mothriders, who tamed the Imperial Moths and use them as mounts. Perhaps you uphold the tenets of the Empire, or perhaps you and your moth have ridden to other lands to seek your own path.

items.name: Tool Proficiencies:
items.entry: One type of artistic {@filter artisan's tools|items|source=phb|miscellaneous=mundane|type=artisan's tools} and one {@filter musical instrument|items|source=phb|miscellaneous=mundane|type=instrument}

items.name: Equipment:
items.entry: One set of {@filter artisan's tools|items|source=phb|miscellaneous=mundane|type=artisan's tools} or {@filter musical instrument|items|source=phb|miscellaneous=mundane|type=instrument}, a set of {@item fine clothes|phb}, and a purse containing 10 gp

entries.name: Lifestyle
entries: Wealthy

entries.name: Overview
entries: From your hilltop home, you have looked down (literally and perhaps figuratively) on the unwashed masses of Mulmaster for your entire life. Your fur-trimmed robes and training in the visual and performing arts mark you as wealthy and perhaps well-born; you are a member of the City of Danger's aristocracy. None of your immediate family members sits on the Council of Blades or is even a Zor or Zora...yet. Nevertheless, you are one of Mulmaster's elite, and whether you personally covet a higher standing or not, you are at home in the dance halls where the aristocracy gathers to plot, to scheme, to do business, to discuss the arts, and, above all, to see, and to be seen.

entries.name: Feature: Highborn
entries: Mulmaster is run by and for its aristocracy. Every other class of citizen in the city defers to you, and even the priesthood, Soldiery, Hawks, and Cloaks treat you with deference. Other aristocrats and nobles accept you in their circles and likely know you or of you. Your connections can get you the ear of a Zor or Zora under the right circumstances. Note: This feature is a variant of the Noble feature.

rows: My ambitions are boundless. I will be a Zor or Zora one day!
I must always look my best.
Beauty is everywhere. I can find it in even the homeliest person and the most horrible tragedy.
Decorum must be preserved at all costs.
I will not admit I am wrong if I can avoid it.
I am extremely well-educated and frequently remind others of that fact.
I take what I can today, because I do not know what tomorrow holds.
My life is full of dance, song, drink, and love.
Generous. I have a responsibility to help and protect the less fortunate. (Good)
Loyal. My word, once given, is my bond. (Lawful)
Callous. I am unconcerned with any negative effects my actions may have on the lives and fortunes of others. (Evil)
Impulsive. I follow my heart. (Chaotic)
Ignorant. Explanations bore me. (Neutral)
Isolationist. I am concerned with the fortunes of my friends and family. Others must see to themselves. (Any)
I have dedicated my wealth and my talents to the service of one of the city's many temples.
My family and I are loyal supporters of High Blade Jaseen Drakehorn. Our fortunes are inexorably tied to hers. I would do anything to support her.
Like many families who were close to High Blade Selfaril Uoumdolphin, mine has suffered greatly since his fall. We honor his memory in secret.
My family plotted with Rassendyll Uoumdolphin brother usurped brother as High Blade. Betrayal is the quickest route to power.
Wealth and power are nothing. Fulfillment can only be found in artistic expression.
It's not how you feel, who you know, or what you can do - it's how you look, and I look fabulous.
I have difficulty caring about anyone or anything other than myself.
Having grown up with wealth, I am careless with my finances. I overspend and am overly generous.
The ends (my advancement) justify any means.
I must have what I want and will brook no delay.
My family has lost everything. I must keep up appearances, lest we become a laughingstock.
I have no artistic sense. I hide that fact behind extreme opinions and have become a trendsetter.

name: Mummer
entries: You never performed for fame. You had no expectation of riches. It was enough to get a few coins to pay for a hot meal and a roof over your head. You travelled for a time in the company of a group of mummers, donning your shabby costumes and carrying on your silly plays to entertain the masses. Sometimes you played the valiant knight, sometimes you played the ferocious dragon, and sometimes you played the quack doctor come to revive the loser with a magic potion.

items.name: Tool Proficiencies
items.entry: Disguise kit, one type of musical instrument

items.name: Equipment
items.entry: A set of colorful but shabby clothes, a disguise kit, a (fake) potion of healing, a purse containing 10gp.

entries.name: Feature: Playing The Fool
entries: You've entertained nobles and peasants alike, and you're quite used to coming off as a silly, unimportant street performer. People don't often ask why a mummer is where they are. You're less likely to be held in suspicion for where you travel, showing up at events, or wandering around, as long as you carry on the act and remain in costume. People may still become suspicious or hostile if they find you in an area that should be absolutely off limits to you (a room that was locked or heavily guarded, etc). You may extend this feature to a group accompanying you, as long as they are also disguised as mummers.

entries.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: Mummers are performers at their core, however, they are generally very relaxed about their arts. A mummer is accustomed to street shows or even door-to-door performances, and receiving pocket change or maybe a mug of something hot on a cold night. The mummer performs for the love of the art, not for accolades. That's not to same some don't hold greater expectations, but generally they are more modest folk.

rows: I grew up on stories of heroes fighting villains. It's my dream to live a life that someday, someone else will be performing a play of.
I'm a carefree and lighthearted sort of person, and I worry very little over mistakes I make. If things go poorly today, tomorrow is just a do-over!
I love nothing more than a good pun, even if some people believe there's no such thing as a good pun.
Slapstick comedy is my forte, and I'm always willing to take a pratfall if it puts a smile on someone's face or lightens a heavy mood.
I love learning new stories, and will ask locals any time I arrive somewhere new.
I don't care if it's "just a silly play", I settle for nothing less than perfection.
Some call it compulsive lying. I call it creative storytelling.

Some people say I ramble, or I never get around to the point. Well I say, sometimes you slay the dragon, and sometimes the dragon slays you, but at least there's always a helpful quack to pick you back up. I don't know where I was going with this analogy, but you get the drift!
Fantasy. When I'm performing, I take people away to a better, maybe more simple world, if only for a little while. (Good)
Tradition. It's my duty as a mummer to preserve our stories and the way we tell them for future generations. (Lawful)
Escapism. Performing in disguise lets me be anybody but myself. (Neutral)
Pride. Nothing feels better than knowing all eyes in the room are on me, and people are hanging on my every word. (Any)
Temptation. I'm granted a lot of leeway as a mummer, and I love pushing to see just how much I can get away with. (Chaotic)
Unaccountable. As long as I can change my mask or makeup, I don't see why I can't get away with anything. (Evil)
As a child, I was saved by a healer. I've spent years parading as the quack doctor in our plays, but truthfully, I idolize people who heal the sick and dying.
My troupe and I started as impoverished children, performing door-to-door for spare change or food to survive. I have a soft spot for the poor, especially kids.
Whilst performing at a party of rich people, I accidentally insulted a powerful noble. I just hope they have no idea who was under the mask...
I performed at a wedding that went awry when only one of the lovebirds showed up at the altar. I fell in love that day with the heartbroken bride/groom, but they have no idea I exist.
My mentor taught me everything I know about being a mummer. I'd give anything to find them and show them what I have become.
Knowing a mummer's life is generally a poor one, I made a promise to someone that I'd become rich and famous to win their heart. I just hope they'll wait for me.
Just because I'm a mummer doesn't mean I'm not a {@i serious thespian}.
I have no sense of when it's time to be serious.
My time in mummers plays has lead me to believe 'playing dead' is a worthwhile strategy in any losing situation... or even a merely uncomfortable one.
I have absolutely dreadful stage fright, and I can't speak in front of a crowd if I don't have a mask on.
I refuse to be seen without my makeup unless in the most dire of circumstances, and I wouldn't be caught dead in public without my face on.
I'll try to make a rhyme out of anything. {@i Anything}
