entries: You have made a pact with a devilish entity, willingly exchanging a piece of your soul for otherworldly power. As a Pactbound Agent, you are both servant and wielder of infernal magic. Your pact has granted you a unique set of skills and a connection to the depths of Hell.

entries.name: Feature: Infernal Pact
entries: You have forged a pact with a devilish entity, granting you access to infernal magic and providing you with a warlock spellcasting ability. The entity you made the pact with might be a powerful devil, an infernal archfiend, or a cunning fiendish entity. Consult your Dungeon Master to determine the specifics of your pact.

entries.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: Pactbound Agents are complex individuals, torn between their desire for power and the consequences of their pact. They often possess a dark charisma, using their charm and infernal magic to deceive others.

rows: I have an unsettling aura that unnerves those around me.
I speak in hushed whispers, as if constantly sharing secrets.
I have a fiendish sense of humor, finding amusement in the suffering of others.
I always seem to have a mysterious and captivating smile.
I am fascinated by the occult and enjoy discussing infernal lore.
I have an uncanny ability to blend into shadows and go unnoticed.
I find solace in solitude and often contemplate the nature of my pact.
I exude an air of confidence and superiority, looking down on those who are weaker.
{@b Power.} I seek to increase my own power and influence through my infernal pact.
{@b Knowledge.} I strive to uncover hidden secrets and forbidden knowledge.
{@b Ambition.} I have grand ambitions and will stop at nothing to achieve them.
{@b Freedom.} I yearn to break free from the shackles of my pact and regain my independence.
{@b Revenge.} I seek vengeance against those who wronged me, using my infernal powers to exact my retribution.
{@b Corruption.} I am drawn to the darker aspects of my pact, embracing the temptations of evil.
I made my pact to protect someone I hold dear, and I will do anything to keep them safe.
My infernal patron holds a piece of my soul, and I must complete certain tasks to regain my freedom.
I seek to uncover the truth behind my patron's hidden agenda and the true nature of our pact.
I owe a life debt to a powerful devil or fiend, and I am bound to fulfill their commands.
My pact is a means to an end, a stepping stone toward achieving a greater goal or fulfilling a prophecy.
I am part of an infernal organization that wields influence and power, and I am loyal to their cause.
I am constantly tempted to use my infernal powers for personal gain, regardless of the consequences.
I am haunted by the screams and torments of those whose souls have been damned by my patron.
I find it difficult to trust others, believing that everyone has their own hidden agenda.
I am paranoid that my patron will discover a way to claim my soul entirely and condemn me to eternal torment.
I have a crippling fear of the consequences that await me when my pact comes to an end.
I am unable to resist the allure of forbidden knowledge and will risk everything to acquire it.

name: Palaeontologist

_.special: plaster of Paris with medical bandages
a fist-sized fossil (bone fragment, claw, skull, ammonite, or trilobite)

items.name: Tool Proficiencies
items.entry: Mason's tools, Cartographer's tools, and Research Scrolls

items.name: Equipment
items.entry: A shovel, a miner's pick, a brush, plaster of Paris with medical bandages, a fist-sized fossil (bone fragment, claw, skull, ammonite, or trilobite), a traveller's {@item backpack|phb}, a tankard, and 20 gp in coins

entries: Palaeontologists are those who have dedicated a portion of their lives to the study of ancient organisms and environments. They are able to interpret how creatures may behave, based on their morphology.

entries.name: Feature: Natural Historian
entries: You have advantage on History checks that involve animals or the natural world.

entries.name: Feature: Hazard Training
entries: You are acutely aware of geological hazards and have proficiency on saving throws against geological hazards (i.e. falling from cliffs, escaping landslides, cave-ins, etc.).

entries.name: Palaeontological Specialism
entries: In addition to being a general palaeontologist, you also specialise in one particular area of palaeontology. Roll a {@dice d6} and consult the table below or choose whichever you find most appealing.

rows: Theropoda
You can instantly recognise if a beast is carnivorous and likely to be hostile to you if you approach it further.
Cladistics
You can tell if a beast has been unnaturally altered or is not behaving of its own accord.
Ornithischia
Years of studying herbivores has given you insight into their behaviour. You can tell if they're likely to be hostile when approached.
Palaeobotany
You are able to recognise if a plant or plant-based creature may be dangerous.
Arthropoda
You can tell if large arthropods (i.e. giant spiders, giant scorpions, giant crabs etc.) inhabit an area.
Taphonomy
When encountering a carcass, you can easily tell how long the creature has been dead for.

entries.name: Suggested Starting Feat and Ability Scores
entries: If you use your background to determine your ability score increases and provide a starting feat, we recommend the following:

items: {@bold Feat:} {@feat Naturalist|DrDhrolinsDictionaryofDinosaurs} or {@feat Miner|DrDhrolinsDictionaryofDinosaurs}.
{@bold Ability Scores:} +1 Wisdom, +1 Intelligence, +1 Constitution.

entries.name: Suggested Tool: Research Scrolls
entries: {@i Uncommon, 50 gp, 2 lb.} A collection of research scrolls on your chosen topic. When using these scrolls, select one skill from History, Arcana, Nature, or Religion. If you spend 10 minutes studying the scrolls, you gain temporary proficiency in the selected skill (or expertise if you are already proficient) for the next 6 hours. If you already have expertise in that skill, these do not provide any benefit.

entries.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: Palaeontologists come in many varieties. Below are some suggestions for traits, ideals, bonds, and flaws that a palaeontologist may have.

entries.caption: Personality Traits
rows: I talk about fossils all the time, much to the annoyance of my friends.
I like to watch modern animal behaviour to learn how ancient animals behaved.
I'm always looking at the ground in front of me, just in case I spot a fossil.
I sometimes find myself staring into the distance, imagining what this area may have looked like millions of years ago.
Whenever we visit a city, the museum is the first place I want to go.
I love to doodle sketches of dinosaurs.
I keep fossils as jewellery and wear them all the time.
Whenever I meet a new creature, I'm always trying to figure out its place in the tree of life.

entries.caption: Ideals
rows: I see myself as a 'Gentleman Scientist'. Studying these ancient creatures is a pastime that should be reserved for the academic elite.
Anyone with a trowel and the right attitude can do it! Let's get in the dirt.
There are wonders in our past that few people know about – I want to show them to everyone!
I'm a big fossil fan. Big teeth and big claws are what matter to me.
I want to be the name behind an awesome dinosaur.
I'm a fossil dealer. These fossils have great value, and I can make my living selling them, even if it has to be done shadily.

entries.caption: Bonds
rows: Theropoda. Sharp-toothed predatory dinosaurs excite you the most.
Sauropoda. Giant long-necked dinosaurs excite you the most.
Thyreophora. Heavily armoured dinosaurs excite you the most.
Marginocephalian. Crested and horned dinosaurs excite you the most.
Pterosauria. Flying reptiles excite you the most.
Sauropterygia. Marine reptiles excite you the most.

entries.caption: Flaws
rows: I'm a Splitter. Whenever I meet a non-humanoid creature, I always assume it's a new species and am wary of new abilities and behaviours it might have.
I'm a Lumper. I often assume that groups of similar beasts will all behave in the same way.
I'm overly experimental, setting up little vials of acid with rocks sizzling in them wherever I rest.
I have a clumsy swing. I'm prone to hurting myself when trying to smash rocks.
I'm a bit vacant. My head is so stuck in the past that I often lose interest in conversation and daydream about ancient worlds.
I'm jaded. I've seen so many bones and carcasses that the sight of a dead body doesn't bother me in the slightest.

_: A {@item Combat Wheelchair|CombatWheelchair} (a gift to you when you first started training and participating in wheelchair sports), 5 sticks of {@item chalk (1 piece)|PHB|chalk} (for drying out your palms for grip), {@item costume clothes|PHB} (essentially a sports uniform), {@item Tinker's Tools|PHB}, {@item common clothes|PHB}, and a {@item pouch|phb} containing 15 gp.

_.special: costume clothes which function as a sports uniform

items.name: Equipment
items.entry: A {@object Combat Wheelchair|CombatWheelchair} (a gift to you when you first started training and participating in wheelchair sports), 5 sticks of {@item chalk (1 piece)|PHB|chalk} (for drying out your palms for grip), {@item costume clothes|PHB} (essentially a sports uniform), {@item Tinker's Tools|PHB}, {@item common clothes|PHB}, and a {@item pouch|phb} containing 15 gp.

entries.name: Feature: Sportsmanship
entries: As a paralympian, you are an impressive athlete in your favoured sport (murderball, WCX-ing, etc.) and you can teach others the rules and play of this chosen sport without having to make any checks to do so. You and your adventuring companions can expect to be able to get a match of your favoured sport together so long as there are 10 or more willing humanoids in the area, your party is included in this number. Depending on the type of sport, the opposing teams involved make contesting Athletics or Acrobatics checks (for example, murderball requires an Athletics check, whereas WCX requires an Acrobatics check), adding only the bonus from the character with the highest score from each team involved. The team with the highest score wins.

You might also have ties to a specific team within your favoured sport and you know you have a space and friends there. This could be your birthplace's team, so long as you remain on good terms with the members, or a team you found yourself joining whilst off touring the Realms to play either professionally or casually. Whilst near your team's town/city/village of residence, you can seek out and call upon your team for assistance. Providing the assistance you ask for is non-hazardous and that you remain in good standing with the team, they will come to your aid.

entries.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: Paralympians are often shaped by their experiences from working in a team and the outcome of tournaments or matches they participated in. Their close relationships with people and the study of tactics both on and off the pitch affect their mannerisms and ideals. Their flaws, as is common sometimes with athletes, are often based around overconfidence or not having enough of it to begin with.

rows: I idolize a particular hero within my sport, and constantly talk about refer to them whenever it is relevant in conversation.
I often think in terms of tactics when it comes to combat, years of sports training having rubbed off on me. I'm able to think quickly and find new approaches when others fail.

I am supportive and encouraging of my party - they are my new 'team' now after all! I often have a few words of wisdom or a personal experience of securing a win when all else seems lost and use these to give my friends pep talks.
More often than not, I have an optimistic attitude. I can do anything I put my mind to, especially with my friends beside me!
I talk in terms of sports a lot, even if it doesn't always fit the conversation.
I'm great at giving inspiring speeches - I've had to give a lot of them during my career.
I am patient (or impatient) when explaining the rules of my favoured sport.
I firmly believe that my plans of attack/tactics are the best (or the worst).
By the books. The rulings and my experience in games have given me the opinion that fairness is key. I try to never fight or play dirty. (Lawful)
Patience. Anyone can learn with time and dedication. The win comes to those who wait and help their teammates. (Good)
Rule breaker. The rules are more what you'd call guidelines. I'm not above hitting below the belt to secure a win. The trick is to never get caught. (Chaotic)
Perseverance. Failure is the greatest teacher. Learn from your mistakes and keep getting back up to try again. Eventually you will prevail. (Lawful)
Team worker. I know the value of working together. When I'm with my party, anything is achievable. (Lawful)
Aspiration. I want to be the best paralympian and adventurer in the Realms. I will do whatever it takes to achieve my dream. (Any)
My sports team members are very dear to me and I would do anything for them.
I will one day get revenge on a sports rival I had during my career who I caught cheating but no one believed me.
I owe a favour to an old teammate who gave me courage and inspiration when I needed it most.
I will do anything for my party who I now consider to be my new team. I care deeply for them.
I was falsely accused of cheating in my past and it tarnished my career. I will do anything to clear my name.
I seek to teach others about my sport, especially if they use wheelchairs too.
I am sometimes a bit overconfident (or have no confidence at all) in my tactical approach to things.
Sometimes it's my way or no way at all.
I am overly competitive which can come back to bite me at the worst of times.
I am liable to make an intense rivalry in any competitive situation.
Sometimes I try to give out advice, even when it isn't welcome or particularly useful.
Once I become fixed on a potential win or success, I will pursue it no matter the cost.

entries: You have spent the past however many years of your life as a wheelchair athlete, specialising in a sport of your choice (e.g. murderball, WCX, basketball, etc.) You have travelled all over the Realms participating in professional or casual sporting events and, as a result have picked up a couple of languages of your choice along the way. You are not necessarily a rogue, but you have honed your skills in using your wheelchair in impressive feats of acrobatics and athletics.

Choose a sport (you can even research the many different types of wheelchair sports online) and work with your DM to detail how the game looks or any additional fun rulings it may have in your setting - perhaps cantrips are permitted during play, or everyone must play in an Anti-Magic Field to prevent any cheating, get creative with it! You can also choose what position you played in. Were you a goalkeeper? Or were you centre right field? Perhaps you were centre attack or were the kind of player generally skilled to play in any position.

_.special: a leather satchel containing perfume recipes, research notes, and chemical and botanical samples

items.name: Equipment:
items.entry: {@item Herbalism kit|PHB}, a leather satchel containing perfume recipes, research notes, and chemical and botanical samples; {@dice 1d4} metal or crystal (shatter-proof) perfume bottles, a set of {@item fine clothes|PHB}, and a {@item pouch|PHB|silk purse} containing 10 gp

entries.name: Feature: Aromas and Odors and Airs, Oh My
entries: Before you became an adventurer, you crafted perfumes for customers in your home town or city. When not out adventuring, you can fall back on that trade to make a living. For each week you spend practicing your profession, you can craft one of the following at half the normal cost in time and resources: 5 samples of fine perfume worth 10 gp each, 2 {@item Acid (vial)|PHB|vials of acid}, or 1 vial of parfum toxique worth 50 gp. As an action, you can throw a vial of parfum toxique up to 20 feet, shattering it on impact. Make a ranged attack against a creature or object, treating the parfum as an improvised weapon. On a hit, the target takes {@damage 1d6} poison damage and is {@condition poisoned} until the end of its next turn.

entries.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: As with many parfumiers with the extensive training you received, you are well spoken, stately of bearing, and possessed of a self-assuredness that sometimes is found imposing. You are not easily impressed and rarely subscribe to notions like "insurmountable" or "unavoidable." Every problem has a solution.

rows: I do not deal in absolutes. There is a solution to every problem, an answer for every riddle.
I am used to associating with educated and "elevated" society. I find rough living and rough manners unpalatable.
Years spent witnessing the dealings, intrigues, and industrial espionage of the Bouquet Districts' mercantile-elite have left me secretive and guarded.
I have a strong interest and sense for fashion and current trends.
I eagerly discuss the minutiae, subtleties, and nuances of my profession to any who will listen.
I am easily distracted by unusual or exceptional botanical specimens.
I can seem distant and introverted. I listen more than I speak.
I always strive to make allies, not enemies.
{@bold Responsibility.} It is my duty to share my exceptional gifts and knowledge for the betterment of all. (Good)
{@bold Pragmatism.} I never let passion, preference, or emotion influence my decision-making or clear headedness. (Lawful)
{@bold Freedom.} Rules, particularly those imposed by others, were meant to be broken. (Chaotic)
{@bold Deep Science.} I live a life based on facts, logic, probability, and common sense. (Lawful)
{@bold Notoriety.} I will do whatever it takes to become the elite that I was witness to during my time among the boutiques, salons, and workshops of the noble's district. (Any)
{@bold Profit.} I will utilize my talents to harvest, synthesize, concoct, and brew almost anything for almost anyone. As long as the profit margin is right. (Evil)
I will return to my home city someday and have revenge upon the elitist perfume consortium and corrupt shipping magnates who drove my dreams to ruin.
I have been experimenting and searching my whole career for the ultimate aromatic aphrodisiac. The "alchemists' stone" of perfumery.
My home is safely far behind me now. With it go the unfounded accusations, spiteful rumors, and perhaps some potential links to a string of corporate assassinations.
I am cataloging an encyclopedia of flora and their various chemical, magical, and alchemical properties and applications. It is my life's work.
I am dedicated to my craft, always seeking to expand my knowledge and hone my skills in the science and business of aromatics.
I have a loved one who is threatened (held hostage?) by an organized gang of vicious halfling thugs who control many of the "rackets" in the perfumeries in my home city.
I am driven to reclaim the status and respect of the socially and scientifically elite and will sacrifice much to gain it.
I am highly competitive and not above plagiarizing or stealing the occasional recipe, idea, formula, or sample.
I am hard-pressed to treat anyone who is not (by my standards) "well schooled" or "well heeled" as little more than lab assistants and house servants.
A pretty face is always able to lead me astray.
I am secretly addicted to a special perfume that only I can reproduce.

On a stormy night, I heard a voice in the wind, which led me to a mysterious plant. Its scent was intoxicating, and I consumed it. Now, that voice occasionally whispers in my dreams, urging me to some unknown destiny.

entries: You are educated and ambitious. You spent your youth apprenticed among a city's more reputable greenhouses, laboratories, and perfumeries. There, you studied botany and chemistry and explored properties and interactions with fine crystal, rare metals, and magic. You quickly mastered the skills to identify and process rare and complex botanical and alchemical samples and the proper extractions and infusions of essential oils, pollens, and other fragrant chemical compounds—natural or otherwise.

Not all (dramatic) changes to one's lifestyle, calling, or ambitions are a result of social or financial decline. Some are simply decided upon. Regardless of your motivation or incentive for change, you have accepted that a comfortable life of research, science and business is — at least for now — a part of your past.

a.special: a begging bowl for collecting coins

b.special: a tin cup for collecting coins

items.name: Skill Proficiency
entries: {@skill Persuasion}, choose one from {@skill Deception}, {@skill Insight}, {@skill Perception}, {@skill Stealth}, or {@skill Survival}.

items.name: Languages
entries: Choose one standard language.

items.name: Tool Proficiency
entries: Choose one {@filter gaming set|items|source=phb|miscellaneous=mundane|type=gaming set}

items.name: Equipment
entries: A worn {@item blanket|phb}, a set of ragged clothing, a {@item sack|phb}, a begging bowl or tin cup for collecting coins, a crutch, spare scraps of cloth, and a small stick of grease paint and 10 copper pieces.

entries.name: Friends in Low Places
entries: Upon spending an hour speaking to other beggars and making a DC 10 Charisma ({@skill Persuasion}) check, you can manipulate the underground currents of information that flow throughout the city. This allows you to manipulate the mood of the lower classes for or against a specific individual, group, or decision. The unrest caused may manifest itself in a number of ways, at the GM's discretion.

entries.name: Rank 1 - Street Beggar
entries: Driven by desperation, you are forced to the streets to earn what you need to survive. Poor decisions or bad luck drained away whatever funds you managed to scrape together, and you have no real home to return to. As an adventurer you have certain alternatives not available to most, but between forays into the wilds the fact remains that you have no steady occupation and no place to call home.

items: A spot in an alley that you have managed to stake out and must defend against newcomers.
The name of a sympathetic merchant with space in a high-traffic area of the city.

entries.name: Progression
entries: Gain the friendship of a local business owner by performing odd jobs or doing some other service.

entries.name: Rank 2 - Mendicant
entries: A common sight to locals, you have moved up to a better location in a busy street or plaza. You no longer have to fight for your place and have gained the tolerance of the guards and the friendship of other local beggars. By this time you have established a begging "pitch" designed to attract attention without inconveniencing those passing by. This could be a persona or some sort of script that you devise in order to amuse or elicit sympathy from the general populace.

items: A safe place to sleep near a merchant stall or building.
Friendship with local beggars and a few local traders, who may offer you some spare coin, food, or odd jobs from time to time.

entries.name: Progression
entries: Split a significant windfall with other beggars, earning their loyalty.

entries.name: Rank 3 - Gutter Baron
entries: You have risen to a position of prominence, such as it is, among the beggars in your city. You are able to direct the actions of a number of other paupers and split the rewards in a far more efficient manner than they could do alone, and they respect and defer to you in important decisions.

items: Squatter's rights in an abandoned building.
A handful of other beggars who defer to your authority and aid you in gathering money and information.
Knowledge of an illicit deal that took place in an alley in the dead of night, which implicates a minor noble.

entries.name: Progression
entries: Perform a great service for the poor of the city either by thwarting the plans of a ranking noble or leveraging your influence to gain a powerful aristocrat patron.

entries.name: Rank 4 - Beggar King
entries: You have become the undisputed master of the city's destitute population, and none of them act without your knowledge. Having control of such a wide-ranging network of informants and agents puts you at the center of the city's political power struggles. Even leaders of criminal organizations know that you are not someone to be trifled with.

items: A comfortable hideout hidden in the slums or sewers.
A network of beggars, informants, and criminals that keep you informed of all illicit activity within the city.
Influence with at least one major player in local crime or politics.

entries: Any structured society has those who fall through the cracks. Misfortune is no stranger to Etharis, and those who suffer under its hand have to make do any way they can. Some attempt to survive by begging or turning their hands to whatever jobs they can find, while others are cast out to wander from place to place through the unforgiving wilds.

This background is a good fit for characters who want to use adventuring as a way to escape their unfortunate circumstances or for those who possess character flaws relating to debt or misfortune. Their views on wealth and material goods are undoubtedly a primary feature of their adventuring career.

_.special: a pair of tough leather gloves

items.name: Skill Proficiency
entries: {@skill Intimidation}, choose one from {@skill Deception}, {@skill Insight}, {@skill Perception}, {@skill Persuasion}, {@skill Stealth}, or {@skill Survival}.

items.name: Languages
entries: Choose one standard language.

items.name: Tool Proficiency
entries: Choose one {@filter gaming set|items|source=phb|miscellaneous=mundane|type=gaming set}

items.name: Equipment
entries: A worn {@item blanket|phb}, a set of ragged clothing, a {@item sack|phb}, a pair of tough leather gloves, one {@filter gaming set|items|source=phb|miscellaneous=mundane|type=gaming set} of your choice, a {@item mess kit|phb} and 10 copper pieces.

entries.name: Street Tough
entries: While you are in a large town or city, you may spend an hour and make a DC 10 Charisma ({@skill Intimidation}) check. If you do, your tough demeanor and familiarity with the Fighter's Guild attracts attention from the local members. You learn the location of any underground prize-fighting rings, guild friendly businesses, and the names of upper-class arena patrons. You also learn of any minor jobs being offered to street toughs, such as bodyguard positions or debt collection.

entries.name: Rank 1 - Scrapper
entries: Life on the streets has toughened you, and now you have started down the path of an illegal underground fighter. You have yet to make a name for yourself, but your training is starting to pay off. All you need is a chance to prove yourself.

items: Room and board at a guildhouse near an underground arena.
An invitation to an exhibition match that will be attended by promoters and scouts for the Fighter's Guild.

entries.name: Progression
entries: Attract the notice of a patron among the various underground fight handlers of the Guild.

entries.name: Rank 2 - Prize Fighter
entries: You've made your debut and are now a part of the Fighter's Guild. As part of a small stable of up-and-coming fighters, you are mostly booked for minor tournaments and as warmups for some of the bigger names in arena fighting.

items: A mentor in the form of a handler, trainer, or promoter who helps organize and book your fights.
Access to a small training area equipped with dummies and frequented by potential sparring partners.

entries.name: Progression
entries: Enter a fight with a high-ranked fighter and either last three rounds or knock your opponent out.

entries.name: Rank 3 - Contender
entries: Recognized as one of the most promising fighters in the Guild, you are now eligible for entry into major tournaments for ever-increasing amounts of prize money. Most of the money goes to your handlers, but your standard of living has increased dramatically along with your value.

items: A private room at a high quality inn or other establishment.
Several admirers among the arena patrons, willing to ingratiate themselves with gifts or bribes.

entries.name: Progression
entries: Win a major championship bout.

entries.name: Rank 4 - Arena Champ
entries: Being champion of an underground tournament makes you a major figure within the Fighter's Guild. As your fights draw greater and greater crowds, your duties are lessened and you live in relative luxury. Admired by some, envied by others, you nevertheless command respect among those in your line of work. Even your patron is willing to bend to most of your wishes, out of fear that you will defect to another noble or trainer.

items: A collection of toadies and sycophants, eager to follow your wishes.
Job offers and party invitations from various nobles and criminals aware of your status.
A fancy championship trophy, which can take the form of a belt, cup, or some other trinket.

entries: Unterland was the first of the provinces to host blood sport arenas, back in the days before the formation of the Bürach Empire. Since then the practice has been driven underground, but, like poison spreading silently throughout a healthy body, it has infiltrated nearly every major city.

Ostensibly illegal, you can almost always find small groups of desperate individuals putting their lives on the line for the amusement and enrichment of others. This hidden network of arenas has recently organized into the self-proclaimed Fighter's Guild and developed a series of coded phrases and symbols to identify its members. Following the unspoken rule of Etharis, it is a place where only the strong survive.

items.name: Skill Proficiency
entries: {@skill Insight}, choose one from {@skill Deception}, {@skill Perception}, {@skill Persuasion}, {@skill Stealth}, or {@skill Survival}.

items.name: Languages
entries: Choose one standard language.

items.name: Tool Proficiency
entries: Choose one {@filter gaming set|items|source=phb|miscellaneous=mundane|type=gaming set}

items.name: Equipment
entries: A worn {@item blanket|phb}, a set of ragged clothing, a {@item sack|phb}, a walking stick, an old wool cloak, an {@item iron pot|phb} and 10 copper pieces.

entries.name: Friendly Face
entries: Upon spending an hour in a town or other settlement and making a DC 10 Wisdom ({@skill Insight}) check, you can track down an ally that you made on a previous visit during your wandering. This ally begins as friendly to you and will answer questions you have regarding the town, its services, and its inhabitants.

entries.name: Rank 1 - Outcast
entries: For whatever reason, you can't go home again. Bereft of family, property, and support, you are now cut loose to wander and survive as best you can. You stand out more as a stranger in smaller settlements, where people shun you as if you have the plague, but even in larger cities you are viewed with suspicion by the local authorities.

items: A tarnished compass.
A posting from a town seeking able-bodied workers to deal with a recent disaster.

entries.name: Progression
entries: Survive a major storm on the road or participate meaningfully in a town's internal disputes.

entries.name: Rank 2 - Drifter
entries: You have gotten used to life on the road and now travel aimlessly from town to town. At each stop you take on odd jobs, greet familiar faces, and then move on. Outside your small group of friends spread across Etharis, others are beginning to recognize you as a frequent visitor.

items: News from far parts of your current region that are not public knowledge.
A letter or package that one of your contacts asked you to deliver to another town.

entries.name: Progression
entries: Save the life of one of your contacts.

entries.name: Rank 3 - Seeker
entries: Your aimless wanderings have taken on a new purpose. Competent in the rigors of the road and dealing with suspicious villagers, you travel from place to place in search of a new life or new direction. For good or ill, you are recognized as you travel, much as a caravan leader or traveling merchant.

items: A lightweight tent and bedroll.
The ability to send messages across long distances through your network of contacts.

entries.name: Progression
entries: Play a major role in the downfall of a prominent member of society.

entries.name: Rank 4 - Wanderer
entries: You now travel the world not out of necessity, but choice. Your deeds have garnered you an almost mythical reputation, and whispers follow you whenever you enter a new city or settlement. As a champion of righteousness or a walking plague, everyone knows that even the best laid plans are uncertain when you arrive.

items: A respected or feared reputation in any settlement you visit.
Information about major events across Etharis that has not yet made its way to your current location.

entries: Those paupers who choose to leave their past behind and take to the open road are known as vagabonds. Some do so in an attempt to flee whatever painful memories caused their descent into poverty, while others hold out hope of starting a new life in another city. Most don't survive outside the protective walls of a guarded settlement, but those that do often find little welcome in the cities they visit. Vagabonds must therefore work hard to gain trust and forge what connections they may have in each place they visit, and invariably they must move on before they wear out their welcome.

items.name: Skill Proficiencies
entries: {@skill Arcana}, {@skill Survival}

items.name: Languages
entries: One of your choice

items.name: Equipment
entries: {@item Navigator's tools|phb}, a {@item backpack|phb}, 2 {@item torch|phb|torches}, and a {@item pouch|phb} containing 15 gp

entries.name: Life in the Peaks
entries: What brought you to the Peaks of Gravity? You can work with your GM to determine the exact characteristics of your life within the mountain range, or roll on the table below.

rows: I was born and raised in Rigi.
I came here on a pilgrimage and decided to stay, living in the mountains.
I was lost as a child within the range.
I choose to live in a place of immense natural magical energy.
I feel pulled to the location and feel safest here.
I moved to Rigi.
I stay here to study the magic of the location.
Living in the mountains allows me to stay away from those I don't want to see.

entries.name: Feature: Known Direction
entries: You are used to travel through harsh terrain. While in a place where north exists, you always know the direction of north.

entries.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: Those that spend so much time in the mountains often find enjoyment from some aspect of it. Pick one or two reasons, or roll on the table below.

rows: Being above the clouds is the only real way to connect with nature.
Looking down at the world makes me realize how small I really am.
I love the chill of cold mountain air.
The immediate danger of falling is the thrill I love.
The accomplishment of climbing to a summit drives me to keep moving.
I prefer to stay out of societies way and in unexplored terrain.
I climb to search for lost treasure and undiscovered secrets.
Jumping from great heights is the payoff for a hard climb.

entries: The Peaks of Gravity are home to the small summit town of Rigi as well as scattered travelers and vagabonds. You are of them, either growing up in Rigi, or moving to the Peaks of Gravity later in life. Due to your extended time in the region, you have become accustomed to life here and gained specific abilities.

_.displayName: small trinket that connects you to the life you once had before the occupation of Phlan
dark common clothes that includes a cloak and hood

items.name: Tool Proficiencies:
items.entry: One type of {@filter artisan's tools|items|source=phb|miscellaneous=mundane|type=artisan's tools}, {@filter vehicles (land)|items|source=phb;dmg|miscellaneous=mundane|type=vehicle (land)}

items.name: Equipment:
items.entry: A bag of {@item caltrops (bag of 20)|phb}, a small {@item trinket|phb} that connects you to the life you once had before the occupation of Phlan, a {@item healer's kit|phb}, a set of dark {@item common clothes|phb} that includes a cloak and hood, and a belt {@item pouch|phb} containing 5 gp

entries.name: Lifestyle
entries: Poor

entries.name: Overview
entries: The taking of Phlan by Vorgansharax is a clear memory in your mind. You were going about your everyday business when the green dragon's forces spilled out of the sewers and assailed your home. Many of Phlan's citizens, young and old alike, were captured, killed, or offered as tribute to the Maimed Virulence. You, yourself were one of those captured. But, either with the help of adventurers or through your own wits and sheer determination, you escaped.

Rather than flee the region, you've chosen to stay and fight. Finding refuge outside the town and the deadly thicket surrounding it, you strike out against the Tears of the Virulence and their monstrous allies. You've learned to survive in dire and desperate circumstances, with supplies running low and the arrival of reinforcements uncertain. You've grown accustomed to acting under the cover of night, dealing what blows you can to avenge the friends and family you lost within the currently occupied Phlan. You will drive Vorgansharax out, or you die trying.

entries.name: Origin
entries: Removed from your life as a townsperson, you've adapted to rough life in the wilds surrounding Phlan. The trade you practiced still influences your outlook, the manner in which you approach situations, and the way you contribute to the resistance movement against the Maimed Virulence. You can roll on the following table to determine what your occupation was before the fall, or choose one that best fits your character (select from either the general column or the specific column, but not both).

rows: Fisher
Stojanow River Worker
Hunter
Twilight Marsh Worker
Craftsperson
Mantor's Library Scribe
Priest/Priestess
Clergy of Ilmater
Cook
Laughing Goblin Server
City Watch
Black Fist Guard
Servant
House Sokol Retainer
Unskilled Laborer
Bay of Phlan Dockworker

entries.name: Feature: Guerrilla
entries: You've come to know the surrounding forests, streams, caves, and other natural features in which you can take refuge—or set up ambushes. You can quickly survey your environment for advantageous features. Additionally, you can scavenge around your natural surroundings to cobble together simple supplies (such as improvised torches, rope, patches of fabric, etc.) that are consumed after use. Note: This feature is a variant of the Outlander feature.

entries.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: You have given up the life you knew as a citizen of Phlan. However, the Maimed Virulence's invasion resonates deep inside you. Perhaps you have a few friends or family members who were able to escape with you. Or, perhaps, everyone you held dear either perished or went missing during the fall. You may know of someone who is, against all odds, surviving within the thicket and you long to liberate them from a life of peril within the town.

rows: My patience knows no bounds, so long as my goal is in sight.
In life and in struggle, the ends justify my actions.
If you aren't helping me, you'd best at least stay out of my way.
I long for the life that was taken away from me.
Friends and family perished, tragically, before my eyes. I hope never to undergo that again.
Making the right choices in life are important to me. The choices I make might save not just my life, but the lives of others as well.
I can never allow my foes to get the drop on me.
Time is a precious resource that I must spend wisely.
Leadership. The oppressed need someone to inspire them to courageous acts. (Good)
Unpredictability. Keeping the enemy guessing and off-balance is my tactical strength. (Chaos)
Determination. Threats to my home must be eliminated at all costs. (Any)
Freedom. Those who are enslaved and unjustly imprisoned deserve my aid. (Good)
Resourcefulness. Our wits are our most valuable resource in troubled times. (Any)
Unity. Working together, we can overcome all obstacles, even the most seemingly insurmountable ones. (Any)
I'll never let my fellow insurgents down. They are my only remaining friends.
I was separated from a loved one during my escape from town. I will find them.
One of the Tears of the Virulence was a trusted friend, until the day they betrayed the city. They will pay harshly for their transgressions.
An item I hold close is my last remaining connection to the family I lost during the fall.
The dragon who took my past life away from me will feel the full extent of my vengeance.
The knowledge in Mantor's Library is an irreplaceable treasure that must be protected.
I have no respect for those who flee. I harbor a deep grudge against the citizens who abandoned Phlan.
Ale is the only way I can escape the desperation of my circumstances.
It doesn't take much to get me into a fight.
Being an insurgent means doing things that aren't always ethical. I'm still learning to live with that.
My desire to liberate Phlan oftentimes clouds my judgment, despite my best efforts.
I relentlessly despise the Maimed Virulence and his allies. I'd abandon other goals in order to strike out at them.

_.special: token of the life you once knew

items.name: Equipment:
items.entry: A set of {@filter artisan's tools|items|source=phb|miscellaneous=mundane|type=artisan's tools} (one of your choice), a token of the life you once knew, a set of {@item traveler's clothes|phb}, and a belt {@item pouch|phb} containing 15 gp

entries.name: Lifestyle
entries: Modest

entries.name: Overview
entries: Gone are the happier days of walking into the Laughing Goblin Inn after a hard day's labor. Everything has changed, and you are lucky to be alive. Back in Phlan you could count yourself among those street-wise folks who knew when to pay a bribe and who to work with to make a living. Your ability to listen to the winds of change have saved you before, and this time they allowed you to be one of the lucky few who escaped Phlan with something more than just the shirt on your back.

entries.name: Feature: Phlan Survivor
entries: Whatever your prior standing was, you are now one of the many refugees that have come to Mulmaster. You are able to find refuge with others from Phlan and those who sympathize with your plight. Within Mulmaster this means that you can find a place to bed down, recover, and hide from the watch with either other refugees from Phlan, or the Zhents within the ghettos. Note: This feature is a variant of the Folk Hero feature.

rows: I may have lost everything I worked for most of my life, but there's work to be done, no time to linger on the past.
I worked hard to get where I am and I refuse to let a little hardship stop me from succeeding.
I protect those around me, you never know when one of them will be useful.
I have always gotten ahead by giving, why change now?
I prepare for everything, it paid off in Phlan and it will pay off again.
I will reclaim my home, though the path may be long, I will never give up hope.
I never cared for personal hygiene, and am amazed that It bothers others.
I am always willing to volunteer my services, just as long as don't have to do anything.
Justice. Corruption brought Phlan down, I will not tolerate that any longer. (Lawful)
Acceptance. Stability is a myth, to think you can control your future is futile. (Chaotic)
Hope. I am guided by a higher power and I trust that everything will be right in the end. (Good)
Restraint. I hate those who caused my loss. It is all I can do not to lash out at them. (Any)
Strength. As shown in Phlan, the strong survive. If you are weak you deserve what you get (Evil)
Openness. I am always willing to share my life story with anyone who will listen. (Any)
I have the chance at a new life and this time I am going to do things right.
The Lord Regent brought this suffering upon his people. I will see him brought to justice.
I await the day I will be able to return to my home in Phlan.
I will never forget the debt owed to Glevith of the Welcomers. I will be ready to repay that debt when called upon.
There was someone I cared about in Phlan, I will find out what happened to them.
Some say my life wasn't worth saving, I will prove them wrong.
I used the lives of children to facilitate my escape from Phlan.
I am a sucker for the underdog, and always bet on the loosing team.
I am incapable of standing up for myself.
I will borrow money from friends with no intention to repay it.
I am unable to keep secrets. A secret is just an untold story.
When something goes wrong, it's never my fault.

items.name: Equipment:
items.entry: Choose A or B: (A) {@item Dagger|XPHB} (scalpel), {@item Healer's Kit|XPHB}, {@item Herbalism Kit|XPHB}, Bandages, Book of Remedies, Jar of Leeches, {@item Robe|XPHB}, 10 GP; or (B) 50 GP

entries: Your skills treating the sick and injured have given you a vast knowledge of illnesses and remedies based on the latest science—or the most recent theories from those who like to push the limits of what science might allow.

You may have come into the field in a variety of ways and with a variety of specialties. You might have learned at an institute with the finest medical minds in all of Etharis. Or you might have learned your skills through trial and error, as the poor residents of the surrounding area come to you based on rumors of your preternatural healing powers that are rather mundane.

_.special: lucky charm such as a maneki-neko

items.name: Tool Proficiencies
items.entry: {@item Navigator's tools|PHB}, vehicles ({@filter land|items|source=|type=vehicle (land)|category=} or {@filter air|vehicles|terrain=air})

items.name: Equipment
items.entry: {@item Navigator's tools|PHB}, a pair of goggles, a lucky charm such as a maneki-neko, a pilot's jumpsuit ({@item traveler's clothes|PHB}), and a belt pouch containing 10 gp

entries.name: Feature: Mech Tech
entries: Whenever you make a Dexterity or Intelligence check related to piloting or repairing a vehicle with which you are proficient, you can add twice your proficiency bonus, instead of any proficiency bonus you normally apply.

You are a skilled pilot, of mechs or other vehicles. Pilots are sought after by nearly every faction, and often make their own independent names for themselves as racers, criminals, or even vigilantes.

items.name: Equipment:
items.entry: Choose A or B: (A) {@item Dagger|XPHB}, {@item Carpenter's Tools|XPHB} or {@item Mason's Tools|XPHB} (same as above), {@item Mule|XPHB} and {@item Cart|XPHB}, {@item Traveler's Clothes|XPHB}, 8 GP; or (B) 50 GP

entries: There is still land in Etharis where no one has lived before, and pioneers are the hardy folk who set out to tame that land for the first time. You've learned to find a suitable area to live, set up the beginnings of a village, build the dwellings needed for settlers, then move on.

You have weathered punishing storms, migrations, and harsh winters. You and yours have adapted to the environment. Everything you own is built with your own two hands, and your aptitude in working with natural materials has provided you with shelter, tools, and clothing.

items.name: Equipment:
items.entry: Choose A or B: (A) {@item Navigator's Tools|XPHB}, {@item Dagger|XPHB|}, {@item Traveler's Clothes|XPHB}, {@item Rope|XPHB}, 20 GP; or (B) 50 GP

entries.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: You spent your youth under the sway of a dread pirate, a ruthless cutthroat who taught you how to survive in a world of sharks and savages. You've indulged in larceny on the high seas and sent more than one deserving soul to a briny grave. Fear and bloodshed are no strangers to you, and you've garnered a somewhat unsavory reputation in many a port town.

rows: I grew up by the sea, and the allure of adventure and freedom on the open waves was irresistible.
A pirate crew took me in when I was destitute, and I earned my keep among them.
I was wrongfully accused of a crime and had no choice but to flee to the seas.
The promise of riches and plunder drew me to piracy like a moth to flame.
I sought vengeance against those who wronged me, and the pirate life offered the means to achieve it.
I was betrayed by someone I trusted and found a home among outlaws who understood my pain.
My friends know they can rely on me, no matter what.
I work hard so that I can play hard when the work is done.
I enjoy sailing into new ports and making new friends over a flagon of ale.
I stretch the truth for the sake of a good story.
To me, a tavern brawl is a nice way to get to know a new city.
I never pass up a friendly wager.
My language is as foul as an otyugh nest.
I like a job well done, especially if I can convince someone else to do it.
Respect. The thing that keeps a ship together is mutual respect between captain and crew. (Good)
Fairness. We all do the work, so we all share in the rewards. (Lawful)
Freedom. The sea is freedom—the freedom to go anywhere and do anything. (Chaotic)
Mastery. I'm a predator, and the other ships on the sea are my prey. (Evil)
People. I'm committed to my crewmates, not to ideals. (Neutral)
Aspiration. Someday, I'll own my own ship and chart my own destiny. (Any)
I'm loyal to my captain first, everything else second.
The ship is most important—crewmates and captains come and go.
I'll always remember my first ship.
In a harbor town, I have a paramour whose eyes nearly stole me from the sea.
I was cheated out of my fair share of the profits, and I want to get my due.
Ruthless pirates murdered my captain and crewmates, plundered our ship, and left me to die. Vengeance will be mine.
I follow orders, even if I think they're wrong.
I'll say anything to avoid having to do extra work.
Once someone questions my courage, I never back down no matter how dangerous the situation.
Once I start drinking, it's hard for me to stop.
I can't help but pocket loose coins and other trinkets I come across.
My pride will probably lead to my destruction.

name: Pirate Crew
entries: {@b Adventuring Company.} Whether pirates or privateers, you and your fellow characters are the ranking officers of a small frigate. You might be criminals of the sea, pillaging and looting the coasts of the Iron Kingdoms, or officially recognized privateers bearing a letter of marque.

entries.name: Prerequisites
entries: Any character can be a member, but at least one member must be proficient with vehicles (water).

entries.name: Downtime: Smuggle Cargo
entries: You can earn extra finances by smuggling illicit cargo or passengers. This activity requires at least 3 days finding an employer and securing cargo, plus travel days to the destination. For each day of travel, each member earns {@dice 1d10} gp.

entries.name: Company Accomplishments
entries: Prestige increases through acts such as: plundering at least 1,000 gp in goods from a merchant vessel; navigating a dangerous storm; defeating a significant beast of the sea; stealing a navigational rudder from a rival captain; surviving a battle against a military vessel; or plundering a coastal village.

entries.name: Tier 1 – Local Corsairs
entries: {@b Any Port in a Storm.} Your company knows a network of hidden pirate lairs and smuggling ports along the coast.
{@b Five Cant.} You can replace one language from your race or background with Five Cant.
{@b Starter Vessel.} Your company has a small keelboat crewed by three loyal sailors (commoner stat block). One or more systems has been damaged to half total hit points.

entries.name: Tier 2 – Privateers
entries: {@b Letter of Marque.} Your company gains a letter of marque authorizing you to take rival vessels as prizes. For each rival vessel defeated in battle, your company earns 1 prestige.

{@b Variant – Hostis Humani Generis.} Rather than taking a letter of marque, you can choose to be true pirates. For each vessel your crew defeats in battle, you earn 1 prestige and gain a +1 bonus to Charisma (Intimidation) checks. However, you are subject to legal consequences and are not welcomed in civilized ports.
{@b Sea Dogs.} You gain {@dice 1d4} hirelings (CR 1/4 or lower) for boarding actions and coastal raids.

entries.name: Tier 3 – Infamous Marauders
entries: {@b Dread Pirates.} While flying your colors, any creature not part of your crew who recognizes your flag must make a DC 13 Wisdom saving throw or be frightened of all crew members for 10 minutes. A creature can repeat the save at the start of each of its turns.
{@b Better Recruits.} Your number of hirelings increases by {@dice 1d4}, and hirelings can have CR 1 or lower.

entries.name: Tier 4 – Sea Reavers
entries: {@b Commodores.} When launching a pirate raid, you can call upon {@dice 1d4} keelboats each crewed by {@dice 1d10+10} NPCs (CR 1 or lower). These vessels accompany your crew for the duration before looting what plunder they can.
{@b Premier Recruits.} Your number of hirelings increases by {@dice 2d4}, and these NPCs can have CR 2 or lower.

items.name: Equipment:
items.entry: Choose A or B: (A) {@item Dagger|XPHB}, {@item Spear|XPHB}, {@item Gaming Set|XPHB} (same as above), {@item Robe|XPHB}, 10 GP; or (B) 50 GP

entries: Pit fighting was once a major institution in the Bürach Empire. Since then, the practice has been driven underground, but, like poison spreading silently throughout a healthy body, it has infiltrated nearly every major city.

Ostensibly illegal, you can almost always find small groups of desperate individuals putting their lives on the line for the amusement and enrichment of others. This hidden network of arenas has recently been organized into the self-proclaimed Pit Fighter's Guild and developed a series of coded phrases and symbols to identify its members. You follow the unspoken rule of Etharis: only the strong survive.

items.name: Skill Proficiencies
entries: {@skill Arcana}, {@skill Survival}

items.name: Languages
entries: Two of your choice out of Abyssal, Celestial, Deep Speech, Infernal, Primordial, or Sylvan

items.name: Equipment
entries: a {@item bedroll}, a {@item waterskin}, a {@item Pole (10-foot)|PHB|10-foot pole}, {@item Silk Rope (50 feet)|PHB|50 feet of silk rope}, a {@item steel mirror}, a piece of a broken metal tuning fork used for the {@spell plane shift} spell attuned to the Material Plane, a trinket from another plane, a set of {@item traveler's clothes}, and a belt {@item pouch} containing two gemstones each worth 10 gp.

entries.name: Main Plane
entries: Though you have traveled far, you once spent a great deal of time in a particular plane or realm, growing familiar with it. You can roll on the following table to determine the plane or realm that you spent so much time in, or choose one that best fits your character.

rows: The Feywild
The Shadowfell
An Elemental Plane
An Upper Plane
A Lower Plane
A Plane of Chaos
A plane of Law
The Far Realm

entries.name: Feature: Planar Familiarity
entries: You are as familiar with your main plane as someone who had lived there for hundreds of years, in addition to the basic familiarity with the Material Plane that most player characters have. You know your main plane's general inhabitants, geographies, cultures, and so on. Also, you always recognize a magical portal that leads to your main plane.

entries.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: Your journey across the planes has informed much of your current personality because of its difficulty. Your personality traits are also likely responsible for some of your journey—only certain kinds of people seek to make this perilous trek across the planes as you have.

Use the tables for the {@background sage} or {@background hermit} background in the {@i Player's Handbook} as the basis for your traits and motivations, modifying the entries when appropriate to• suit your identity as someone who has ventured across the planes to reach where you are. For example, if you are using the {@background hermit} tables, you could swap mentions of your seclusion to be your reason for planar travel.

_.special: hand-drawn map of a plane you have visited

items.name: Equipment
items.entry: A staff, a {@item hunting trap|phb}, a hand-drawn map of a plane you have visited, a set of {@item traveler's clothes|phb}, and a belt pouch containing 10 gp.

entries.name: Feature: Portal Key
entries: You know the location of at least one portal or planar gate to Sigil, the City of Doors. This portal could be just about anything, from an archway to a manhole. To others, there's nothing out of the ordinary about this spot, as the portal only opens, allowing travelers to pass through if they possess a portal key. The key, too, could consist of any object, passphrase, or ritual of which a bystander would be unaware.

This portal might be guarded, or in a dangerous location, and you might not possess the key, if it's a unique physical object. Work with your DM to decide under what circumstances your character can leave the Material Plane.

entries.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: Planeswalkers know a lot about the multiverse and this knowledge makes them cautious. They know there are doors that shouldn't be opened and beasts that shouldn't be disturbed. No planeswalker survives long without practicing restraint. In spite of this, they tend to be extremely ambitious, for the planes are full of possibilities and wonders.

rows: I've made friends (or business contacts) on every plane I've visited.
I always wear the expression of a world-weary poker face.
I get antsy if I stay in one place for more than a week.
My weapon of choice is an impractical one that I learned from an ancient people on a far-off plane.
When I find myself in a new place, I create a map of the area. I carry with me dozens of such maps.
I'm fluent in few languages of the Material Plane, but know fragments of many extraplanar languages.
I am terrible at conversation, and am likely to just stare down my traveling companions for an entire journey.
Nothing gets my mind off the road like sharing a few stories over a campfire.
{@b Respect.} While traveling far afield, you come to know that everyone, regardless of position, have worth. (Good)
{@b Honor.} Every man must have a code. (Lawful)
{@b Survival.} On hostile planes, the only priority is self-preservation. (Chaotic)
{@b Greed.} I take what I can, and give nothing back. (Evil)
{@b Live and Let Live.} Meddling in the affairs of others only causes trouble. (Neutral)
{@b Wanderlust.} The Great Wheel contains countless wonders, and I want to see all of them. (Any)
I must find the key to a secret portal within Sigil.
I have traveled the planes for years to find my home.
I will find a way to the fabled Plane of Time, and unmake great mistakes of the past.
The {@i Codex of Infinite Planes} will be mine.
I am protective of my less experienced fellow travelers.
Throughout the planes, I am hunted by a powerful evil entity.
I'm addicted to an exotic drug found only on the Plane of Fire.
I have made enemies of angels and devils alike.
I once looked into a portal to the Far Realm, which left me slightly out of touch with reality.
My crippling insomnia often strikes when I'm confined to a particular city for too long.
I have few scruples when it comes to theft.
I compulsively diffuse diplomatic situations by speaking out of turn and disrespecting the other party.

entries: Due to powerful magic, the portals of Sigil, or divine intervention, you were shunted from your home plane, and forced to wander the multiverse in search of a way back. You have seen the shores of a dozen oceans, met creatures too fantastical to describe, and glimpsed the Lady of Pain (from afar.) Though your legs have become heavy from travel, your eyes always constantly search for new horizons.

Perhaps you eventually found your way home with a wealth of experience gained, or perhaps you still wander the Great Wheel in search of it. Perhaps, even, you travel the multiverse of your own accord for its sights, its dangers, and its treasure. After all, not all who wander are lost.

name: Political Strategist

_.displayName: notebook with contact information (and relevant details) for your boss and their political allies

_.special: broadsheet clipping from a story you helped place in a publication

items.name: Skill Proficiencies:
items.entry: Your choice of two of the following: {@skill Deception}, {@skill Insight}, or {@skill Investigation}

items.name: Equipment:
items.entry: A notebook with contact information (and relevant details) for your boss and their political allies, a broadsheet clipping from a story you helped place in a publication, a set of {@item fine clothes|PHB}, a {@item writing kit|Arcadia9} (small {@item pouch|PHB} with {@item ink pen|PHB|a quill}, {@item ink (1-ounce bottle)|PHB|ink}, folded {@item parchment (one sheet)|PHB|parchment}, and a penknife), and a {@item pouch|PHB} containing 10 gp

entries: You work for a candidate, elected official, guild, or other entity that seeks to maneuver local politics as strategically and deftly as possible. You advise your bosses on who to make strategic alliances with, how to outmaneuver political opponents, and where to go and what to say to build support among the city's influential citizens. Whether you're helping your boss get that power or you're their puppet master is up to you and your GM.

entries.name: Feature: Trusted Adviser
entries: You work for someone who holds power in the city—a city council member, the head of a guild, the archmage of a mystic circle, the dean of a university, a lieutenant of the city watch, etc. You are this person's confidante and trusted counselor. They always hear what you have to say and seriously consider your advice and perspective. On relatively small matters, they're likely to agree with you on the spot (at the GM's discretion). They can supply you with favors and nonmagical equipment.

entries.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: To a political strategist, the world is a chess board and people are pieces to be moved around strategically. A political strategist loves nothing more than thinking analytically and creatively about how to achieve goals. Their speciality is building and consolidating power. See the tables in the Personal Characteristics section below for more ideas.

You are a veteran statesman and bureaucrat, with an intimate understanding of the inner workings of government. Whether you occupy the public eye as an elected official or hold a tiny role in a labyrinthine bureaucracy, you belong to a modern government.

Though a politician has an essential role, you often face ire from every direction. You may need to shake the hand of a political rival while they scheme up the best ways to demolish your reputation—while you do the same to them. In lean times, the common people despise you and your decisions, or even hate you for policies entirely outside your control. All too often, you must enforce rules whose creation you had no part in with ruthless efficiency, lest you find yourself cast out of government and among the rabble that despise you.

items.name: Equipment:
items.entry: A set of {@item fine clothes|phb}, a {@item signet ring|phb}, {@item ink (1-ounce bottle)|phb|ink}, a quill, twenty sheets of {@item parchment (one sheet)|phb|parchment}, and a belt {@item pouch|phb} containing 10 gp

entries.name: Position
entries: No one in government holds exactly the same role. Each job in a bureaucracy has a unique functional niche and sphere of influence. Choose a position or roll on the table below to determine the scope of your jurisdiction and how you serve the people or government that appointed or elected you. Unlike a noble, you did not inherit your position; you earned it through honest work or underhanded maneuvering.

rows: Secretary or clerk
Tax collector
Legal scholar
Mayor
Regional governor
Councilman
Ambassador
Judge

entries.name: Feature: Official Business
entries: With your intimate knowledge of political vocabulary and official terminology, you can often bluff your way into important locations. If a person or group recognizes the authority of the government from which your power derives, you can call on that authority to reinforce your barrage of jargon. With these intangible tools, you can bulldoze your way into locations and situations that you could never reach otherwise.

entries.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: Some politicians are truly the slimy, unscrupulous, and corrupt officials the people believe them to be. Others are former idealists in over their heads, or even zealots ready to fight for their beliefs to the bitter end. Only the passionate personalities can survive the political arena, whether they care about others or themselves.

rows: I thrive when given responsibility.
I empathize with my opponents and easily understand their perspectives.
I have plans for enormous, sweeping reforms.
Despite my experience with bureaucracy, I loathe waiting and small talk.
I watch my words and actions with great care lest a scandal mar my career beyond repair.
I speak slowly, choosing my words carefully and with gravitas.
For better or worse, I love to exercise my authority and expertise.
I am often tempted to abuse my power, but refuse to give in to corruption.
{@b Compliance.} The machine of government has checks and balances that I follow to the letter. (Lawful)
{@b Service.} I serve the people, not the other way around. (Good)
{@b Infiltration.} I joined this system to bring it down from within. (Chaotic)
{@b Greed.} My position will enrich me and my prospects, no matter what it takes. (Evil)
{@b Routine.} I once had great ideas, but now I'm just here for the stable paycheck. (Neutral)
{@b Reform.} Government has many benefits, but also much that we can improve. (Any)
I lost a home and loved ones due to a governmental oversight, and I'll not let it happen again.
I or my family were once nobility, and I'm fighting to remain at the top in this new system.
Every day is an intellectual exercise and an opportunity to study the law, which I find thrilling.
I will work my way to the top and earn the highest position I can.
I will not let the people who appointed me down.
I adore the attention brought by the public eye and will do anything to maintain it.
I cheated to earn the position I have now and will eliminate anyone who tries to find out.
I can't imagine my rulings being wrong.
Anyone who stands in the way of my righteous crusade is an enemy to be crushed.
I am susceptible to bribes and flattery.
I insult opponents and misrepresent their arguments.
My blunders and antics keep me in the public eye for all the wrong reasons.

name: Politician

b.special: other accessory with the mark of your office or political party

items.name: Equipment:
items.entry: A set of {@item fine clothes|PHB}, a {@item writing kit|Arcadia9} (small {@item pouch|PHB} with {@item ink pen|PHB|a quill}, {@item ink (1-ounce bottle)|PHB|ink}, folded {@item parchment (one sheet)|PHB|parchment}, and a penknife), a ceremonial ribbon-cutting blade, a brooch or other accessory with the mark of your office or political party, and a {@item pouch|PHB} containing 10 gp

entries: You are running for office or have already been elected (or maybe appointed; talk to your GM about what makes sense for the setting). Your office is one of moderate power and influence; you might be a member of a city council or a community elder or alderperson. You can't control major political decisions in your city, but you certainly have access to, and maybe the respect of, the people who do.

entries.name: Feature: Expense Account
entries: Your political party (or perhaps a benefactor or other group that supports you) funds a comfortable lifestyle for you and up to eight of your traveling companions. They pay for your food, shelter, clothing, daily needs, and anything else you can reasonably justify as being part of your political career (at the GM's discretion). They do not fund armor, weapons, or magic items.

entries.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: Politicians tend to be networkers, movers and shakers, and people who see themselves as just the right person to be giving speeches, representing constituents, making laws, and doing a whole lot of shaking hands and kissing babies. Your politician might be looking to make change, enjoy the social status of their position, or both!

_.special: realistic ink drawing of your polymorphed form

items.name: Skill Proficiencies
items.entry: {@skill Survival} and choose one additional from either {@skill Animal Handling} or {@skill Deception}.

items.name: Equipment
items.entry: A bag of {@item caltrops|phb}, a realistic ink drawing of your polymorphed form, a set of common clothes, and a belt pouch with 10 gp.

entries.name: Overview
entries: You were transformed into a beast, a monstrosity, or a mundane object, and lived that way for years. You most likely entered this form unwillingly, but how you came down with this affliction is up to you. A caster with an axe to grind may have cast polymorph or true polymorph for some petty offense committed by you or a loved one. Maybe you unwittingly donned a cursed magic item. Perhaps you activated some arcane trap when you accidentally stumbled into an ancient ruin in the tunnels below the city. You also should decide who or what changed you back into your true form. You were in your alternate form for years. How was living in that form different from the way you lived your life before? In what ways were you more powerful? Less powerful? Do you miss the strength of your old form, or are you glad to be back in your own flesh? If you were a wild animal or a monster, how did you survive in the crowded urban environment of Solace? Were you kept in a menagerie or a circus? Or as an exotic pet? If you were an object, what were you used for and by whom? Was your owner aware of your true nature?

entries.name: Feature: Kindred Spirit
entries: Non-hostile creatures of the same type as your previously polymorphed form are inclined to like you. These creatures might help guide you to a place if they know its location, provide you with shelter, or shield you from danger, provided they aren't put directly into harm's way.

_.special: a realistic ink drawing of your polymorphed form

items.name: Skill Proficiencies
entries: {@skill Survival} and choose one additional from either {@skill Animal Handling} or {@skill Deception}

items.name: Languages
entries: Two of your choice

items.name: Equipment

entries.name: Feature: Kindred Spirit
entries: Nonhostile creatures of the same type as your polymorphed form are inclined to like you. These creatures might help guide you to a place if they know its location, provide you with shelter, or shield you from danger, provided they aren't put directly into harm's way.

entries.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: You have spent so much time in the skin of another form that you're not comfortable with your true body. This discomfort may manifest in a physical form like fidgeting, wearing baggy or eccentric clothing, or the need to change your appearance through tattoos or piercings. You may have more of a subconscious mental tick like targeting the appearance of others to make yourself feel better or nightmares of once again living in your polymorphed form. Your old form was a prison that hid your true self, but it was also a way to keep yourself shielded from harm.

rows: I am always fidgeting because I am uncomfortable.
I retained a rude physical behavior of my polymorphed form.
I obsess over my appearance and wear eccentric outfits.
I always judge the way others look.
I am unsure of what to say when people ask about me.
I often speak in my head by accident instead of aloud.
I find it's easier to lie than give real personal details.
I must keep touching my body to reassure myself I'm in it.
{@b Freedom}. People should be free to express who they are. (Chaotic)
{@b Power}. If it gets me what I want, I'll manipulate anyone. (Evil)
{@b Security}. All people deserve a place where they feel at peace. (Good)
{@b Beauty}. All people should appreciate who they are. (Neutral)
{@b Authority}. If you respect authority, you will be protected. (Lawful)
{@b Dog Eat Dog}. To survive you must be the smartest or strongest. (Neutral)
I have altered my appearance to look like my polymorphed form.
Some friends I made in my polymorphed form don't know I've been turned back.
I carry a piece of my old body.
The place where I spent most of my time while polymorphed is home to me.
I still haven't seen my family since before I was polymorphed.
I still enjoy eating what I ate in my polymorphed form.
I want to be back in my polymorphed form.
I sometimes believe I still possess abilities of my polymorphed form that I no longer have.
All transmutation magic is terrible and must be stopped.
I physically hurt myself for assurance I am in my true form.
It's easier to back down from an argument than try to convince someone I'm right.
The opinions of my friends are more important than my own.

entries.name: Variant Feature: Body Horror
entries: This feature is meant for games using the variant {@variantrule madness|DMG} rules in chapter 8 of the {@i Dungeon Master's Guide}. Before choosing this feature you must ask your DM. You have spent so much time in the form of another creature that you aren't easily shocked by bodily manipulation and mutilation. Whenever such a sight would cause you to save against a madness effect you automatically succeed.

You were transformed into an animal or monster and lived that way for years. You most likely entered this form unwillingly but how you came down with this affliction is up to you. A caster with an axe to grind may have cast {@spell true polymorph} for some petty offense committed by you or a loved one. Maybe you unwittingly donned a cursed magic item. Perhaps you activated some arcane trap when you accidentally stumbled into an ancient ruin. You could have made the choice willingly to infiltrate some group of monsters or hide as a beast from someone hunting you. You also should decide who or what changed you back to your true form.

You were in your alternate form for years. How was living in that form different from the way you lived your life before? In what ways were you more powerful? Less powerful? Do you miss the strength of your old form or are you glad to be back in your own flesh?

name: Posse
entries: {@b Adventuring Company.} When the territory of a swampie village or gatorfolk congregation must be defended, they round up the biggest, strongest, and angriest members of their community and form a posse. What posses lack in training or equipment, they make up for in determination.

entries.name: Prerequisites
entries: Any character can belong to a Posse company. Characters with proficiency in the Survival skill are particularly prized, but spellcasters and other classes are also welcome.

entries.name: Special: The Toughest Around
entries: When it comes time to defend your tribal territory, you need the sturdiest folks in town. Each member's hit point maximum increases by an amount equal to twice the member's level. Whenever a member of the posse gains a level, that member's hit point maximum increases by an additional 2 hit points.

entries.name: Company Accomplishments
entries: Your company's prestige increases through acts such as: defending the community from a force with superior numbers; capturing or slaying a large beast causing trouble in the region; bringing in a local criminal or proving someone is wrongfully accused; protecting the community during a disaster or famine; expanding the territory or resources available to the community.

entries.name: Tier 1 — Unruly Mob
entries: {@b Bring 'Em Back Alive.} You can replace one proficiency you gained from your background or class with proficiency in the Survival skill, and you can double your proficiency bonus when you use the Survival skill for tracking.

{@b No Place Like Home.} So long as you are in your community, you can enjoy a modest lifestyle at no expense. The community will protect you from discovery and provide wares and services at little or no charge if they can.

entries.name: Tier 2 — Local Toughs
entries: {@b Billet.} The community has set aside a structure for your use—a converted barn, empty house, or storefront—that houses your company, provides room for extra supplies, and can act as a makeshift jail.
{@b The Law in These Parts.} You are seen as arbiters of local justice. Those in your area will generally go along with you as you interrogate people, search houses, take captives, and so on.

{@b Spiritual Support.} Your community's spiritual advisors have taken a keen interest in your well-being. You gain one bone grinder, cleric, shaman, or other spiritual leader with a challenge rating of 3 or lower.

entries.name: Tier 3 — Regulators
entries: {@b Deputize.} When you need them, the people of your community will take up arms to help repel an attack or bring down a threat. At the GM's discretion, you can unofficially deputize up to {@dice 3d6} members of your community with a challenge rating of 1/4 or lower, plus one steamjack, myrmidon, warbeast, or community member with a challenge rating of 6 or lower. These individuals follow your orders for 48 hours or until the specific problem is resolved. Once you deputize members in this way, you can't do so again for {@dice 1d4} days.

{@b Friends in High Places.} You have the ear of whoever is in charge in your community. You are largely immune to being held accountable for your actions if you can demonstrate they are in the best interests of the community. Even if you get into trouble outside your territory, your contacts may send someone to advocate on your behalf or break you out of jail.

entries.name: Tier 4 — Community Champions
entries: {@b Hard-Won Respect.} Brigands and raiders for leagues around know better than to bring trouble to your door, and the people of your community see you as heroes. Local leaders must actively curry your favor to maintain their position of power, since anyone you support is sure to have a significant advantage.

items.name: Skill Proficiency
entries: {@skill Intimidation}, {@skill Medicine}

items.name: Tool Proficiencies
entries: {@item herbalism kit|phb}

items.name: Languages

items.name: Equipment
